# Manifest

> Build, publish, and run websites and apps by chatting with Claude.


# Overview


## Manifest — Build and publish with Claude

Source: https://manifestx.dev/

Free forever. Runs on your Claude plan, no credits. Claude builds your app. website. dashboard. platform. game. Manifest makes it real. Live on your own domain, with sign-ins and saved data built in. From a simple site to a full platform, without leaving Claude. No hosting accounts or API keys. Never per seat. Publish free, for as long as you like. Upgrade a project when it needs more, and cancel anytime. The framework itself is always free and open source. Monthly Yearly · 2 months free USD EUR Free For launching anything $0 forever Preview and publish from Claude Connect your own domains Last 7 days' analytics 100 form submissions per month API access Manifest badge & public showcase Add Manifest to Claude Pro For businesses and teams $15 per project, monthly Everything in Free, plus No badge, showcase optional Invite your team Rollback to your last 5 versions All-time analytics 5,000 form submissions per month Start free, upgrade anytime Enterprise Publishing, built into your product Custom by contract Bulk projects through the API Managed projects Full support & SLA Bespoke tools and templates Talk to us API docs Compare everything included Questions Common questions Something else? Contact the team . What counts as a project? One site or app with its own address and versions. Plans are per project, so teammates never cost extra; inviting them comes with Pro. Should I use Claude chat or the Code tab? Both publish to Manifest. A chat suits small sites: Claude sends the files with the conversation, which keeps projects to 10 MB (2 MB per file), and it works on Claude's Free plan. The Code tab, on paid Claude plans, keeps the project in a folder on your computer with no size limit, so it's the better start for apps and anything you'll keep working on. How does Claude know a project uses Manifest? Once Manifest is added to Claude, ask for it by name, like "build me a site with Manifest." In the Code tab, the project folder includes a CLAUDE.md file that tells every new session it's a Manifest project, so open the same folder to pick up where you left off. The folder works with Git like any code project, and GitHub is optional: handy for teams, never needed to publish. Can I publish a site I already have? Yes, if it builds to static files, like a React, Vite, Astro, or plain HTML site. Claude publishes the build as it is, without moving it to Manifest. Sites that need a server of their own, such as server-side rendering or API routes, aren't hosted; the published site can call a backend that runs elsewhere. Who owns what I build? You do. Any project can download its last 5 published versions on any plan. The framework is open source under the MIT License and runs anywhere, and the API publishes from your own code, so Claude is optional. What is the badge? Free sites show a small "Made with Manifest" link, and Free projects may be featured in the showcase on manifestx.dev. Pro removes the badge and lets you choose whether the project is featured. How does billing work? Per project through Stripe, monthly or yearly. Upgrade or cancel from the dashboard, or just ask Claude. If you cancel, your site stays live: Pro runs to the end of the paid period, then the project moves to Free, the badge returns, and form submissions older than 30 days are removed. What will you make real? A booking site for my yoga studio Add Manifest to Claude Free, on any Claude plan

Common questions Something else? Contact the team . Is Manifest cheaper than Lovable? Yes, and it stays that way. Manifest's free plan has no time limit: build your projects in Claude and publish them publicly on your own domains for $0, month after month. You only pay for Pro on a project that needs its extras, like teammates or rollback. On Lovable's free plan, only people you invite can open your site. Public sites and custom domains start at $25 a month, and building spends credits. Does Manifest use credits? No. Building happens in your Claude chats. Can I move a Lovable project to Manifest? Yes. Give Claude your Lovable app's address and ask for a copy in a new Manifest project. It's rebuilt as yours, ready to edit and publish. Can I use my own domain for free? Yes, on Manifest's free plan, with the certificate handled for you. Lovable connects new custom domains on paid plans. Do I need to know how to code? No, for either. You describe what you want in plain words, and the AI builds it. Do I need Claude? Yes. Manifest works through Claude, so one subscription covers building. Claude's free plan works too. Common questions Something else? Contact the team . Is Manifest cheaper than Webflow? Yes, and it stays that way. Manifest's free plan has no time limit: build in Claude and publish on your own domain for $0, month after month. Pro is $15 a month per project, with teammates included. On Webflow, a custom domain needs a paid site plan, from $25 a month, or $15 billed yearly, its CMS starts at $39 a month, and each teammate who edits is a paid seat. Does Manifest use credits? No. Building happens in your Claude chats. Can I move a Webflow site to Manifest? Yes. Give Claude your Webflow site's address and ask for a copy in a new Manifest project. It's rebuilt as yours, ready to edit and publish. A Webflow code export can also be published as it is. Does Manifest have a visual editor like Webflow? Claude is the designer. Describe the change, and see it in a live preview, then publish. Teammates you invite do the same, from their own Claude. If you'd rather drag and style every element by hand, Webflow is built for that. Can I use my own domain for free? Yes, on Manifest's free plan, with the certificate handled for you. Webflow needs a paid site plan for each site on a custom domain. What happens to my Webflow CMS content? Claude copies it, blog posts and other lists included, into data your new project reads, stored with the project or in the cloud. From then on, Claude is your CMS: ask it to add a post or change a price. Need a dashboard for others? Claude can build you a custom CMS in minutes, hosted on Manifest, that updates your site. Switching from WordPress There's nothing to export. Point Claude at your WordPress site, and it copies it, pages and posts included, into a new Manifest project. Prompt idea Copy Copy my-site.wordpress.com into a new Manifest project, exactly as it is 1 Connect Manifest Add Manifest to Claude once, in a minute. 2 Point Claude at it Give Claude your WordPress site's address and ask for a copy. 3 Publish Check it on staging, then take it live on your own domain. Common questions Something else? Contact the team . Is Manifest cheaper than WordPress? For most small sites, yes. Manifest's free plan has no time limit: build in Claude and publish on your own domain for $0, month after month, with staging included and no ads. WordPress.com's free plan has no custom domain and shows ads. Its Personal plan adds a domain from $9 a month, or $4 billed yearly, which is cheaper than Manifest Pro's $15. Staging and restoring backups start on its Business plan, $40 a month or $25 billed yearly. Self-hosted WordPress is free software, but you pay for hosting yourself. Can I move my WordPress site to Manifest? Yes. Give Claude your site's address and ask for a copy in a new Manifest project. Pages and blog posts are rebuilt as yours, ready to edit and publish. From then on, ask Claude to add a post or change a price. Will my site look like other WordPress sites? On WordPress, most sites start from a theme that many others use too, so they tend to look alike. With Manifest, you describe what you want, and Claude designs it for you, so your site looks like yours, not a template. Does Manifest have plugins like WordPress? No, there's no module store. Instead, ask Claude for what you need, like a contact form, a gallery or a booking button, and it builds it into your site. There's nothing to install, and nothing to keep updated. Can I run an online store on Manifest? Yes. Bring the payment provider or store account you already use, like Stripe, and Claude connects it, from a simple checkout link to a fully built-in shop. On WordPress.com, a full store starts on the $70-a-month Commerce plan. Who keeps my site updated and secure? On Manifest, there are no plugins or servers for you to look after. Claude makes the changes, and Manifest hosts the site. WordPress.com manages its own hosting and updates. On self-hosted WordPress, you or your host keep WordPress, its plugins and its security up to date. Can I use my own domain for free? Yes, on Manifest's free plan, with the certificate handled for you. WordPress.com connects custom domains on paid plans only. Your next site, without the upkeep. Get started free Publishing is free, on your own domain

Choose Manifest if… You want it on your own domain. You want staging before changes go live. It's a real site people will visit. Side by side Free plan against free plan, and paid against paid. Free plans Chat app alone Manifest Nothing to set up ✓ Connect once Build by chatting ✓ In Claude Share a public link ✓ ✓ Custom domain — ✓ Staging, then go live — ✓ Visitor analytics — Last 7 days Paid plans Paid chat plan Manifest Pro Price A monthly subscription $15 a month per project More AI use each day ✓ Your Claude plan Custom domain ChatGPT Sites only, in beta ✓ Staging, then go live — ✓ Teammates edit the same site ChatGPT Sites only ✓ Visitor analytics ChatGPT Sites only All time Verified November 2026 from each company's published pages: Claude: publish and share artifacts , Gemini: create apps with Canvas , ChatGPT Sites , ChatGPT Sites: manage a site , . Publish what you made Keep chatting the way you do now. Connect Manifest to Claude, then ask it to publish what you made. Prompt idea Copy Publish this artifact on my own domain with Manifest 1 Connect Manifest Add Manifest to Claude once, in a minute. 2 Ask Claude to publish Give Claude your share link, or ask in the chat where you made it. 3 Go live Check it on staging, then take it live on your own domain. Common questions Something else? Contact the team . How do I publish a Claude artifact on my own domain? Connect Manifest to Claude, then, in the same chat or with your artifact's share link, ask: "Publish this artifact on my own domain with Manifest." Claude publishes it to staging for you to check, then takes it live on your domain, with the certificate handled for you. It's free, with no time limit. Can I host a ChatGPT canvas app on my own domain? Yes. Give Claude the share link, or paste the code, and ask it to publish with Manifest on your domain. ChatGPT's own Sites feature, in beta on paid plans, can also connect a domain you own. Can I put a Gemini canvas app on my own domain? Yes, the same way. Give Claude the share link, or paste the code, and ask it to publish with Manifest on your domain. What does Manifest add to how Claude builds? Manifest's skills guide Claude through building websites, apps, games, and platforms. For projects on the Manifest framework, routing, data, sign-ins, and forms are built in, so Claude doesn't have to piece together outside tools. Sign-ins and cloud data use your own Appwrite account. Can it become a phone app? Yes, for projects built with the Manifest framework. Visitors can install it from the browser like an app, and Claude can set it up for the App Store and Google Play. You build and submit it with your own developer accounts. Does Manifest replace Claude? No. Manifest works inside Claude. You keep building by chatting, exactly as you do now, and Manifest adds the publishing: hosting, your own domain, and staging. Claude's free plan works too. Is Manifest free? Yes. The free plan has no time limit: publish to staging and live on your own domain, with 7 days of visitor analytics and 100 form submissions a month, plus a small "Made with Manifest" badge. Pro is $15 a month per project, and only for projects that need it: it removes the badge and adds teammates, rollback and all-time analytics. When is a chat app's share link enough? For a prototype, a quick tool, or something to show a few people, a share link is instant and needs nothing set up. When it's a site people should find at your own address, with changes checked before they go live, publish it with Manifest. From your chat to your own domain. Get started free Publishing is free, on your own domain

# Platform docs

## Introduction — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/platform/introduction

Introduction Connect Manifest to Claude, then build and publish by chatting. What Manifest Does Manifest lets Claude put what it builds online, and keep it running: hosting, staging, domains, analytics, and teams. You describe what you want; Claude does the work. It's free to start. Connect Claude Do this once. In Claude, go to Customize > Connectors , select + , then Add custom connector . Name it Manifest and paste this server URL: https://mcp.manifestx.dev/mcp Select Add , then Connect , and sign in with Google, GitHub, or your email. This creates your free Manifest account. Manifest is now available in every new Claude session. You never share a password or key with Claude. Chat or Code Sessions You can use Manifest in two kinds of Claude session: Chat sessions (and Cowork) are everyday Claude conversations, with nothing to set up. Claude keeps the project's files in the session and sends them to Manifest when it publishes. Code sessions are in the Code tab of the Claude desktop app. Claude works in a folder on your computer, so projects can be any size, and it can show a live preview. Code session Chat session Build and publish ✓ Projects up to 10 MB and 300 files Preview in the Claude app ✓ Pick up where you left off Open the same folder Continue in the same session Publish live, connect domains ✓ ✓ Invite a team, roll back (Pro) ✓ ✓ See visitors ✓ ✓ Your Project Folder A Code session works in a folder you choose: Make an empty folder wherever you keep your documents, named after the project, like bakery-site . In the Claude desktop app, open the Code tab, start a new session, and choose that folder. Ask Claude to build with Manifest. It saves everything in the folder as it works. The folder is your working copy. Manifest stores what you publish online, including the last 5 versions, which you can download anytime. For a backup of the folder itself, use GitHub Sync . For anything you'll keep growing, start in a Code session. Start a Session Name Manifest in your first message, so Claude knows to use it. Build a landing page for our bakery with Manifest Publish this project with Manifest To come back to a project in a Code session, open its folder: it includes a CLAUDE.md file that tells Claude it's a Manifest project. In any session, you can also name the project, like let's work on the bakery site . What You Can Ask As with anything in Claude, you can ask for whatever you have in mind, in your own words. These are a few ideas to get started. To Prompt ideas Build Build a client portal where customers sign in Make a quiz game for our trade show Draw inspiration Capture the vibe of this other site Grab our theme from our old website Change Use our brand colors: navy and orange Add a French version Publish Put it online Take staging live Use a domain Connect www.example.com Undo Put the previous version back Invite people Invite sam@example.com See visitors How many people visited this week? Upgrade Upgrade this project to Pro Get help Ask the Manifest team for expert help Good to Know Any framework. Claude builds new projects with the open-source Manifest framework unless you ask for another, like React or Svelte. Projects you already have work too. Manifest publishes anything that builds to plain web files. No server code. Manifest runs what works in the browser. Claude can add sign-ins and saved data with an Appwrite account. Your work stays yours. On any plan, you can download a copy of any of the last 5 published versions. If Something Goes Wrong If Try this Claude doesn't use Manifest Name Manifest in your message, and check it's turned on in the session's connectors menu. Manifest stops responding or asks you to sign in Reconnect it in Customize > Connectors . A project is too big for a Chat session Continue it in a Code session. The preview won't start Claude may need to install Node.js, a free tool. Ask it to. A new domain doesn't load yet Domain changes take a while to spread. Ask is my domain ready? Anything else Tell Claude what you expected and what happened. If it can't fix it, contact the team .


## Edit — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/platform/edit

Edit Build and change a project by chatting. Ask for Changes Describe what you want as you would to a person. If something isn't right, say so. Make the headline bigger and center it Show our product list from this spreadsheet Add a French version Make it look like this screenshot Preview In a Code session, ask Claude to preview my project . It opens next to the conversation and updates as Claude works. Only you can see it; to share a version, publish it to staging . If the preview stops, ask Claude to restart the preview . Your work is saved in the project's folder either way. Chat sessions have no preview, so Claude publishes to staging for you to check there. What Claude Knows Manifest teaches Claude how to build with the Manifest framework . Claude uses this on its own, so there's nothing to name. Area Prompt ideas Pages and layout Add an About page Put these three cards in a row Look and feel Use our brand colors Make the buttons rounder Forms and data Add a contact form Load our team from this file Accounts Let people sign in Languages Add a French version Search and sharing Improve how pages look when shared Checking Check everything works before I publish Projects built with something else, such as React or Astro, keep their own setup, and Claude edits them the way they're built. Working as a Team When several people edit a project, start each session with everyone's latest changes: ask Claude to download the latest published version , or, if the project is on GitHub , to get the latest changes . If someone published since your copy was made, Manifest stops you from publishing over their work, and Claude helps you catch up first.


## Publish — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/platform/publish

Publish Put a project online, check changes first, and use your own domain. Put It Online Put it online Claude publishes the project and replies with its address, like acme-launch.manifestx.ai . Projects built with something else, like React or Vite, are built and published as they are. In a Chat session, a project can be up to 10 MB and 300 files, with each file up to 2 MB, because Claude sends the files from the session itself. A Code session publishes from the folder on your computer, with no size limit. See Chat or Code sessions . Staging, Then Live Every project has two addresses: staging for checking changes, and live for everyone else. Search engines skip staging, but anyone with its address can open it. Ask Claude to publish to staging , then open the staging address. When it looks right, ask Claude to take it live . The exact version you checked goes live. If you don't say which, Claude publishes live. Check a Build Before Staging Publish this to staging without changing what's on staging, and give me a preview link Claude stores the build and replies with a preview address that shows exactly that build, while staging stays as it was. When it looks right, ask Claude to take that version live and that exact build goes live. Name a release by asking for a label, like call it v2.4 ; Claude shows labels when it lists versions. For release scripts, the same works with npx mnfst-publish --no-live --label "v2.4" , then npx mnfst-publish --promote --deployment dep_… . npx mnfst-publish --list --json reads which version is live, so your script can pass it to --expect-live dep_… , which refuses the promote unless that version is still live. With --json , the result is one object your script can read, and a refusal carries a code such as live_moved . An option the command doesn't know is refused, so nothing is published. With search-ready pages on, the version you promoted still matches after its finished pages replace it. Preview addresses show pages only: forms, payments and AI chat answer on staging and live. Search-Ready Pages Make my site ready for search engines Search engines and AI assistants read little more than a page's first HTML, so a site built in the browser can look nearly empty to them. With search-ready pages on, Manifest turns each live release into finished pages that they read in full, with titles, descriptions, a sitemap and link previews. Nothing is installed on your computer, and it's free on every plan. Claude turns it on for sites meant to be found, like a business site, blog or portfolio, and sets the site's real address so links point to it. Staging is served as built; each live release takes a few minutes to finish. Rollbacks Put the previous version back Manifest keeps the last 5 versions of staging and live. On Pro, Claude can put any of them back. On any plan, you can ask for a downloaded copy of one. Custom Domains Connect example.com to my project Claude tells you what to add where you bought the domain, and there's no need to move your DNS anywhere. Manifest then sets up the security certificate and renews it for you. A domain on its own, like example.com : two records, an address record and a short code that proves the domain is yours. A subdomain, like shop.example.com : one record. Visitors typing www ? Add the extra record Claude gives you and they're sent to example.com . Moving a live domain? Tell Claude first, and nothing goes offline during the move. To change the .manifestx.ai address , ask Claude to change my address to acme-launch . The old address stops working. Shortcuts In a Code session, you can type these commands instead of asking. Command Same as asking /manifest:preview Preview my project /manifest:staging Publish to staging /manifest:publish Take it live /manifest:status What's the status of my project? Native Apps Projects built with the Manifest framework can also become iPhone and Android apps. Turn this project into an iPhone and Android app Claude sets up the app and can add features like Face ID and push notifications. You build and submit it yourself with your own developer accounts; Manifest doesn't submit apps. See Native Apps . Badge and Showcase Free projects show a small "Made with Manifest" badge and may be featured in Manifest's showcase . Pro removes the badge, and you can ask Claude to keep my project out of the showcase .


## Manage — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/platform/manage

Manage Your projects, plans, teams, and visitors. Dashboard Sign in at dash.manifestx.dev the same way you did in Claude. Each project is a card with its address, plan, team, and status: Live , Staging (published to staging only), or Draft (not published yet). When you have several projects, Claude asks which one you mean before changing anything. Working on two projects at once in separate Claude windows? Claude names the project in each request, so each window stays on its own site. If a window ever gets an answer about a project it didn't choose, Claude says so and asks rather than reporting the other site's details as yours. Which Manifest projects do I have? Plans Each project has its own plan, Free or Pro, so you only pay for the projects that need more. Compare them in the pricing section . Upgrade this project to Pro Manage my billing Only the project's owner can upgrade. Claude replies with a secure checkout link, and the project switches within seconds. The billing link lets you change or cancel the plan, update your card, and download invoices. If you cancel, Pro runs to the end of the paid period, then the project moves to Free and stays online. Teams On Pro, invite people to a project. Each person works from their own Claude with their own sign-in, and only sees the projects they're invited to. Invite sam@example.com to this project Members can edit and publish. Admins can also invite people. To start editing, the invitee opens a new Code session and asks Claude to download the latest published version . To remove someone, ask remove sam@example.com . This works on any plan. Analytics How many people visited this week, and where did they come from? Claude reports views, visits, top pages, sources, countries, and devices: the last 7 days on Free, all time on Pro. No cookies are used and no one is identified. To leave out your own visits, open your live address once with ?mnfst-team at the end, in each browser you use. Add ?mnfst-team=off to count that browser again. Expert Help Rather have the Manifest team build, finish, or fix it? Ask Claude to send this to the Manifest team , or write to us .


## GitHub Sync — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/platform/github-sync

GitHub Sync An optional backup and full history of your project on GitHub. Do You Need It? No. Manifest publishes, hosts, and keeps versions without it. GitHub helps if you want a backup of your working files, a history of every change, smoother teamwork when several people edit often, or hosting somewhere else. It needs a Code session and a free GitHub account . Claude sets up the rest, including GitHub's gh tool the first time. Save to GitHub Save my project to GitHub A GitHub sign-in opens in your browser, then Claude creates a private copy only you and people you add can see. From then on, publishing also saves to GitHub, and /manifest:sync brings in other people's changes. Add a Teammate Add sam to the project on GitHub Claude asks for their GitHub username and email, and invites them to both GitHub and the Manifest project (a Pro feature). They accept both, start a new Code session, and ask Claude to join the Manifest project . Host Somewhere Else Host this project on Netlify instead Claude connects Netlify , Cloudflare Pages , or Appwrite Sites to your GitHub copy, and the current version stays online until the new host is ready. To come back, ask Claude to move this back to Manifest hosting .

# API docs / Getting Started


## Getting Started — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/api/getting-started

Article does not exist There is no documentation at this path.


## Introduction — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/api/getting-started/introduction

Introduction The Manifest platform's API reference. Create, update, and publish projects from your own code. What the API Is For The API does from code what Claude does in a session: it creates projects, updates them, and publishes them. A project can be anything that runs in a browser, like a website, app, dashboard, or game. Manifest hosts it, with staging, HTTPS, and custom domains. For example, you could: Publish at scale , like a page for every product, location, or event. Give your customers projects , like a help center or portal for each one. Publish from your own tools , like a content system or a build pipeline. Your API key also reaches the projects you already have. How It Works Create a project , tagged with your own ID so you can find it again. Send updates : a full build, or just the files that changed. Updates land on staging. Check staging , a separate address each project has for checking changes. Promote , so the exact version you checked goes live. Add a domain , if you want one, like help.example.com . Each publish creates a deployment , one saved version of the project. Manifest keeps recent ones, so a Pro project can roll back. Both addresses are public, but staging is kept out of search results. It's for checking a change before visitors see it on production, not for keeping it private. The Quickstart runs through all of this in a few minutes. Ways to Update Upload a build. Zip your project's files and upload them. Any static build works, from the Manifest framework or any other. See Publish . Change files. Send only the files that changed: pages, data, settings, styles, or images. See Edit . Use the docs template. Send Markdown pages and get a documentation site, with no build of your own. See Docs Template . What's Included Every Manifest account can use the API. Create a key on the dashboard's API page ; see Authentication . No account yet? Signing in to the dashboard creates a free one. Projects your key creates are ordinary Manifest projects. They show in your dashboard and in Claude, and can be upgraded to Pro there. Every account Enterprise Projects created through the API Two, on the Free plan A higher cap, by contract Your existing projects ✓ "Made with Manifest" badge Shown None How to get it Dashboard Talk to us Each project keeps its own plan, so a Pro feature such as rollback needs that project on Pro. An Enterprise account's keys reach only the projects that account creates. Rate limits and storage caps are on Limits . Base URL All requests go to one versioned base URL: https://api.manifestx.dev/v1 Only /v1 paths exist on this host. Conventions JSON. Requests and responses are JSON. Bearer key. Every request sends Authorization: Bearer <key> . See Authentication . Server only. Call the API from your server. Browsers are refused. Timestamps are Unix seconds, like 1760140800 . Ids start with a prefix: acct_ for accounts, proj_ for projects, dep_ for deployments. request_id is on every response. Quote it when you contact Manifest. Safe retries. Every request that changes something can be retried safely. See Idempotency . Stuck? Common Problems maps symptoms to fixes.


## Quickstart — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/api/getting-started/quickstart

Quickstart Go from an API key to a live documentation site in a few minutes. Before You Start You need an API key from the dashboard. See Authentication . The cURL steps use jq to read ids from responses. The JavaScript steps build one script, such as quickstart.mjs , for Node 18 or later. The project you create here uses one of the two projects your free allowance can create through the API, until you delete it. The last step deletes it. Check the Key Put your key in an environment variable, then ask the API who you are. cURL JavaScript export MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY= "mnfst_api_…" curl https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/me \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " const API = 'https://api.manifestx.dev/v1' const headers = { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` , 'Content-Type' : 'application/json' , } const me = await fetch ( ` ${API} /me` , { headers }). then ( ( r ) => r. json ()) console . log (me. account . name ) A 200 with your account's name means the key works. Create a Project source_id is your own id for this project, such as a record id in your system. Keep the new project's id for the next steps. Subdomains are unique across all of Manifest, so acme-docs may already be taken. Replace it with your own, or leave subdomain out to get a free one made from name . cURL JavaScript PROJECT_ID=$(curl -s -X POST https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "source_id": "site_8231", "name": "Acme Docs", "subdomain": "acme-docs" }' \ | jq -r .project.id) echo $PROJECT_ID const { project } = await fetch ( ` ${API} /projects` , { method : 'POST' , headers, body : JSON . stringify ({ source_id : 'site_8231' , name : 'Acme Docs' , subdomain : 'acme-docs' }), }). then ( ( r ) => r. json ()) const projectId = project. id The answer is 201 Created : { "project" : { "id" : "proj_…" , "source_id" : "site_8231" , "name" : "Acme Docs" , "plan" : "free" , "status" : "active" , "project_key_prefix" : "mfst_free_AbCd1234" , "created_at" : 1792138921 , "urls" : { "production" : "https://acme-docs.manifestx.ai" , "staging" : "https://acme-docs-staging.manifestx.ai" } , "published" : { "production" : false , "staging" : false } } , "project_key" : "mfst_free_…" , "request_id" : "…" } You can ignore project_key for now. See Projects . A 409 subdomain_taken means someone else has that subdomain. Pick another and send the create again. If any step answers an error, see Common Problems . Send the Content Two Markdown pages, listed under two groups, become a documentation site. cURL JavaScript curl -X POST https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/ $PROJECT_ID /content \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " \ -H "Idempotency-Key: acme-help-sync-1" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "template": "docs", "site": { "name": "Acme Help", "description": "Answers for Acme customers." }, "articles": [ { "group": "Getting started", "title": "Welcome", "slug": "welcome", "markdown": "Hello from Acme." }, { "group": "Billing", "title": "Invoices", "slug": "invoices", "markdown": "## Download\n\nUse the portal." } ] }' const content = await fetch ( ` ${API} /projects/ ${projectId} /content` , { method : 'POST' , headers : { ...headers, 'Idempotency-Key' : 'acme-help-sync-1' }, body : JSON . stringify ({ template : 'docs' , site : { name : 'Acme Help' , description : 'Answers for Acme customers.' }, articles : [ { group : 'Getting started' , title : 'Welcome' , slug : 'welcome' , markdown : 'Hello from Acme.' }, { group : 'Billing' , title : 'Invoices' , slug : 'invoices' , markdown : '## Download\n\nUse the portal.' }, ], }), }). then ( ( r ) => r. json ()) console . log (content. url ) { "deployment" : { "id" : "dep_…" , "env" : "staging" , "status" : "ready" , "files" : 10 , "bytes" : 26537 } , "template" : { "name" : "docs" , "version" : "0.1.2" } , "url" : "https://acme-docs-staging.manifestx.ai" , "request_id" : "…" } Open Staging The site is live at url as soon as the request returns. The Invoices page is at /docs/billing/invoices on that address. The production address still says "This site hasn't been published yet." Staging isn't private. Search engines skip it, but anyone with its address can open it, so treat it as a preview, not a place for secrets. Promote Once staging looks right, make it live. cURL JavaScript curl -X POST https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/ $PROJECT_ID /promote \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " \ -H "Idempotency-Key: acme-help-promote-1" const promoted = await fetch ( ` ${API} /projects/ ${projectId} /promote` , { method : 'POST' , headers : { ...headers, 'Idempotency-Key' : 'acme-help-promote-1' }, }). then ( ( r ) => r. json ()) console . log (promoted. url ) { "deployment" : { "id" : "dep_…" , "env" : "production" , "files" : 10 } , "live_deployment_id" : "dep_…" , "url" : "https://acme-docs.manifestx.ai" , "prerender" : { "status" : "pending" } , "request_id" : "…" } The site now answers at the production url . In the background, Manifest also prerenders its pages to static HTML, and swaps that version in when it's done. See Publish . Clean Up When you're done trying it, delete the project to free its place in your allowance. cURL JavaScript curl -X DELETE https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/ $PROJECT_ID \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " await fetch ( ` ${API} /projects/ ${projectId} ` , { method : 'DELETE' , headers }) Deleting takes both addresses offline at once. The source_id site_8231 stays taken, so use a new one next time. See Delete a Project . Next Steps Update the site by sending new content whenever the pages change. Each request replaces the whole site on staging. Use your own domain with Domains . Publish your own build instead with Publish . Get notified when a publish finishes with Webhooks .


# API docs / Guides


## Guides — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/api/guides

Article does not exist There is no documentation at this path.


## Projects — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/api/guides/projects

Projects Create a project for anything you publish, find it again by your own id, and give people access to it. Create a Project Each thing you publish is one project. Create it once, tagged with your own id for it. cURL JavaScript curl -X POST https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "source_id": "site_8231", "name": "Acme Docs", "subdomain": "acme-docs" }' const res = await fetch ( 'https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects' , { method : 'POST' , headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` , 'Content-Type' : 'application/json' , }, body : JSON . stringify ({ source_id : 'site_8231' , name : 'Acme Docs' , subdomain : 'acme-docs' }), }) const { project, project_key } = await res. json () Field Type Required Notes source_id string yes Your id for this project, 1 to 128 characters. Unique within your account. name string yes Display name, 1 to 120 characters. The default subdomain comes from it. subdomain string no The exact label to use instead: 1 to 40 lowercase letters, digits, or single hyphens. The project gets <label>.manifestx.ai and <label>-staging.manifestx.ai . Unknown fields are refused with 400 invalid_input . A new project answers 201 Created : { "project" : { "id" : "proj_…" , "source_id" : "site_8231" , "name" : "Acme Docs" , "plan" : "free" , "status" : "active" , "project_key_prefix" : "mfst_free_AbCd1234" , "created_at" : 1760140800 , "urls" : { "production" : "https://acme-docs.manifestx.ai" , "staging" : "https://acme-docs-staging.manifestx.ai" } , "published" : { "production" : false , "staging" : false } } , "project_key" : "mfst_free_…" , "request_id" : "…" } project_key is the project's own key, returned once. It starts mfst_live_ on paid accounts. Give it to the project's own build pipeline if it publishes without you, or keep it in your vault. The API doesn't need it. plan is the project's own plan, such as free , pro , or api for projects an Enterprise account creates. published turns true per environment after the first publish there. The subdomains are reserved straight away. Free projects show the "Made with Manifest" badge and can appear in the Manifest showcase. Enterprise projects carry no badge and are private by default, so they never appear in the showcase. Staging and Production Each project has two addresses, both in urls , and both public. Staging is kept out of search results. Before anything is published there, an address answers 404 with "This site hasn't been published yet." Staging gets every publish, file update, and content request by default. Check changes there. Production changes only when you promote , or publish to it directly with env . Custom domains serve production unless you add them for staging. See Domains . Seeing an old version after a publish? Reload. A browser can keep a page for up to a minute. Safe to Repeat source_id makes creates safe to retry, with no extra header. You send You get The same source_id , name , and subdomain (if sent) 200 OK with the existing project, without project_key . The same source_id with a different name or subdomain 409 source_id_conflict , naming the existing project. Nothing changes. Two creates for one source_id at the same moment One project. The first gets 201 , the other 200 . A sync that re-sends the create body breaks once a project is renamed. Look the project up by source_id first, and create only when nothing comes back. Free Allowance Your keys can create up to max_projects projects through the API together, shown on GET /me . On the free allowance that's 2. Projects made with Claude or the dashboard don't count. Past the cap, a create answers 403 project_cap_reached . Existing projects are unaffected, and deleting an allowance project frees its place. Upgrading one to Pro doesn't free it. For more, talk to us about Enterprise. Find a Project by source_id cURL JavaScript curl "https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects?source_id=site_8231" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " const res = await fetch ( `https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects?source_id= ${ encodeURIComponent ( 'site_8231' )} ` , { headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` } }, ) const { projects } = await res. json () const project = projects[ 0 ] ?? null { "projects" : [ { "id" : "proj_…" , "source_id" : "site_8231" , "name" : "Acme Docs" , "…" : "…" } ] , "complete" : true , "request_id" : "…" } projects holds zero or one project: the live project your account created with that source_id . URL-encode the value. A deleted project is never returned. List Projects cURL JavaScript curl https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " const res = await fetch ( 'https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects' , { headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` }, }) const { projects, complete } = await res. json () Returns { "projects": [ … ], "complete": true, "request_id": "…" } : every live project the key reaches, newest first, shaped like the create response without project_key . Good to know: Not paginated. Every project comes in one answer. To look up one, find it by source_id . source_id is null on projects you made outside the API. complete is false when Manifest couldn't check your team roles just then. The list holds only the projects you own, so retry. Get a Project cURL JavaScript curl https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_… \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " const res = await fetch ( `https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/ ${projectId} ` , { headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` }, }) const { project } = await res. json () Returns { "project": { … }, "request_id": "…" } . A project the key can't reach answers 404 not_found , the same as one that doesn't exist. A deleted project answers 410 project_deleted . Rename a Project cURL JavaScript curl -X PATCH https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_… \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "name": "Acme Help Center" }' const res = await fetch ( `https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/ ${projectId} ` , { method : 'PATCH' , headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` , 'Content-Type' : 'application/json' , }, body : JSON . stringify ({ name : 'Acme Help Center' }), }) const { project } = await res. json () Field Type Required Notes name string yes New display name, 1 to 120 characters. Answers 200 OK with { "project": { … }, "request_id": "…" } . Only the name changes: source_id , subdomains, and custom domains stay. Creates with the same source_id then match the new name. Any other field, including source_id , is refused with 400 invalid_input . Send an Idempotency-Key to make a retry safe. Editors Give the people behind a project their own access. An invited editor signs in to Manifest with the invited email, and the project appears in their own Claude, ready to edit and publish. They never see or need an API key. Inviting editors is part of Pro, so a Free project answers 402 pro_required . Enterprise projects include it. Listing and removing editors work on every plan, so access can always be taken away. Invite an Editor cURL JavaScript curl -X POST https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/invites \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "email": "editor@acme.com" }' const res = await fetch ( `https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/ ${projectId} /invites` , { method : 'POST' , headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` , 'Content-Type' : 'application/json' , }, body : JSON . stringify ({ email : 'editor@acme.com' }), }) const { member } = await res. json () Field Type Required Notes email string yes The editor's email. They sign in with this exact address. role string no member (default) can edit and publish. admin can also invite and remove others. Manifest adds the editor to the project's team and emails them a sign-in link. A new editor answers 201 Created : { "member" : { "user_id" : "…" , "email" : "editor@acme.com" , "role" : "member" , "is_owner" : false } , "already_member" : false , "email_sent" : true , "email_skipped" : null , "request_id" : "…" } If Then They're already on the project 200 OK with "already_member": true and their current role. The role never changes. They were emailed in the last 10 minutes No new email. email_skipped is recently_sent . The address is the project owner's No email. email_skipped is self . The email couldn't be sent email_sent is false . They're still added, and can join by signing in with that address. Two invites for the same address at once seat them once. Each project accepts 50 invites a day, on every plan. Past that: 429 invite_limit , with Retry-After . List Editors cURL JavaScript curl https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/members \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " const res = await fetch ( `https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/ ${projectId} /members` , { headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` }, }) const { members, complete } = await res. json () { "members" : [ { "user_id" : "…" , "email" : "owner@example.com" , "role" : "owner" , "is_owner" : true } , { "user_id" : "…" , "email" : "editor@acme.com" , "role" : "member" , "is_owner" : false } ] , "complete" : true , "request_id" : "…" } role is owner , admin , or member , and the owner is always first. complete is false when Manifest couldn't reach the team just then. The list then holds only the owner, so retry. Remove an Editor Use the user_id from the invite or the list. cURL JavaScript curl -X DELETE https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/members/USER_ID \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " await fetch ( `https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/ ${projectId} /members/ ${userId} ` , { method : 'DELETE' , headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` }, }) { "removed" : { "user_id" : "…" , "email" : "editor@acme.com" } , "request_id" : "…" } Access ends at once. The editor keeps their own Manifest account. The project owner can't be removed ( 403 owner_not_removable ). Editors Outlive Your Keys An editor's access belongs to the project, not to the key that invited them. Revoking or rotating a key removes no one. If a key leaks, list each project's editors and remove anyone you didn't invite. Delete a Project cURL JavaScript curl -X DELETE https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_… \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " const res = await fetch ( `https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/ ${projectId} ` , { method : 'DELETE' , headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` }, }) const { purge_after } = await res. json () { "deleted" : "proj_…" , "deleted_at" : 1762041600 , "purge_after" : 1764633600 , "request_id" : "…" } The project goes offline at once. Staging and production stop serving, the default subdomains are released, and custom domains are detached. The source_id stays taken for good. After a delete: The project's own key stops working, and the project leaves GET /projects . Any request for it answers 410 project_deleted , including a second delete. On the free allowance, its place is freed straight away. A create that reuses its source_id answers 409 source_id_deleted . A project.deleted webhook is sent once. Restoring. Files and history are kept for 30 days, until purge_after . Within that window, email team@manifestx.dev with the project id and Manifest can restore it. A restore brings back staging, production, and the default subdomains. Custom domains come back pending, because their certificates were released. Manifest sends the DNS records to check again, and the domain's status shows when it's active. A subdomain or domain another project took in the meantime can't be returned. Who can delete. Only the owner can delete a project made outside the API; an admin gets 403 forbidden . A project with a Pro subscription answers 409 subscription_active , so cancel it in the dashboard first. Which Projects a Key Reaches Project What the key can do Projects you own or admin Publish, promote, roll back, rename, list deployments, manage domains, and invite or remove editors. Projects your keys create All of the above, plus the docs template . Your own projects are the ones in your dashboard, made in Claude, in the dashboard, or through the API. Team projects need the owner or admin role. As a member, the key gets 403 forbidden . Another account's projects are out of reach. They answer 404 not_found , like a project that doesn't exist. Enterprise keys reach only the projects that account creates. Each project keeps its own plan. Publishing, staging, promote, and custom domains work on every plan. Rollback is part of Pro, so a Free project answers 402 pro_required . To move a project to Pro, its owner upgrades it from the dashboard . Projects your keys create are listed there, and in Claude, like any other project of yours. Errors Every error has the same shape . These are the ones specific to projects and editors. Status error Meaning 400 invalid_input A field is missing, malformed, or unknown, or the body isn't JSON. 400 invalid_subdomain subdomain isn't 1 to 40 lowercase letters, digits, or single hyphens. 402 pro_required Inviting editors is part of Pro. Upgrade the project in the dashboard. 403 project_cap_reached Your account's project cap is reached. The message names the cap. 403 forbidden You're a member, not the owner or an admin. Deleting a project made outside the API needs its owner. 403 owner_not_removable The project owner can't be removed. 404 not_found No such project, or the key can't reach it. 404 member_not_found No one with that user_id is on the project. 409 source_id_conflict source_id already names a project with a different name or subdomain . 409 source_id_deleted source_id named a project that was deleted. Use a new one. 409 subdomain_taken Another project has that subdomain. 409 subscription_active The project has a Pro subscription. Cancel it in the dashboard, then delete. 410 project_deleted The project was deleted. The message says until when Manifest can restore it. 422 subdomain_reserved That subdomain is reserved, like login or billing . 422 invite_failed Manifest's team service refused the address. The message says why; fix it rather than retrying. 429 invite_limit The project's 50 invites for today are used. Wait the seconds in Retry-After . 503 membership_unverified Manifest couldn't check your role on a team project. Nothing was done. Retry. 503 team_unavailable Manifest couldn't reach the project's team. No one was invited or removed. Retry. Idempotency errors are on Errors .


## Edit — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/api/guides/edit

Edit Read and change a project's files. How Editing Works Any file in a project can be changed: pages, data, manifest.json , styles, images, and more. Each update becomes a new deployment on staging, so you can check it before you promote it . You read and change the files Manifest serves. For projects built with the Manifest framework or plain HTML, those are the files you wrote. Frameworks like React, Vite, or Astro serve compiled output instead, so change their source and publish a new build . To start from nothing, publish a build , or send an update that includes an index.html . For a documentation site from Markdown, the Docs Template builds one in a single request. Read Files List the files of the live deployment, so you can see what to change. cURL JavaScript curl "https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/files?env=staging" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " const res = await fetch ( 'https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/files?env=staging' , { headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` }, }) Field Type Required Notes env string no staging (default) or production . limit number no Files per page, 1 to 1,000. Defaults to 1,000. cursor string no The next_cursor from the previous page. { "env" : "staging" , "deployment_id" : "dep_…" , "files" : [ { "path" : "_redirects" , "size" : 64 , "content_type" : "application/octet-stream" , "etag" : "9b2e…" } , { "path" : "_redirects.json" , "size" : 210 , "content_type" : "application/json; charset=utf-8" , "etag" : "41c7…" , "compiled_from" : "_redirects" } , { "path" : "articles/intro.md" , "size" : 1834 , "content_type" : "text/markdown; charset=utf-8" , "etag" : "e3b0…" } , { "path" : "index.html" , "size" : 2210 , "content_type" : "text/html; charset=utf-8" , "etag" : "5d41…" } ] , "next_cursor" : null , "request_id" : "…" } Paths match what a file update takes, sorted by path. etag changes when a file's content does. Treat it as opaque: the same content can carry a different etag if published another way. compiled_from marks a file Manifest compiles. Edit the source file instead. Left out: precache.json and manifest.utilities.css , which Manifest writes on every publish. Nothing live yet: deployment_id is null and files is empty. More pages: send next_cursor as cursor . A cursor keeps reading the same deployment, even if a new one goes live meanwhile. Read One File Fetch one file's content from the deployment live on env ( staging by default). cURL JavaScript curl "https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/files/articles/intro.md" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " const res = await fetch ( 'https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/files/articles/intro.md' , { headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` }, }) const text = await res. text () const base = res. headers . get ( 'x-manifest-deployment' ) The answer is the file itself, not JSON, with these headers: Header Value Content-Type The file's type, such as text/markdown; charset=utf-8 or image/png . ETag The file's etag from the list, in quotes. x-manifest-deployment The deployment the file came from. Send it as base with your update. HTML comes back as stored, without the tags Manifest adds when serving. Send If-None-Match with the ETag to get 304 Not Modified when nothing changed. Encode special characters in the path the way a browser would, such as a space as %20 . Update Files When only a few files change, send just those. Manifest keeps everything else that is live on staging and publishes the result as a new staging deployment. cURL JavaScript curl -X PATCH https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/files \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " \ -H "Idempotency-Key: edit-intro-0042" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "base": "dep_…", "files": [ { "path": "articles/intro.md", "content": "# Introduction\n\nUpdated text." }, { "path": "media/logo.png", "content_base64": "iVBORw0KGgo…" }, { "path": "articles/old.md", "delete": true } ] }' const res = await fetch ( 'https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/files' , { method : 'PATCH' , headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` , 'Idempotency-Key' : 'edit-intro-0042' , 'Content-Type' : 'application/json' , }, body : JSON . stringify ({ base : 'dep_…' , files : [ { path : 'articles/intro.md' , content : '# Introduction\n\nUpdated text.' }, { path : 'media/logo.png' , content_base64 : 'iVBORw0KGgo…' }, { path : 'articles/old.md' , delete : true }, ], }), }) Field Type Required Notes files array yes 1 to 1,000 changes, one per path. base string no The deployment your changes start from. If staging has moved on since, nothing changes and the answer is 409 base_mismatch . env string no Only staging . Promote to reach production. Each change has a path from the project root (inside output_dir , if the build has one) and exactly one of these: Field Type Notes content string The new file as UTF-8 text, for Markdown, JSON, HTML, CSS, and other text files. content_base64 string The new file as standard base64, for images and other binary files. delete boolean true removes the file. A path that doesn't exist yet adds a file. The answer is 201 Created , and the new version is live on the staging URL straight away: { "deployment" : { "id" : "dep_…" , "env" : "staging" , "status" : "ready" , "files" : 43 , "bytes" : 320544 , "base" : "dep_…" } , "changes" : { "updated" : 2 , "deleted" : 1 } , "url" : "https://acme-docs-staging.manifestx.ai" , "request_id" : "…" } On a project built from the Docs Template , the next template request rebuilds everything and replaces these changes. The answer warns with a template_site notice. Avoid Overwriting Others Send the last deployment.id you saw as base , so two editors can't overwrite each other. Read the files and note the deployment_id . Send your update with that id as base . On 409 base_mismatch , read the files again, reapply your change, and send it with the new live_deployment_id . Without base , changes apply to whatever is live on staging. Either way, an update is refused with the same 409 if another publish lands while it runs, and you can send it again. Good to Know Limits. A request can be up to 12 MB, with each file up to 8 MB after decoding. Publish larger files in a zip. First publish. If nothing is live on staging yet, the files become the project's first version and must include index.html . No update can remove index.html . Refused paths. .env files, .git , node_modules , .claude , precache.json , and manifest.utilities.css are refused. Redirects and headers. Manifest compiles _redirects and _headers into .json files. Update the source file, not the compiled one. HTML read back is fine. The analytics and badge tags Manifest adds when serving a page are removed before the file is stored. Prerendered builds. On render output, the answer carries a prerendered_site notice: pages built from the changed files aren't rebuilt, so publish a new build to refresh them. It counts as a publish. Each update counts toward a Free project's daily publish limit. It's also a new deployment, so frequent updates push older versions out of rollback reach. A rare warning. If a follow-up step doesn't finish, the answer is still 201 with a warning . Don't resend it: the step completes on the next publish.


## Docs Template — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/api/guides/docs-template

Docs Template Generate a documentation site from Markdown pages in one request. Send Pages Send a name, a theme, navigation groups, and Markdown pages, and Manifest builds a documentation site from its docs template. There's no build step on your side. The template is a shortcut. For your own navigation, files, images, and design, publish your own build instead. Each request replaces the whole site on that environment. Send every page each time, not only the ones that changed. Save the content as content.json : content.json { "template" : "docs" , "env" : "staging" , "site" : { "name" : "Acme Help" , "description" : "Answers for Acme customers." , "theme" : { "tokens" : { "color-brand-surface" : "oklch(55% 0.2 260)" } , "dark" : { "color-brand-surface" : "#6677ff" } } } , "groups" : [ { "slug" : "start" , "description" : "First steps with Acme." } ] , "articles" : [ { "group" : "Getting started" , "group_slug" : "start" , "title" : "Welcome" , "slug" : "welcome" , "markdown" : "Hello from Acme." , "order" : 1 } , { "group" : "Billing" , "title" : "Invoices" , "slug" : "invoices" , "markdown" : "## Download\n\nUse the portal." , "icon" : "lucide:receipt" } ] } Then send it: cURL JavaScript curl -X POST https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/content \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " \ -H "Idempotency-Key: help-center-sync-0193" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d @content.json import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises' const res = await fetch ( `https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/ ${projectId} /content` , { method : 'POST' , headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` , 'Idempotency-Key' : 'help-center-sync-0193' , 'Content-Type' : 'application/json' , }, body : await readFile ( 'content.json' ), }) const { deployment, url } = await res. json () The site answers 201 Created and is live on that environment's address straight away: { "deployment" : { "id" : "dep_…" , "env" : "staging" , "status" : "ready" , "files" : 10 , "bytes" : 26676 } , "template" : { "name" : "docs" , "version" : "0.1.2" } , "url" : "https://acme-docs-staging.manifestx.ai" , "request_id" : "…" } The Invoices page is now at /docs/billing/invoices on that address. Promote, rollback, and the deployment list work exactly as for your own builds. Good to know: Projects your keys created only. On your other projects, content answers 422 not_api_project , so it never replaces a project you built another way. Publish a zip to those instead. Production ingests also return a prerender object, usually { "status": "pending" } . Manifest renders every page to static HTML in the background, then swaps that version in. A warning with code post_publish_incomplete means the site is live but a follow-up step, like setting up the default address, didn't finish. Don't resend. It completes on the next publish that changes the content, and url can be null until then. Fields Field Type Required Notes template string yes docs . env string no staging (default) or production . site.name string yes Page title, header, and app name. site.description string no Meta description and the landing-page intro. site.theme object no tokens (light) and dark : theme token names mapped to CSS values. See Theme Values . groups array no { slug, description? } per group. Listed groups come first, in this order, with their description. articles array yes The pages. At least one. Each entry in articles is one page: Field Type Required Notes group string yes Group name shown in the navigation. group_slug string no The group's URL segment. Defaults to the group name, lowercased, with hyphens. title string yes The page title. slug string yes The page's URL segment. See Slugs . markdown string yes The page body. If its first line isn't a # heading, the title is added as one. icon string no An Iconify name, like lucide:receipt . Defaults to lucide:file-text . order number no Position within the group. Pages without one follow, in the order sent. Any field not listed here is refused, and so is Markdown with control characters. Images and other files aren't part of the request, so link to them by full URL. Unchanged Content On staging, content identical to what's live there answers 200 OK with unchanged: true . No deployment is created, and nothing counts toward the daily publish limit. So a scheduled sync can send everything every time, and the site rebuilds only when something changed. { "unchanged" : true , "deployment" : { "id" : "dep_…" , "env" : "staging" , "status" : "ready" , "files" : 10 , "bytes" : 26676 } , "template" : { "name" : "docs" , "version" : "0.1.2" } , "url" : "https://acme-docs-staging.manifestx.ai" , "request_id" : "…" } Good to know: Order matters, formatting doesn't. Key order and whitespace are ignored, but the order of articles and groups counts. It compares with what's live , not your last request. After a file update or rollback to a version your content didn't build, the next ingest deploys. Production always deploys , even when nothing changed. Slugs A page is served at /docs/<group_slug>/<slug> . Slugs are lowercase words joined by single hyphens, like payment-methods . A page slug is unique across all groups, not only its own. A page slug can't match a group slug. Name a billing page in a billing group billing-overview instead. Neither can be docs , the segment the site lives under. Each group_slug has one group name, and two groups can't share a name. Theme Values tokens and dark map the template's theme token names to CSS values. Write names with or without the leading -- , but not both for one token. Allowed: colors, numbers, lengths, quoted font names, and the functions rgb , rgba , hsl , hsla , hwb , lab , lch , oklab , oklch , color , color-mix , var , calc , min , max , clamp , and light-dark . Refused: url() , comments, semicolons, braces, unclosed quotes or parentheses, and values over 200 characters. Template Version A project's first successful ingest pins the docs template version it used. Later ingests keep that version, so a template update never changes a live site unasked. The version is in every response. Limits Limit Value Request body 12 MB Pages per request 1,000 Markdown per page 512 KB Markdown per request, in total 10 MB Entries in groups 100 Slug and group_slug 80 characters, including a group_slug made from the group name Group name, page title 200 characters Group description, site description 1,000 characters Site name 120 characters Theme tokens 100 each for light and dark Theme value 200 characters Retries Send an Idempotency-Key with every request. A retry with the same key and body returns the first answer and creates no second deployment. See Idempotency . Errors Every error has the same shape . A content problem answers 422 with a field naming the page and property, and no deployment is created: { "error" : "invalid_content" , "message" : "articles[1].slug: invalid slug \"Bad Slug\"." , "field" : "articles[1].slug" , "request_id" : "…" } Status error Meaning 400 invalid_input The body isn't UTF-8 JSON or an object, has an unknown top-level field, or template or env is wrong. 403 plan_required The project's plan doesn't include publishing to that environment. 403 storage_cap_reached The site would take the account over its storage cap. Nothing changed. See Limits . 404 not_found No such project, or the key can't reach it. 413 payload_too_large The body is over 12 MB. 422 invalid_content A slug, size, theme value, or page field is invalid. field says which. 422 not_api_project The project wasn't created through the API. Publish a zip to it instead. 429 publish_limit_reached A Free project's daily publish limit is reached. Wait the seconds in Retry-After . 500 ingest_failed The deployment failed before going live. What was live is unchanged. Retry. 503 template_unavailable The docs template couldn't load. Retry shortly.


## Publish — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/api/guides/publish

Publish Publish a build, take it live, and roll back. Publish a Build If you build the project yourself, publish the output as a zip. Any static build works, from the Manifest framework or any other. Start a publish to get a one-time upload URL. Upload the zip to that URL. Check the status until it's live. Promote staging to production. To review a build before it reaches staging, publish it without going live and promote that exact deployment by id. Every publish is a new deployment, so a bad release can be rolled back . To change a few files without a new zip, see Edit . Start a Publish Get a one-time upload URL for a new deployment. cURL JavaScript curl -X POST https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/publish \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " \ -H "Idempotency-Key: build-4182-staging" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "env": "staging", "source": "spa" }' const res = await fetch ( 'https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/publish' , { method : 'POST' , headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` , 'Idempotency-Key' : 'build-4182-staging' , 'Content-Type' : 'application/json' , }, body : JSON . stringify ({ env : 'staging' , source : 'spa' }), }) const { upload_url, status_url } = await res. json () Field Type Required Notes source string yes spa for any static build. render for mnfst-render output. env string no staging (default) or production . output_dir string no The folder inside the zip to serve, such as dist . Defaults to the zip root for spa , and website for render . label string no A name for this deployment, such as a version or commit subject. Up to 200 characters, no line breaks. Shown in the deployment list and in webhook events. live boolean no Staging only. false stores the deployment without changing what staging serves. See Publish Without Going Live . The answer is 201 Created : { "deployment" : { "id" : "dep_…" , "env" : "staging" , "source" : "spa" , "output_dir" : "" , "status" : "uploading" , "label" : null } , "upload_url" : "https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/uploads/put_…" , "status_url" : "https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/uploads/put_…/status" , "expires_in_seconds" : 900 , "request_id" : "…" } One use, 15 minutes. The upload URL works once and expires after 15 minutes. No key needed to upload. The token in the URL is its own authority, so the machine that uploads never needs your API key. Safe to retry. With an Idempotency-Key , a retried start returns the same URL instead of opening a second deployment. Upload the Zip Send the zip to upload_url . No Authorization header is needed. cURL JavaScript curl -X POST " $UPLOAD_URL " \ -H "x-mnfst-async: 1" \ --data-binary @site.zip import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises' const upload = await fetch (upload_url, { method : 'POST' , headers : { 'x-mnfst-async' : '1' }, body : await readFile ( 'site.zip' ), }) With x-mnfst-async: 1 , the upload answers 202 as soon as the zip is stored, and you check the status from there: { "status" : "ingesting" , "deployment_id" : "dep_…" , "env" : "staging" , "status_url" : "https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/uploads/put_…/status" , "poll_after_ms" : 1000 , "message" : "Upload stored — publishing continues with each status poll. Poll status_url until status is \"done\"." } Without the header, the upload waits and answers with the final outcome, the same as a done or error status. Limits. A zip can be up to 80 MB, or 250 MB unzipped, with up to 10,000 files of 25 MB each. See Limits . Never published. .env files, .git , node_modules , and .claude are skipped, even when they're in the zip. Only changes are stored. Manifest stores each file's content once per project, so a publish only stores files that changed. Sending again is safe. Sending the zip again to a finished URL publishes nothing new. It answers with the first outcome. Check the Status Poll status_url about once a second until status is done or error . cURL JavaScript curl " $STATUS_URL " let status do { await new Promise ( ( r ) => setTimeout (r, 1000 )) status = await ( await fetch (status_url)). json () } while (status. status === 'pending' || status. status === 'ingesting' ) { "status" : "done" , "ok" : true , "deployment_id" : "dep_…" , "env" : "staging" , "files" : 42 , "bytes" : 318211 , "url" : "https://acme-docs-staging.manifestx.ai" } status HTTP Meaning pending 200 The URL is valid, and no upload has arrived yet. ingesting 200 The zip is stored and being published. written and files show progress. done 200 Live on that environment's URL. error 200 The publish failed. error and message say why, and http_status is what the upload would have answered, such as 413 . unknown 404 The URL expired or doesn't exist ( unknown_token ). Start a new publish. Keep polling until the status settles. Each poll carries the publish forward, so a large upload that nobody polls may not finish. Status reads are capped at 120 a minute per IP address. A publish.ready webhook can also tell your systems when a publish is live. Upload and status errors are listed in Errors . Publish Without Going Live Store a build on staging and review it at its own address, while staging keeps serving what it served before. Send "live": false : cURL JavaScript curl -X POST https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/publish \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " \ -H "Idempotency-Key: build-4182-held" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "env": "staging", "source": "spa", "live": false, "label": "v2.4.0" }' const res = await fetch ( 'https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/publish' , { method : 'POST' , headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` , 'Idempotency-Key' : 'build-4182-held' , 'Content-Type' : 'application/json' , }, body : JSON . stringify ({ env : 'staging' , source : 'spa' , live : false , label : 'v2.4.0' }), }) const { deployment, upload_url } = await res. json () { "deployment" : { "id" : "dep_…" , "env" : "staging" , "source" : "spa" , "output_dir" : "" , "status" : "uploading" , "label" : "v2.4.0" , "live" : false , "preview_url" : "https://preview--….manifestx.ai" } , "upload_url" : "https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/uploads/put_…" , "status_url" : "https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/uploads/put_…/status" , "expires_in_seconds" : 900 , "request_id" : "…" } Upload and check the status as usual. When it's done , the status carries "live": false and the same preview_url : { "status" : "done" , "ok" : true , "deployment_id" : "dep_…" , "env" : "staging" , "live" : false , "url" : "https://preview--….manifestx.ai" , "preview_url" : "https://preview--….manifestx.ai" , "label" : "v2.4.0" , "files" : 42 , "bytes" : 318211 } The preview serves exactly that deployment. Its address never changes, and search engines skip it, the same as staging. Unlisted, not private. Anyone with the address can open it, the same as staging. The address can't be guessed. No publish.ready event. Nothing went live. Promoting it sends promote.done . Pages only. Forms, payments and AI chat don't answer on a preview address. Test those on staging or production. Kept like any staging deployment. Staging keeps its five most recent deployments plus the live one, so promote a held build before five newer staging publishes push it out. Production only takes promotes. "live": false with "env": "production" answers 400 invalid_input . Every staging deployment that finished has a preview_url in the deployment list , not only held ones. Promote to Production Ship exactly what is live on staging to production, with no rebuild. To ship a specific staging deployment instead, such as one published without going live , name it. cURL JavaScript curl -X POST https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/promote \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " \ -H "Idempotency-Key: promote-build-4182" const res = await fetch ( 'https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/promote' , { method : 'POST' , headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` , 'Idempotency-Key' : 'promote-build-4182' , }, }) Field Type Required Notes deployment_id string no A staging deployment to promote. Omit it to promote what staging serves. Staging is unchanged either way. expect_live string no The production deployment you expect to be live. The promote is refused with 409 live_moved unless it still is, checked in the same step as the switch, so two releases can't cross. On a prerendered project, the deployment you promoted also matches once its prerendered copy is live. { "deployment" : { "id" : "dep_…" , "env" : "production" , "files" : 42 , "label" : "v2.4.0" } , "from_deployment_id" : "dep_…" , "live_deployment_id" : "dep_…" , "url" : "https://acme-docs.manifestx.ai" , "request_id" : "…" } A deployment_id must be a ready or superseded staging deployment of this project. Anything else is refused and production is unchanged: see Errors . Promote doesn't copy files, so even large projects promote in seconds. Each promote creates a new production deployment, so send an Idempotency-Key : a retry with the same key returns the first result. Some projects are also prerendered after a promote. Roll Back Point an environment back at an earlier deployment, instantly and without copying anything. Rollback is part of Pro. On a Free project it answers 402 pro_required . cURL JavaScript curl -X POST https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/rollback \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " \ -H "Idempotency-Key: rollback-build-4182" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "env": "production" }' const res = await fetch ( 'https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/rollback' , { method : 'POST' , headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` , 'Idempotency-Key' : 'rollback-build-4182' , 'Content-Type' : 'application/json' , }, body : JSON . stringify ({ env : 'production' }), }) Field Type Required Notes env string no production (default) or staging . deployment_id string no The version to restore. Omit it to go back to the version before the live one. { "env" : "production" , "live_deployment_id" : "dep_…" , "url" : "https://acme-docs.manifestx.ai" , "request_id" : "…" } To roll forward again, roll back to the newer deployment_id . Undo on Free Without rollback, undo a mistake by sending the earlier version again as a new deployment: Your own build: publish the earlier zip to staging, then promote it. Docs template: send the earlier content again. File updates: send the earlier file contents, or restore deleted files. Keep your earlier builds and content. The API only reads files from what's live now. List Deployments See an environment's recent deployments, newest first. cURL JavaScript curl "https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/deployments?env=staging" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " const res = await fetch ( 'https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/deployments?env=staging' , { headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` }, }) Field Type Required Notes env string no production (default) or staging . { "env" : "staging" , "live_deployment_id" : "dep_b…" , "deployments" : [ { "id" : "dep_c…" , "env" : "staging" , "source" : "spa" , "status" : "ready" , "is_live" : false , "files" : 43 , "bytes" : 320410 , "created_at" : 1760227200 , "label" : "v2.4.0" , "held" : true , "preview_url" : "https://preview--c….manifestx.ai" } , { "id" : "dep_b…" , "env" : "staging" , "source" : "spa" , "status" : "ready" , "is_live" : true , "files" : 42 , "bytes" : 318211 , "created_at" : 1760140800 , "label" : null , "preview_url" : "https://preview--b….manifestx.ai" } , { "id" : "dep_a…" , "env" : "staging" , "source" : "spa" , "status" : "superseded" , "is_live" : false , "files" : 40 , "bytes" : 301877 , "created_at" : 1760054400 , "label" : null , "preview_url" : "https://preview--a….manifestx.ai" } ] , "request_id" : "…" } ready and superseded deployments can be restored with a rollback. uploading and failed ones can't. held marks a deployment published without going live , and label is the name it was published with. Each environment keeps its five most recent deployments plus the live one, and older ones are deleted. Keep your build artifacts if you might need an older version. Production on a prerendered project keeps ten, since each promoted deployment and its prerendered copy count separately. Prerender Some production deployments are prerendered: Manifest renders every page to static HTML in the background, then makes that live. This applies to projects built from the Docs Template and to spa projects with prerendering turned on. Their promote answer includes a prerender object, usually { "status": "pending" } . The new version is live straight away as built. The prerendered version replaces it when done, unless production has moved on. prerender.status Meaning pending , running Queued or rendering. done The prerendered deployment is live. failed It didn't finish. The deployment you promoted stays live. superseded A newer production deployment replaced it first. Follow it in the production deployment list . There, prerender also shows routes ( done and total ) while it runs, the prerendered deployment_id once done, and error if it failed.
