The prerendered deployment itself has source render and "prerender": { "status": "done", "from": "dep_…" } . Errors Every error code for uploads, file updates, promotes, and rollbacks is in Errors , with what to do.


## Domains — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/api/guides/domains

Domains Serve a project on a domain of its own. How It Works A project can answer on its own domain as well as its manifestx.ai address. Manifest doesn't register or sell domains. Add the domain . The answer lists the DNS record to create. The domain's owner adds that record where the domain's DNS is managed, usually the registrar. Manifest issues the HTTPS certificate. Check the status until it reads active . Add a Domain Attach a hostname to a project and get the DNS records to add. cURL JavaScript curl -X POST https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/domains \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " \ -H "Idempotency-Key: domain-site_8231-docs" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "hostname": "docs.acme.com" }' const res = await fetch ( 'https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/domains' , { method : 'POST' , headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` , 'Idempotency-Key' : 'domain-site_8231-docs' , 'Content-Type' : 'application/json' , }, body : JSON . stringify ({ hostname : 'docs.acme.com' }), }) Field Type Required Notes hostname string yes Such as docs.acme.com . No scheme or path. env string no The environment it serves: production (default) or staging . validation string no http (default) or txt . See Moving a Live Domain . A new domain answers 201 Created : { "domain" : { "hostname" : "docs.acme.com" , "requested" : "docs.acme.com" , "env" : "production" , "validation" : "http" , "status" : "pending" , "certificate_status" : "pending_validation" } , "records" : [ { "purpose" : "Point the domain to the site" , "type" : "CNAME" , "name" : "docs" , "value" : "cname.manifestx.ai" } ] , "root_redirect" : null , "request_id" : "…" } Each item in records is one DNS record to create. Put type in the record type, name in the Name or Host field, and value in the value or target. These are the same records the Manifest connector gives. Sending the same hostname again updates it in place, for example to switch validation , and answers 200 . A project can have up to 25 custom domains, and a hostname can belong to only one project. Root Domains A root domain such as acme.com is served at www.acme.com , shown in domain.hostname . Most DNS providers can't point a root domain with a CNAME. root_redirect then describes the forwarding to set up at the registrar, so acme.com goes to https://www.acme.com . Moving a Live Domain For a domain already in use elsewhere, send "validation": "txt" . records then starts with a TXT record. Add only the TXT record. The certificate is issued while the old site keeps serving. Once the status shows the certificate active , add the CNAME. Traffic moves with HTTPS on both sides. Check the Status See whether the domain is live, and which records are still needed. cURL JavaScript curl https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/domains/docs.acme.com \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " const res = await fetch ( 'https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/domains/docs.acme.com' , { headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` }, }) { "domain" : { "hostname" : "docs.acme.com" , "env" : "production" , "status" : "pending" , "hostname_status" : "pending" , "certificate_status" : "pending_validation" , "certificate_validation" : { "method" : "http" , "expected_records" : [ ] , "errors" : [ ] } } , "records" : [ { "purpose" : "Point the domain to the site" , "type" : "CNAME" , "name" : "docs" , "value" : "cname.manifestx.ai" } ] , "request_id" : "…" } status Meaning pending Waiting for the DNS record or the certificate. Usually a few minutes after the record is added. active Verified, with its certificate, and serving the project. error Validation failed or timed out, or the domain was removed at the provider. Check the records and add the domain again. Poll about once a minute while status is pending . records repeats what to add, so you can show it again. With txt validation, the TXT record is listed until the certificate is issued. hostname_status and certificate_status are the underlying states. certificate_validation lists what's still expected until the certificate is active. Once active , a later error , such as a failed renewal, doesn't take the project off the domain. Fix the records and add it again. The exception is hostname_status deleted : that domain stops serving until it's added again and validates. Remove a Domain Detach a domain from the project. cURL JavaScript curl -X DELETE https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/domains/docs.acme.com \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " const res = await fetch ( 'https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/domains/docs.acme.com' , { method : 'DELETE' , headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` }, }) { "removed" : "docs.acme.com" , "request_id" : "…" } The project stops answering on that domain at once, and the domain is free to add elsewhere. The CNAME can then be deleted at the DNS provider. Errors Domain errors, such as hostname_taken and domain_cap_reached , are in Errors , with what to do.


## Webhooks — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/api/guides/webhooks

Webhooks Get told when a publish goes live or fails, a promote or rollback lands, or a project is deleted, instead of polling. Set Up an Endpoint A webhook endpoint is an https URL on your side. It receives a POST for each event on the projects your API keys created. Your other projects send no events. Each endpoint has its own signing secret, starting whsec_ , shown once when the endpoint is created. An account can have 3 endpoints on the free allowance and 10 on Enterprise, counting disabled ones. Create an Endpoint cURL JavaScript curl -X POST https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/webhooks \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " \ -H "Idempotency-Key: add-webhook-prod-1" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "url": "https://example.com/hooks/manifest", "events": ["publish.ready", "publish.failed"] }' const res = await fetch ( 'https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/webhooks' , { method : 'POST' , headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` , 'Idempotency-Key' : 'add-webhook-prod-1' , 'Content-Type' : 'application/json' , }, body : JSON . stringify ({ url : 'https://example.com/hooks/manifest' , events : [ 'publish.ready' , 'publish.failed' ], }), }) const { webhook, secret } = await res. json () Field Type Required Notes url string yes Where events are sent. See the rules below. events array no The events to receive. Omit it to receive every event, including types added later. The response is 201 and carries the secret once: { "webhook" : { "id" : "whep_…" , "url" : "https://example.com/hooks/manifest" , "events" : [ "publish.ready" , "publish.failed" ] , "created_at" : 1793437200 , "status" : "enabled" , "disabled_at" : null , "disabled_reason" : null , "delivery" : { "last_attempt_at" : null , "last_status" : null , "last_error" : null , "last_success_at" : null , "consecutive_failures" : 0 , "failing_since" : null , "pending" : 0 , "dead" : 0 } } , "secret" : "whsec_…" , "request_id" : "…" } Store the secret where your receiver reads it, such as MANIFEST_WEBHOOK_SECRET . It is never shown again. To replace it, delete the endpoint, then create a new one. Send an Idempotency-Key so a retried request returns the same endpoint and secret instead of creating a second. See Idempotency . events is null on an endpoint that receives every event. The URL must be https on the default port, with no username or password. It must name a public host, such as hooks.example.com . IP addresses, single-label names, names ending in a dot, localhost , localhost.localdomain , and names ending in .localhost , .local or .internal answer 400 invalid_url . List Endpoints GET /webhooks lists the account's endpoints, oldest first, each with its delivery health . It never returns a secret. cURL JavaScript curl https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/webhooks \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " const res = await fetch ( 'https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/webhooks' , { headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` }, }) const { webhooks } = await res. json () { "webhooks" : [ { "id" : "whep_…" , "url" : "https://example.com/hooks/manifest" , "events" : null , "created_at" : 1793437200 , "status" : "enabled" , "disabled_at" : null , "disabled_reason" : null , "delivery" : { "last_attempt_at" : 1793440800 , "last_status" : 204 , "last_error" : null , "last_success_at" : 1793440800 , "consecutive_failures" : 0 , "failing_since" : null , "pending" : 0 , "dead" : 0 } } ] , "request_id" : "…" } GET /webhooks/:id returns one endpoint in the same shape, as webhook . Delete an Endpoint cURL JavaScript curl -X DELETE https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/webhooks/whep_… \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " await fetch ( `https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/webhooks/ ${webhookId} ` , { method : 'DELETE' , headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` }, }) { "deleted" : "whep_…" , "request_id" : "…" } Nothing more is sent to it, including retries of events it hadn't received yet. Test It Send a test event to check that your receiver answers 2xx and verifies the signature. cURL JavaScript curl -X POST https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/webhooks/whep_…/test \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " const res = await fetch ( `https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/webhooks/ ${webhookId} /test` , { method : 'POST' , headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` }, }) const { message_id } = await res. json () { "message_id" : "msg_test_…" , "event" : "webhook.test" , "request_id" : "…" } The response is 202 : a webhook.test event is on its way to that endpoint only, whatever events it lists. It is signed and retried like any other event, and message_id is its webhook-id header. Read the endpoint again to see the result under delivery . Events Event Sent when publish.ready A publish, content request, or file update is live on its environment. publish.failed A publish stopped before going live, including an upload not finished within a day. What was live is unchanged. promote.done A staging deployment is live on production: what staging served, or the one the promote named. rollback.done An environment points at an earlier deployment again. project.deleted A project was deleted. Its sites are offline, and Manifest can restore it for 30 days. webhook.test You asked for a test event . Only that endpoint receives it, and it can't be listed in events . Publishes, promotes, and rollbacks send their events whether they're made through the API, from Claude, or in the dashboard. Deletes send theirs from the API or the dashboard. New fields and event types may be added, so ignore what you don't recognise. Payload Each event is one JSON body with type , timestamp (ISO 8601, when it happened), and data . publish.ready publish.failed promote.done rollback.done project.deleted webhook.test { "type" : "publish.ready" , "timestamp" : "2026-10-31T09:14:05.000Z" , "data" : { "project_id" : "proj_…" , "source_id" : "site_8232" , "deployment_id" : "dep_…" , "env" : "staging" , "label" : "v2.4.0" , "url" : "https://acme-docs-staging.manifestx.ai" , "files" : 42 , "bytes" : 318211 } } { "type" : "publish.failed" , "timestamp" : "2026-10-31T09:14:05.000Z" , "data" : { "project_id" : "proj_…" , "source_id" : "site_8232" , "deployment_id" : "dep_…" , "env" : "staging" , "error" : "upload_expired" } } { "type" : "promote.done" , "timestamp" : "2026-10-31T09:14:05.000Z" , "data" : { "project_id" : "proj_…" , "source_id" : "site_8232" , "deployment_id" : "dep_…" , "env" : "production" , "from_deployment_id" : "dep_…" , "label" : "v2.4.0" , "url" : "https://acme-docs.manifestx.ai" , "files" : 42 } } { "type" : "rollback.done" , "timestamp" : "2026-10-31T09:14:05.000Z" , "data" : { "project_id" : "proj_…" , "source_id" : "site_8232" , "deployment_id" : "dep_…" , "env" : "production" , "previous_deployment_id" : "dep_…" , "url" : "https://acme-docs.manifestx.ai" } } { "type" : "project.deleted" , "timestamp" : "2026-10-31T09:14:05.000Z" , "data" : { "project_id" : "proj_…" , "source_id" : "site_8232" , "deleted_at" : 1793438045 , "restorable_until" : 1796030045 } } { "type" : "webhook.test" , "timestamp" : "2026-10-31T09:14:05.000Z" , "data" : { "endpoint_id" : "whep_…" } } publish.failed : error is a short code, such as upload_expired , storage_cap_reached (see Limits ), store_failed , ingest_failed , bad_zip , too_large , or publish_failed . Treat any other code as a failure too. Start a new publish to recover. promote.done : deployment_id is the new production deployment, and from_deployment_id is the staging deployment it was made from. files is the number of files the production deployment serves. label is the staging deployment's label. rollback.done : deployment_id is live now, and previous_deployment_id was live before. env is production or staging . project.deleted : deleted_at and restorable_until are Unix seconds. It is sent once per delete. label on publish.ready and promote.done is the name the deployment was published with, or null . url can be null when the address couldn't be read at that moment. Verify the Signature Requests follow Standard Webhooks , so any Standard Webhooks library verifies them. Verify against the raw request body, before parsing it. Node (Express) Python (Flask) import express from 'express' import { Webhook } from 'standardwebhooks' const wh = new Webhook (process. env . MANIFEST_WEBHOOK_SECRET ) const app = express () app. post ( '/hooks/manifest' , express. raw ({ type : 'application/json' }), ( req, res ) => { let event try { event = wh. verify (req. body . toString ( 'utf8' ), req. headers ) } catch { return res. status ( 400 ). end () } if (event. type === 'publish.ready' ) { // event.data.url is live } res. status ( 204 ). end () }) import os from flask import Flask, request from standardwebhooks.webhooks import Webhook wh = Webhook(os.environ[ "MANIFEST_WEBHOOK_SECRET" ]) app = Flask(__name__) @app.post( "/hooks/manifest" ) def manifest_hook (): try : event = wh.verify(request.get_data(), dict (request.headers)) except Exception: return "" , 400 if event[ "type" ] == "publish.ready" : pass # event["data"]["url"] is live return "" , 204 The libraries also reject a timestamp more than five minutes from your clock, which stops replays. Each request carries three headers: Header Value webhook-id The message id. The same on every retry of the same event. webhook-timestamp Unix seconds when this attempt was sent. webhook-signature v1, and a base64 HMAC-SHA256 of webhook-id.webhook-timestamp.body , keyed with the base64-decoded part of the secret after whsec_ . Retries Answer with any 2xx within 10 seconds. Anything else, a timeout, or a redirect counts as a failure, and the event is sent again. Retries start after one minute, then wait twice as long each time (2, 4, 8 minutes and on), up to 6 hours apart. They stop 24 hours after the event. A retry has the same webhook-id and body, with a new timestamp and signature. Deduplicate on webhook-id . Delivery is at least once, so the same event can arrive twice. Answer first, then work. Queue the event and return 2xx straight away, so slow processing doesn't cause a retry. Don't rely on order. Events can arrive out of order. Compare timestamp , or read the current state from List Deployments . Delivery Health Each endpoint's delivery shows how sending to it is going. Field Meaning last_attempt_at Unix seconds of the last attempt. last_status Your HTTP status on that attempt, or null when there was none, such as a timeout or a connection error. last_error Why the last attempt failed, such as HTTP 503 . null after a success. last_success_at Unix seconds of the last 2xx . consecutive_failures Failed attempts in a row since the last success. failing_since Unix seconds of the first of those failures. null while healthy. pending Events not yet delivered and still being retried. dead Events given up on in the last 30 days: retried for 24 hours without a 2xx , or still waiting when the endpoint was disabled. Disabled Endpoints An endpoint is disabled once it has failed at least 10 attempts in a row and the first of those failures is 3 or more days old. status becomes disabled , with disabled_at and "disabled_reason": "failing" . A disabled endpoint receives nothing, and a test answers 409 endpoint_disabled . To recover, fix your receiver, delete the disabled endpoint, then create a new one. A disabled endpoint still counts toward the cap. The count resets on a single success, and after more than 24 hours with no attempts. A short outage or a quiet spell doesn't disable an endpoint. Errors Every error has the same shape . These are the ones specific to webhook endpoints. Status error Meaning 400 invalid_input On create: the body isn't {"url", "events"?} , events is empty or names an unknown event, or a field is unknown. 400 invalid_url On create: the URL isn't a public https address on the default port. The message says why. 404 not_found No endpoint with that id in this account. 409 webhook_limit On create: the account has its 3 endpoints on the free allowance, or 10 on Enterprise, counting disabled ones. Delete one first. 409 endpoint_disabled On a test: the endpoint is disabled. Create a new one. 503 webhooks_unavailable Webhooks are briefly unavailable. Retry later. Idempotency errors are on Errors .


## Usage — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/api/guides/usage

Usage See what your API account used in a month, per project. Get a Usage Report Use it for your own reporting or billing, or to check what Manifest counts. cURL JavaScript curl "https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/usage?period=2026-09" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " const res = await fetch ( 'https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/usage?period=2026-09' , { headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` }, }) Field Type Required Notes period string yes A calendar month in UTC, as YYYY-MM , such as 2026-09 . { "period" : "2026-09" , "starts_at" : 1788220800 , "ends_at" : 1790812800 , "complete" : true , "projects" : [ { "id" : "proj_…" , "source_id" : "site_8231" , "name" : "Acme Docs" , "created_at" : 1789210805 , "deleted_at" : null , "active" : true , "publishes" : 3 , "domains_attached" : 1 , "domains_removed" : 0 } ] , "totals" : { "active_projects" : 1 , "publishes" : 3 , "domains_attached" : 1 , "domains_removed" : 0 } , "request_id" : "…" } The report lists every project your API account created that existed at any time in the month. Projects you were only invited to aren't included. Fields Field Meaning starts_at , ends_at The month's bounds in Unix seconds: its first second, and the first second of the next month. complete false while the month is still running, so its numbers can still grow. active Created before the month ended, and not deleted before it began. Every listed project is active, including one deleted during the month. publishes Deployments that went live in the month, on staging or production. Each zip, file update , and content request counts once. Promotes and rollbacks don't. domains_attached Custom domains newly added in the month. Updating one doesn't count again. domains_removed Custom domains removed in the month. Domains released by deleting their project aren't counted. totals active_projects is the number of listed projects. The other totals add up the rows. A period that is missing or isn't YYYY-MM answers 400 invalid_input . CSV Send Accept: text/csv for the same report as a spreadsheet file. cURL JavaScript curl "https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/usage?period=2026-09" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " \ -H "Accept: text/csv" \ -o manifest-usage-2026-09.csv const res = await fetch ( 'https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/usage?period=2026-09' , { headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` , Accept : 'text/csv' , }, }) const csv = await res. text () period,project_id,source_id,name,created_at,deleted_at,active,publishes,domains_attached,domains_removed 2026-09,proj_…,site_8231,Acme Docs,2026-09-12T11:00:05.000Z,,1,3,1,0 2026-09,,,Total,,,1,3,1,0 There's one row per project, then a Total row. Times are ISO 8601 in UTC, and active is 1 . A text cell starting with = , + , - , @ , a tab, or a carriage return gets a leading ' . That way spreadsheet apps show it as text instead of running it as a formula. The JSON report always has the values unchanged.


# API docs / Reference


## Reference — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/api/reference

Article does not exist There is no documentation at this path.


## Authentication — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/api/reference/authentication

Authentication Send your API key with every request, and rotate it without downtime. Create an API Key Open the API page of the dashboard. It's also in the account menu, under API . New to Manifest? Signing in creates your free account. Select New key , name it after the service that will use it, like "CI" or "Docs sync", then select Create key . Copy the key and store it in your secrets manager. The key is shown once. If you lose it, revoke it and create another. Your first key also sets up your API account , which holds your keys, your project allowance, and your caps. Keys start with mnfst_api_ . An account can hold up to 10 live keys. Give each service its own, so you can revoke one without touching the others. Enterprise keys are issued by Manifest when the account is set up. Send the Key Send the key on every request as a bearer token, Authorization: Bearer <key> . GET /me checks that it works. cURL JavaScript curl https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/me \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " const res = await fetch ( 'https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/me' , { headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` }, }) const me = await res. json () { "account" : { "id" : "acct_…" , "name" : "Sam Rivera" , "plan" : "free" , "max_projects" : 2 , "max_storage_bytes" : 524288000 , "created_at" : 1760140800 } , "rate_limit" : { "requests_per_minute" : 60 , "writes_per_minute" : 30 } , "key" : { "prefix" : "mnfst_api_AbCd1234" } , "request_id" : "…" } plan is free for the allowance every account gets, or platform for an Enterprise account. max_projects is how many projects your keys can create through the API. max_storage_bytes and rate_limit are the account's other caps. See Limits . The examples name the key MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY , so it's never mixed up with a project's own MANIFEST_API_KEY . A key acts on every project it reaches. Call the API from your server only: browsers are refused (no CORS). Never put the key in code that runs in a browser, or in a repository. Project Keys Creating a project also returns that project's own key, project_key , once. It publishes that one project headless, for example from its CI with mnfst-publish . The API doesn't need it: your API key already reaches the project. See Create a Project . Revoke a Key On the API page , select the trash icon next to the key, then Revoke key . The key stops working on the next request and can't be restored. If a key leaks, revoke it and create a new one. Enterprise accounts revoke keys with the API . Manage Keys With the API A key can create, list, and revoke its own account's keys. This is how a server rotates its key without the dashboard. Create a Key With the API cURL JavaScript curl -X POST https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/keys \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "label": "CI 2026-11" }' const res = await fetch ( 'https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/keys' , { method : 'POST' , headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` , 'Content-Type' : 'application/json' , }, body : JSON . stringify ({ label : 'CI 2026-11' }), }) const { key } = await res. json () Field Type Required Notes label string no 1 to 60 characters. The answer is 201 Created , with the new key shown once: { "key" : "mnfst_api_…" , "prefix" : "mnfst_api_EfGh5678" , "label" : "CI 2026-11" , "created_at" : 1761868800 , "last_used_at" : null , "request_id" : "…" } Good to know: The 10-key cap counts dashboard keys too. Over it: 409 key_limit . An account can create 20 keys a day this way, revoked ones included. Over that: 429 mint_limit , with Retry-After . Idempotency-Key is ignored here, so a key is never stored or replayed. If a request times out, list the keys and revoke any you didn't receive. List Keys GET /keys lists the account's live keys, newest first. It shows each key's prefix, never the key itself. cURL JavaScript curl https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/keys \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " const res = await fetch ( 'https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/keys' , { headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` }, }) const { keys } = await res. json () { "keys" : [ { "prefix" : "mnfst_api_EfGh5678" , "label" : "CI 2026-11" , "created_at" : 1761868800 , "last_used_at" : null , "current" : false } , { "prefix" : "mnfst_api_AbCd1234" , "label" : "CI" , "created_at" : 1760140800 , "last_used_at" : 1761868740 , "current" : true } ] , "request_id" : "…" } current marks the key that made the request. last_used_at is accurate to the minute. Revoke a Key With the API cURL JavaScript curl -X DELETE https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/keys/mnfst_api_AbCd1234 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " await fetch ( 'https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/keys/mnfst_api_AbCd1234' , { method : 'DELETE' , headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` }, }) { "revoked" : "mnfst_api_AbCd1234" , "request_id" : "…" } The key stops working on the next request, and a key can revoke itself. The account's last live key can't be revoked with the API ( 409 last_key ), so there's always a working key. Create another key first. Rotate a Key Create a new key with the old one. Deploy the new key to every service that uses the old one. Check that last_used_at on the old key stops moving. Revoke the old key. Both keys work until step 4. They share one request limit, so extra keys never add capacity. See Limits . Errors Every error has the same shape . Status error Meaning 400 invalid_input POST /keys : label isn't a string of 1 to 60 characters. 401 unauthorized The key is missing, malformed, or not recognised. 401 key_revoked The key was revoked. If the account has no live keys left, create one on the dashboard, or contact Manifest for an Enterprise account. 404 not_found DELETE /keys/:prefix : no live key with that prefix in this account. 409 key_limit POST /keys : the account already has 10 live keys. 409 last_key DELETE /keys/:prefix : that's the account's only live key. 429 mint_limit POST /keys : 20 keys created in the last 24 hours. Wait the seconds in Retry-After . 429 rate_limited Too many requests or writes from this account. Wait the seconds in Retry-After . The message on a 401 says which key problem it is.


## Endpoints — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/api/reference/endpoints

Endpoints Every endpoint on one page, each linked to its guide. All Endpoints Paths are relative to https://api.manifestx.dev/v1 , and need your API key . The upload and status URLs are the exception: their token is the authority. Every POST , PATCH , and DELETE accepts an Idempotency-Key , except POST /keys . Pro marks endpoints that need a Pro project. Method Path What it does Account & keys GET /me The API account the key belongs to POST /keys Create another key, shown once GET /keys List live keys, with when each was last used DELETE /keys/:prefix Revoke a key, never the last one Projects POST /projects Create a project, safe to repeat on source_id GET /projects List projects, or find one with ?source_id= GET /projects/:id One project, with its URLs and publish state PATCH /projects/:id Rename a project DELETE /projects/:id Delete a project, restorable for 30 days Editors POST /projects/:id/invites Invite an editor by email . Pro GET /projects/:id/members List who has access DELETE /projects/:id/members/:user_id Remove an editor Content POST /projects/:id/content Build a docs site from Markdown pages Publish & files POST /projects/:id/publish Start a publish and get a one-time upload URL POST /uploads/:token Upload the zip to upload_url GET /uploads/:token/status Check an upload at status_url GET /projects/:id/files List the files of the live deployment GET /projects/:id/files/:path Read one file PATCH /projects/:id/files Update individual files on staging Deployments POST /projects/:id/promote Ship what's live on staging, or a named staging deployment, to production POST /projects/:id/rollback Go back to an earlier deployment . Pro GET /projects/:id/deployments List an environment's recent deployments Domains POST /projects/:id/domains Add a custom domain and get its DNS records GET /projects/:id/domains/:hostname Check a domain and its certificate DELETE /projects/:id/domains/:hostname Remove a custom domain Usage GET /usage?period=YYYY-MM Per-project usage for a month, as JSON or CSV Webhooks POST /webhooks Add a webhook endpoint, with its secret shown once GET /webhooks List webhook endpoints, with delivery health GET /webhooks/:id One webhook endpoint DELETE /webhooks/:id Remove a webhook endpoint POST /webhooks/:id/test Send a signed test event to one endpoint


## Errors — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/api/reference/errors

Errors What an error looks like, what each code means, and how to retry safely. Error Shape Every error has the same shape. message is written for a person, so branch on error instead. { "error" : "unauthorized" , "message" : "That API key is not recognised." , "request_id" : "…" } Quote the request_id when you contact Manifest . Some errors add a property: field names the input at fault, such as "articles[1].slug" or "files[0].path" . live_deployment_id comes with base_mismatch , so you can reapply your change on it. Upload and status URL errors carry error and message , but no request_id . Any path outside /v1/* answers 404 not_found with "No such API route." A rare unexpected failure can answer 500 without a JSON body. Retry it like any 5xx. Common Problems Symptom Likely cause Fix 401 unauthorized on every request The header isn't Authorization: Bearer mnfst_api_… , or it sends a project key ( mfst_… ) instead. Send an API key from the dashboard's API page . A browser fetch fails with a CORS error The API refuses browsers. Call it from your server. 404 not_found for a project in your dashboard The path is missing /v1 , the id is wrong, or the project belongs to another account. Check the URL, and the id from GET /projects . 403 forbidden on a team project You're a member of it, not its owner or an admin. Ask the owner for the admin role. 409 subdomain_taken on create Another project, perhaps someone else's, has that subdomain. Pick another, or leave subdomain out. 409 source_id_conflict on create The project exists under that source_id with another name. Look it up instead of creating it. 403 project_cap_reached The free allowance's two projects are in use. Delete a test project, or talk to us about Enterprise. 402 pro_required Rollback and inviting editors are part of Pro. Upgrade the project in the dashboard. On Free, publish the earlier version again . An address says "This site hasn't been published yet." Nothing is live on that environment. Publish to staging, then promote . Production doesn't show your change Updates land on staging. Check staging, then promote. An old version still shows The browser kept the page. Reload. Pages are cached for up to a minute. "No Manifest site is configured for this address." The custom domain isn't active, was removed, or its project was deleted. Check the domain's status . An upload's status stays ingesting Each poll moves the publish forward. Keep polling status_url until done or error . 429 A rate or daily limit is reached. Wait the seconds in Retry-After . See Limits . Error Codes Status error What to do 400 invalid_input A field is missing, malformed or unknown, env is wrong, or the body isn't JSON. Fix the request. 400 invalid_idempotency_key Idempotency-Key is blank or over 200 characters. 400 invalid_subdomain Use lowercase letters, digits, and single hyphens, 1 to 40 characters. 400 invalid_url A webhook URL isn't a public https address on the default port. The message says why. 400 invalid_hostname The hostname has spaces, no dot, or is an IP address. 400 invalid_cursor The file list cursor isn't valid, or its deployment is gone. List again without it. 400 invalid_path A file read's path doesn't name a file, for example it ends in / or contains .. . 400 staging_only File updates go to staging only. Update staging, then promote. 400 empty_upload The upload had no body. Start a new publish. 400 store_failed The zip couldn't be stored. Start a new publish. 400 retry_upload On the status URL: the upload was lost before it was stored. Send the same zip to the same upload URL. 401 unauthorized The key is missing, malformed, unknown, or not an API key. Check it. 401 key_revoked The key was revoked, and stays revoked. Use a current key. 402 pro_required Rollback and inviting editors are part of Pro. Upgrade the project in the dashboard, then retry. 403 forbidden You're a member of the project, not its owner or an admin. Deleting a project made outside the API needs its owner. 403 plan_required The project's plan doesn't include this, such as publishing to that environment, promote, file reads, deployment history, or custom domains. Every current plan includes these, so contact Manifest with the request_id . 403 project_cap_reached Your account's project cap is reached. The message names it. See Limits . 403 domain_cap_reached The project has 25 custom domains. Remove one first. 403 storage_cap_reached The publish would take the account over its storage cap. Nothing changed. See Limits . 403 owner_not_removable The project owner can't be removed. 404 not_found No such project, domain, key, or webhook endpoint, or the key can't reach it. Also any unknown route. 404 member_not_found No one with that user_id is on the project. 404 unknown_deployment That deployment_id isn't one of this project's deployments for that environment. On promote, it isn't one of this project's deployments at all. 404 file_not_found A file read names a file that isn't live, or nothing is live on that environment yet. 404 unknown_token On the status URL: the link expired or doesn't exist. Start a new publish. 409 source_id_conflict That source_id already names a project with a different name or subdomain . 409 source_id_deleted That source_id belonged to a deleted project. Use a new one. 409 subdomain_taken Another project has that subdomain. Pick another. 409 subscription_active The project has a Pro subscription. Cancel it in the dashboard, then delete. 409 hostname_taken Another project has that hostname. 409 key_limit The account has 10 live keys. Revoke one first. 409 webhook_limit The account has its 3 webhook endpoints on the free allowance, or 10 on Enterprise, counting disabled ones. Delete one first. 409 endpoint_disabled A test was sent to a disabled webhook endpoint. Create a new one. See Webhooks . 409 last_key That's the account's only live key. Create another before revoking it. 409 nothing_on_staging Nothing is live on staging to promote. Publish to staging first. 409 no_earlier_version There's no earlier version to roll back to. 409 already_live That deployment is already live. 409 not_restorable That deployment is still uploading or failed. 409 base_mismatch Staging moved on from your base . Read the files again and reapply on live_deployment_id . 409 idempotency_in_progress The first request with this key is still running. Retry shortly. 409 ingest_in_progress An earlier upload to this URL is still processing. Poll the status URL. 409 promote_in_progress Another promote of this project is still running. Retry shortly. 409 not_staging Promote takes a staging deployment, and that deployment_id is a production one. To restore a production version, roll back . 409 not_ready That staging deployment is still uploading or failed, so it can't be promoted. Wait for its status to be done , or publish again. 409 live_moved Production isn't serving your expect_live deployment any more, so nothing was promoted. The message names what is live. Check deployments before retrying. 410 project_deleted The project was deleted. The message says until when Manifest can restore it. See Projects . 410 expired The upload URL expired or was already used. Start a new publish. 413 too_large The zip is over 80 MB, a file is over 25 MB, or the unzipped build is over 250 MB. 413 too_many_files The zip holds more than 10,000 files. 413 payload_too_large A content or file update body is over 12 MB. 413 file_too_large A file update's file is over 8 MB. Publish it in a zip. 413 deployment_too_large The updated project would pass 250 MB or 10,000 files. 422 invalid_content A content slug, size, theme value, or page field is invalid. field says which. 422 not_api_project Content only works on projects created through the API. Publish a zip instead. 422 invalid_path A file update path is unsafe, private, written by Manifest, compiled, or listed twice. field names it. 422 invalid_file A change needs exactly one of content , content_base64 , or delete , or its base64 is invalid. 422 file_not_found A delete names a file that isn't on staging. 422 no_index The update would leave the project without index.html . 422 hostname_reserved The hostname is on a Manifest domain, such as manifestx.ai . 422 subdomain_reserved That subdomain is reserved, such as login or billing . 422 idempotency_key_reused The key was already used for another body, endpoint, or project. Use a new key. 422 invite_failed Manifest's team service refused the address. The message says why. Fix it rather than retrying. 429 rate_limited Too many requests or writes. Wait the seconds in Retry-After . On the status URL there's no Retry-After : wait a minute. 429 mint_limit 20 keys were created in the last 24 hours. Wait the seconds in Retry-After . 429 invite_limit The project's 50 invites for today are used. Wait the seconds in Retry-After . 429 publish_limit_reached A Free project's daily publish limit is reached. Wait the seconds in Retry-After . 500 ingest_failed Content failed before going live, and what was live is unchanged. Retry. 500 update_failed A file update failed. The message says whether staging is unchanged, or to check deployments first. 502 domain_attach_failed The domain couldn't be added. Check the hostname, then retry. 503 update_timed_out Storing the files took too long, and staging is unchanged. Retry, or send fewer files. 503 promote_failed The promote couldn't finish, and production is unchanged. Retry shortly. 503 publish_unavailable A publish couldn't be started. Retry shortly. 503 template_unavailable The docs template couldn't be loaded. Retry shortly. 503 domain_status_unavailable The domain status couldn't be read just now. Retry shortly. 503 domains_unavailable Custom domains are briefly unavailable. Retry later. 503 membership_unverified Your role on a team project couldn't be checked. Nothing was done. Retry. 503 team_unavailable The project's team couldn't be reached. No one was invited or removed. Retry. 503 webhooks_unavailable Webhooks are briefly unavailable. Retry later. 503 idempotency_unavailable Idempotent requests are briefly unavailable. Retry later. Retrying without the header loses its duplicate protection. Retrying 400 and 422: fix the request. Sending it again unchanged gives the same answer. 409: retry the _in_progress codes shortly. The others need a change first. 429: wait the seconds in Retry-After , then retry. 5xx: retry with the same Idempotency-Key . Failures are never stored, so the retry runs again. Two 5xx codes need a check first. When update_failed says the update may or may not be live, check deployments . On 502 domain_attach_failed , check the hostname. Idempotency Send an Idempotency-Key header so a retried request never runs twice. cURL JavaScript curl -X POST https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/promote \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY " \ -H "Idempotency-Key: help-center-sync-0193-promote" const res = await fetch ( 'https://api.manifestx.dev/v1/projects/proj_…/promote' , { method : 'POST' , headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${process.env.MANIFEST_ACCOUNT_KEY} ` , 'Idempotency-Key' : 'help-center-sync-0193-promote' , }, }) Which requests. Every POST , PATCH , and DELETE accepts it, such as content, file updates, publish, promote, rollback, domains, and editors. It's ignored on GET . Creating a project needs no header. source_id is the key, so re-sending the same body returns the existing project with 200 . See Projects . Creating an API key ( POST /keys ) ignores the header, so a new key is never stored or replayed. The key itself is 1 to 200 characters, unique per operation, and scoped to your API account. Derive it from your own job id, such as help-center-sync-0193 , so a retry of the same job reuses it. Responses are kept for 24 hours. A key is bound to the method, the path (including the project id), and the body of its first request. JSON key order and whitespace don't change the match. Repeat with the same key Result Same request, first one finished The stored response, byte for byte, with an Idempotent-Replayed: true header. Nothing runs twice. Same request, first one still running 409 idempotency_in_progress . Retry shortly. Different body, endpoint, or project 422 idempotency_key_reused . Nothing runs. First one answered 402 , 403 , 409 , 429 , or 5xx Not stored, so the retry runs again. It succeeds once the plan, role, cap, conflict, or limit allows it. A replayed project create returns the original project_key , so a retry after a dropped response still gets it.


## Limits — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/api/reference/limits

Limits Every cap the API enforces, and what it answers when you reach one. Requests Limit Free allowance Enterprise Requests per minute 60 600 Writes per minute 30 120 API keys created with POST /keys 20 a day 20 a day Editor invites per project 50 a day (UTC) 50 a day (UTC) Per account. Request and write limits count all the account's keys together, so extra keys add no capacity. A burst up to the limit at once is fine. Writes are POST , PATCH , and DELETE . Reads and revoking a key don't count. Your cap is rate_limit.writes_per_minute on GET /me . Free projects can publish 30 times a day, counting publishes from Claude and file updates. Pro projects, and projects on an Enterprise account, have no daily publish limit. Over a limit , the answer is 429 with Retry-After : rate_limited , mint_limit , invite_limit , or publish_limit_reached . Repeat invites to an existing editor send at most one email every 10 minutes. Inside that window, the answer has "email_skipped": "recently_sent" . Account and Projects Limit Free allowance Enterprise Projects created through the API 2 Set per account Storage 500 MB 10 GB Live API keys 10 10 Custom domains per project 25 25 Webhook endpoints 3 10 Deployments kept per environment 5 plus the live one 5 plus the live one Projects. Your cap is max_projects on GET /me . Over it, a create answers 403 project_cap_reached . Storage is the total size of the live staging and production versions of the projects the account created. Your cap is max_storage_bytes on GET /me . Over the storage cap , a publish, content request, or file update answers 403 storage_cap_reached and changes nothing. Promotes and rollbacks are never refused. Webhook endpoints count disabled ones too. Over the cap, a create answers 409 webhook_limit . See Webhooks . Deployments. Production on a prerendered project keeps ten. Older deployments can't be rolled back to. To raise an Enterprise cap, talk to us . Sizes and Files These are the same on every plan. Limit Value Zip upload 80 MB zipped, 250 MB unzipped Files in a zip 10,000, each up to 25 MB Upload URL One upload, within 15 minutes Upload status reads 120 a minute per IP address File update request 12 MB body, 1,000 changes, each file up to 8 MB Project after a file update 250 MB and 10,000 files Content request body 12 MB. See Docs Template for per-page limits. File list page 1,000 files. Follow next_cursor for the rest. Idempotency-Key 1 to 200 characters, kept 24 hours Webhook delivery 10 seconds per attempt, retried for 24 hours. An endpoint that fails at least 10 attempts in a row over 3 days is disabled .

# Framework docs / Getting Started


## Getting Started — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/framework/getting-started

Article does not exist There is no documentation at this path.


## Introduction — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/framework/getting-started/introduction

Introduction A website and app framework built directly into HTML. No bundler, no build step, no boilerplate. What is the Manifest framework? The Manifest framework lets you build complete websites and apps — from marketing pages to enterprise platforms — in plain HTML enhanced with a small set of attributes. Drop in two lines and you're set: <head> < script src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mnfst@latest/lib/manifest.min.js" data-tailwind > </ script > < link rel = "stylesheet" href = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mnfst@latest/lib/manifest.min.css" > That's the whole install. No compile step, no node_modules , no dev server required. Manifest pairs with — or replaces — frameworks like React, Vue, and HTMX. It's built for developers, designers who code, and AI coding assistants that want a modern web stack without complex tooling. Why Manifest? HTML is read more times each day than any human language is spoken — and written by machines at staggering scale. Yet after 30+ years of evolution, it still lacks native support for much of what modern websites and apps demand, forcing developers to patch it with layers of frameworks that ultimately compile back into HTML. Manifest brings the developer experience home to HTML , making modern web development faster, lighter, and more enjoyable — without sacrificing flexibility or power. Its design philosophies: Plug and play, no mandatory build steps. Style and function with less code. No performance sacrifice. Use only what you need. Develop with less noise and complexity. What's Included Pure HTML. A script tag and a stylesheet — that's the install. Universal data. One reactive syntax for files, APIs, and cloud databases. HTML components. Reusable files with route bindings on any element. Style system. Theme variables, utility classes, dark mode, and a CSS reset. Translation-ready. Locale-keyed strings, right-to-left support. SEO & AI-ready. One command renders a site optimized for search engines and LLM crawlers. Accessibility, forms, dropdowns, toasts, tooltips, 200,000+ icons — and plenty more, all included, none required. Manifest went public in 2026. Ideas, bug reports, and pull requests are welcome on GitHub . Full credits live in the Acknowledgements article.


## Setup — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/framework/getting-started/setup

Setup Get Manifest with CDN links or copied from GitHub . Overview Manifest consists of: manifest.js script for your project's functionality. manifest.json for central management of your project. manifest.*.css stylesheets for your project's UX/UI. These files are modular, designed to work alone or together to best suit your project. A project using all Manifest features would be set up like: <head> <!-- Meta --> < link rel = "manifest" href = "/manifest.json" > <!-- Scripts --> < script src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mnfst@latest/lib/manifest.min.js" data-tailwind > </ script > <!-- Styles --> < link rel = "stylesheet" href = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mnfst@latest/lib/manifest.min.css" > < link rel = "stylesheet" href = "/manifest.theme.css" > manifest.json Outside this framework, manifest.json is a common file for web applications to centrally store project-level metadata. It's stored in the root for automatic browser detection. We leverage this file as a place to declare HTML components and local or cloud data sources. It can also be used as a data source itself to render content. Web-standard fields come first, followed by the declarations Manifest's modules read — components , preloadedComponents , and data : manifest.json { "$schema" : "https://manifestx.dev/manifest.schema.json" , "name" : "My Project" , "short_name" : "Project name" , "description" : "A short description of your project." , "start_url" : "/" , "scope" : "/" , "display" : "standalone" , "orientation" : "any" , "background_color" : "#FFFFFF" , "icons" : [ { "src" : "/assets/icons/192x192.png" , "sizes" : "192x192" , "type" : "image/png" } , { "src" : "/assets/icons/512x512.png" , "sizes" : "512x512" , "type" : "image/png" } ] , "components" : [ "components/home.html" , "components/about.html" ] , "preloadedComponents" : [ "components/footer.html" , "components/header.html" , "components/logo.html" ] , "data" : { "content" : { "locales" : "/locales.csv" } } } +19 An optional version field acts as a release stamp that busts component caches on deploy — see browser caching . Projects published through Manifest are stamped automatically. If your project is not a downloadable web app, and does not include HTML components or data sources, manifest.json can be omitted. Script manifest.js dynamically loads Alpine JS and our modules to make your project functional. Add the <script> tag anywhere in the HTML head or body (within index.html if routing ). All Modules (default) Select Modules Omit Modules Include Tailwind CSS < script src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mnfst@latest/lib/manifest.min.js" > </ script > <!-- Load only specified modules --> < script src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mnfst@latest/lib/manifest.min.js" data-modules = "components,router,utilities" > </ script > <!-- Load all core modules except omitted ones --> < script src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mnfst@latest/lib/manifest.min.js" data-omit = "markdown,charts" > </ script > <!-- Include Tailwind CSS --> < script src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mnfst@latest/lib/manifest.min.js" data-tailwind > </ script > The script loads: Manifest Modules (latest versions) from our CDN. The optional data-modules or data-omit attributes will include or omit comma-separated modules. Prefix a name with + to add it on top of the defaults ( data-modules="+chat" ) instead of replacing them. See Reference for every loader attribute. Without these attributes, most core modules load by default, and the rest load when needed: Data, localization, components, status, payments, chat, device and the Appwrite modules load when manifest.json configures them. Rich text, submissions, chat, presence and device also load when the page uses them (for example x-submit or $chat ). Edit never loads by itself. Add it with data-modules . Alpine JS v3 (the version tested with the framework release) from CDN, unless it's been added separately to your project. Override it with data-alpine (an Alpine version, a full URL, or a path starting with / ). Tailwind CSS (modified production version from our CDN) if the data-tailwind attribute is added. Manifest scripts load the latest version from CDN by default. Load a specified version by referencing it in the URL and with a data-version attribute for modules: < script src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mnfst@<version>/lib/manifest.min.js" data-version = "<version>" > </ script > To have the browser check the loader and everything it loads against published hashes, see Security . Your own scripts can be native modules ( <script type="module"> ), with an import map for short import paths. Manifest starts Alpine after the module scripts in index.html run, so components and stores they register in an alpine:init listener are always in time. See Large Apps . Styles Stylesheets are divided by UI category, available individually or bundled in manifest.css . A separate manifest.theme.css can be downloaded from GitHub for local modification. It maintains CSS variables referenced by the other sheets if present, centralizing your project's visual identity. See theme for more. Add the desired Manifest CSS files to the HTML head (within index.html if routing ). Bundled (~22 kB gzipped) Individual < link rel = "stylesheet" href = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mnfst@latest/lib/manifest.min.css" > < link rel = "stylesheet" href = "/manifest.theme.css" > < link rel = "stylesheet" href = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mnfst@latest/lib/manifest.reset.css" > < link rel = "stylesheet" href = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mnfst@latest/lib/manifest.button.css" > < link rel = "stylesheet" href = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mnfst@latest/lib/manifest.utilities.css" > < link rel = "stylesheet" href = "/manifest.theme.css" > CLI Commands Manifest provides a handful of handy npx commands to assist with project development: Command Purpose Reference npx mnfst-starter <name> Scaffold a new Manifest project Starter Project npx mnfst-starter --here Scaffold into the current folder; add --name "<name>" to set the project name, --force to overwrite template files Starter Project npx mnfst-run Zero-dependency dev server with live reload Setup npx mnfst-render Prerender the SPA into a static MPA Websites npx mnfst-export Batch / CI exports — PDF, image, CSV, JSON, RSS Export npx mnfst-types Generate TypeScript ambient types from manifest.json TypeScript npx mnfst-test Project linter + component-test harness Testing Run a Project Enter npx mnfst-run to fire up a local server of the project. Sub-directories can be targeted with a path like npx mnfst-run website for /website . npx mnfst-run The server provides the following conveniences: Auto launch — launches a new browser tab when started. Auto reload — refreshes when content edits are made to html , css , json , yaml , csv , or md files. Auto close — kills the server instance if all its browser tabs are closed. No duplication — on launch, provides an existing localhost URL if the project is already running on the device. Option Description --port <n> , -p <n> Preferred port (default 5001 , or the PORT environment variable); moves up if taken --no-open Don't open a browser tab on start --idle-shutdown <s> Seconds to wait after the last tab closes before exiting (default 30 ) --no-idle-shutdown Keep running when no tabs are open --list , -l List the servers running on this device


## Starter Project — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/framework/getting-started/starter-project

Starter Project Kickstart new websites and apps with a turnkey template. Install Install the starter project locally with the npx command: New Folder Current Folder npx mnfst-starter Name npx mnfst-starter --here npx mnfst-starter Name creates a Name/ folder and sets it as the project name in manifest.json . It stops if that folder already exists. npx mnfst-starter --here installs into the current folder instead, using the folder's name as the project name. Add --name to either command to set a different project name: New Folder Current Folder npx mnfst-starter my-site --name "My Site" npx mnfst-starter --here --name "My Site" A folder name given to npx mnfst-starter Name may contain ASCII letters, numbers, spaces, dots, underscores, and hyphens, and can't start or end with a dot or space or contain two dots in a row. The --name value can be any text, so use it for names with other characters. The starter stops with an error on an option it doesn't recognise, such as a misspelt --frce , or on an empty value like --name= . Run npx mnfst-starter --help to list the options. Alternatively, download the template directory from GitHub . Existing Files --here never overwrites files. If any template file already exists in the folder, nothing is written and the conflicts are listed: Error : these files already exist in this folder and would be overwritten : index. html manifest. json README . md Move them aside, or re-run with --force to overwrite them. Move those files aside, or add --force to replace them with the template versions. Other files are never touched, apart from the config merges below. npx mnfst-starter --here --force --force lists every file it overwrote. It keeps the project name already in manifest.json unless --name is also given; everything else in manifest.json is replaced by the template. If the existing manifest.json can't be read, the starter warns and uses the folder name instead. Outside --here , --force has no effect and the starter prints a warning; likewise a folder name passed alongside --here is ignored with a warning. Merged Config Some files are merged with what's already in the folder rather than replaced, even with --force : .gitignore keeps its existing rules. Any missing starter entries (such as .env ) are appended under # Added by Manifest . .mcp.json keeps its other servers. Only the manifest server entry is added or updated. .claude/settings.json keeps its settings. mcp__manifest is added to permissions.allow . .env keeps its other variables. Only MANIFEST_API_KEY is added or updated. The last three apply only to key-authenticated (headless) setups, where Manifest passes --project-id and --key for you. Setups through the Manifest connector or plugin pass neither, so the starter writes no .mcp.json , .claude/settings.json or .env : the connector already provides the Manifest server. If .mcp.json or .claude/settings.json isn't valid JSON, the starter stops before writing anything. Run From Root From Subdirectory npx mnfst-run npx mnfst-run path Run this project locally from the project root with npx mnfst-run , or any subdirectory with npx mnfst-run path , where "path" is the folder path. Alternatively, most local server solutions can run Manifest projects. See websites for deploying live to production. Capabilities The project is provided with ready-made content for: Routing (page-level views & 404 content) Header, footer, and logo components Responsive layout with mobile sidebar Color modes Localization (English, Spanish, Arabic, and Chinese examples) Markdown article injection Files & Folders The project begins with this folder structure for both development and deployment: Project Name/ ├── assets/ # Visual files │ ├── fonts/ # Web fonts │ │ └── Inter.woff2 │ └── icons/ # Web app icons │ ├── 192 x192.png │ └── 512 x512.png ├── components/ # HTML components │ ├── header.html │ ├── footer.html │ └── logo.html ├── .gitignore # Files Git should skip ├── _redirects # SPA routing support for modern static hosts ├── favicon.ico # Browser tab icon ├── index.html # Rendering entry point / main page ├── LICENSE.md # MIT License ├── locales.csv # Translated content in English, Spanish, Arabic, and Chinese ├── manifest.json # Project & web app manifest ├── manifest.theme.css # Project theme variables ├── privacy.md # Privacy policy template, required by most sites & apps └── README.md # Project README The only mandatory file required is index.html . All other files and folders are provided for template purposes. index.html This main HTML file serves as the router's single-page application (SPA) entry point. It includes: Head tags for Manifest framework loading (from CDN), SEO, and web app configuration. Component placeholders ( <x-header> , <x-footer> ) of HTML templates . Routing views ( x-route="..." ) for URL-specific content . Dynamic references ( x-text="$x.content.page1" ) to localized data source values. manifest.json This web application manifest allows browsers to identify and export the website as an app to mobile and desktop devices. As a progressive web app (PWA), your project is often more portable, scalable, and popular than traditional native apps, and can be packaged for app store distribution. This project also uses the manifest to register its components and localized content, and to define author and email fields referenced by the Privacy Policy.


## Compatibility — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/framework/getting-started/compatibility

Compatibility Designed to work in all major browsers. Frameworks The latest version of Manifest is designed to be used with: Alpine JS v3 and above Tailwind CSS v4 and above Depending on scope, Manifest's modular scripts and stylesheets can be dropped into projects running on other frameworks, e.g. just to apply icons, color modes, or theme styles. Browsers The latest version of Manifest is designed for and tested on the current stable versions of Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and Safari. Manifest only uses native language features that have been declared web-standard, but older browser versions may lack some of the newer CSS ones it uses: anchor positioning ( anchor-name , position-area ) for dropdowns, tooltips and pickers; customizable selects ( appearance: base-select ); field-sizing ; and @starting-style entry animations. Check Can I Use? for specific browser feature support.


## Accessibility — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/framework/getting-started/accessibility

Accessibility Allow your project to support all audiences. Overview Manifest is accessible by default. Its reset stylesheet, semantic element styles, and interactive modules all align with WCAG 2.1 Level AA . Keyboard navigation, focus management, ARIA attributes, and live-region announcements are handled automatically. All code snippets in these docs are intended to be semantically correct for screen readers and SEO crawlers. Built-in Support Focus states provide visible focus indicators for keyboard navigation. Form elements are accessible controls with proper labeling support. Semantic HTML styles preserve the semantic meaning of HTML elements. Text scaling uses font sizes and line heights optimized for readability. Reduced motion includes support for the prefers-reduced-motion media query. ARIA styles are provided for common ARIA attributes. Elements Manifest's advanced elements, including those supported by module scripts, implement the relevant WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices patterns. No setup is required beyond using them as documented: Element Accessibility Accordions Native <details> / <summary> — focusable, Enter / Space to toggle, aria-expanded implicit Color Pickers Keyboard-navigable swatches and inputs with labeled controls Dialogs Native <dialog> / popover API — focus trap, Escape to close, return focus on close, role="dialog" and aria-modal implicit Dropdowns aria-haspopup="menu" , reactive aria-expanded , aria-controls , role="menu" / "menuitem" , arrow navigation, Escape to close with focus return to trigger, roving tabindex Forms Native HTML5 validation, error states, and semantic labeling Sidebars Native popover dismissal with Escape Tabs With a role="tablist" wrapper: role="tab" / "tabpanel" , reactive aria-selected , aria-controls , aria-labelledby , roving tabindex , Left / Right / Up / Down / Home / End arrow navigation Toasts role="status" + aria-live="polite" for confirmations; role="alert" for negative / destructive types Tooltips role="tooltip" , aria-describedby linking the trigger to the tooltip content, fires on hover and keyboard focus (WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.13) Motion Manifest's CSS animations and the View Transitions API respect prefers-reduced-motion automatically. Users with reduced-motion enabled see instant navigation instead of crossfade, and component animations resolve immediately rather than easing. WCAG 2.1 Coverage Manifest's defaults align with WCAG 2.1 Level AA criteria: Criterion Covered by 1.4.4 — Resize Text Text-scaling reset styles 1.4.13 — Content on Hover or Focus Tooltips fire on focus, not hover-only 2.1.1 — Keyboard Tabs, dropdowns, dialogs, accordions are fully keyboard-operable 2.3.3 — Animation from Interactions prefers-reduced-motion honored across reset CSS and view transitions 2.4.7 — Focus Visible Focus indicators on all interactive elements 4.1.2 — Name, Role, Value ARIA roles wired on tabs, menus, tooltips, dialogs, toasts 4.1.3 — Status Messages Toasts route through role="status" / role="alert" per type Authors retain responsibility for content-level criteria like heading hierarchy, image alt text, link discernibility, custom theme contrast ratios, and form label association. Automated Testing Run Manifest's project linter to catch accessibility violations alongside other regressions: npx mnfst-test The runtime pass injects axe-core against a headless render of your project and reports each failure with severity, the offending element, and (for color-contrast issues) the theme CSS variable driving the bad color. See testing for full details. Manual Checklist Automated tools catch about a third of accessibility issues. Always test your applications against the rest: Keyboard navigation (Tab, Enter, Space, arrow keys) Focus indicators visible throughout Color contrast ratios pass at WCAG 2.1 AA Screen readers usable (VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS) Form controls have proper labels Text remains readable when zoomed to 200% Reduced-motion preferences honored in custom CSS Heading hierarchy and document outline coherent Interactive elements have sufficient touch targets (44×44 px) Different input methods (mouse, keyboard, touch, voice)


## Performance — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/framework/getting-started/performance

Performance What Manifest optimizes, what to reach for, and how to measure. Overview Most of Manifest's performance work is automatic. Closed containers cost nothing, data updates touch only what changed, and text is never rewritten when it hasn't changed. Each element's own article says how it behaves. This guide explains the mechanics behind those defaults, the few knobs that adjust them, and the checks to run when a page is slow. What Is Automatic Closed containers cost nothing. A closed menu, a closed dialog, a collapsed <details> , a hidden element and a tab panel that isn't selected are left alone until they are shown; nothing inside them runs. Their full markup is still in the prerendered HTML, so search engines and readers without JavaScript see everything. Once shown, they stay ready. Data updates touch only what changed. Each part of the page that reads a data source follows just that source. When new data arrives, existing rows are updated in place rather than replaced, so lists don't flicker and edits in progress are not disturbed. Your own changes show immediately, and network updates arriving together are applied in one go. $x.all , which combines every source, is only built when something reads it. See how data updates . Text only updates when it changes. A text binding whose value comes back unchanged leaves the page alone, and empty values ( null or undefined ) show as empty text rather than the word "null". Searches and filters on data are cached. $search , $query and $route remember their result until the source they read changes, so binding the same search in fifty rows costs one pass, not fifty. Your own derivations get the same treatment with x-computed . Repeat visits load from the browser. Sites on Manifest hosting register a small service worker that keeps the page shell, scripts, styles and components on the visitor's device. The first visit loads from the network as usual; from the next visit on, the shell comes from the device and only the data is fetched, and a page that was already open keeps working offline. Publishing still takes effect on the next load, because the page itself is always checked against the network first. Local previews with mnfst-run never register it. To turn it off for a site, set "sw": false in manifest.json , or add data-sw="off" to the loader <script> . None of this needs an attribute or a setting. The one switch is data-defer="off" on the loader script, which turns closed-container deferral off for the whole page; x-defer.off does the same for a single element. Utility Classes Publishing bakes a stylesheet of every Tailwind-style utility class your pages use ( flex , gap-4 , hover:underline , bg-brand-surface , and their variants) instead of shipping an engine that scans the page and generates them live. When that baked sheet covers every class on a page, the live engine never loads at all — one less script, sooner interactivity. Classes a scan can't see. A class assigned only from a runtime value — :class="ok ? 'bg-green-500' : 'bg-amber-500'" — may not appear anywhere the publish-time scan looks. List it under utilities.safelist in manifest.json so it's baked in like any other class: manifest.json "utilities" : { "safelist" : [ "bg-amber-500" , "bg-green-500" ] } For a whole family built at runtime, utilities.patterns takes regular expressions matched against each class token instead. These aren't baked — a pattern can't be expanded into concrete classes — but the runtime treats a match as already covered rather than flagging it: manifest.json "utilities" : { "patterns" : [ "^bg-(red|green|blue)-[0-9]+$" ] } If a class still turns up uncovered on a live page, Manifest loads the full engine automatically and logs a warning — a page never renders unstyled without saying so. What To Reach For Situation Use A list, table or total built from data x-computed — a named value recalculated only when its inputs change Any list over ~100 rows, especially inside a menu x-virtual — renders only the visible rows The one or two menus people open most x-defer.priority="1" — warmed first, so they open instantly (see dropdowns ) x-defer Reference Closed containers are deferred without any attribute. x-defer is for the cases where you want to change that, like warming a container early, discarding its contents on close, or keeping it eager. Automatic Rule These containers are deferred automatically: [popover] elements (any value) Closed <dialog> Closed <details> [hidden] elements — except [x-route] panes, because inactive pages are handled by the router Tab panels that are not initially selected Containers with their own rendering directive are never deferred: x-html , x-text , x-virtual , x-colorpicker , x-date , x-rich-text , x-chart , x-icon , x-svg , x-code , x-markdown and the like. Empty containers are not deferred. Deferred contents are initialized on the container's own open signal: beforetoggle for popovers and dialogs, toggle for details, selection for tab panels, and removal of the hidden attribute. Once initialized they stay that way unless the container has x-defer.discard . $refs inside a deferred container resolve after its first open. Blocks toggled with x-show are not deferred automatically. Add x-defer to one explicitly to defer its contents until it is shown. Modifiers Modifier Effect x-defer.lazy No warming — contents render on open only x-defer.discard Throw the contents away when the container closes; they initialize again on the next open x-defer.priority="n" Warm this container before any container without a priority (lower n first). The modifier is part of the attribute name and the number is its value; x-defer="priority:1" does nothing x-defer.off Never defer this container Kill Switch Add data-defer="off" to the loader <script> to turn automatic deferral off for the whole page. < script src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mnfst@latest/lib/manifest.min.js" data-defer = "off" > </ script > Experimental — route-level deferral. Add data-defer-routes to the loader <script> to make inactive x-route pages inert until they are first shown. They render on activation, before the page is visible. This changes when code runs: with the flag on, an inactive page's x-init and data reads run when the page is first opened, not at load, and $refs or id s on another page resolve only after that page has been shown. Escape hatches: x-defer.off on a route, or data-defer="off" globally. How Warming Works After the page settles, idle time is used to warm the on-screen menus nearest the visitor's last click — a few at a time, and never more than the cap. Warmed menus open instantly; the rest render on open. x-defer.priority moves a container to the front of that queue, and x-defer.lazy keeps it out. Measuring Manifest uses shared definitions so numbers from different pages and teams compare: Blocked time — the sum of long tasks from a gesture to settle. Settle — 500ms with no DOM mutations in the target region. Mutation count — the number of DOM mutations in the target region. For teams that want a CI gate, the framework repo's scripts/perf/probe.mjs implements these definitions. Troubleshooting When your project is slow, work through this checklist: A closed menu with x-defer.off ? Remove it unless the contents must exist while closed. A big x-for without x-virtual ? Wrap it — see virtual . A getter that filters on every render? Make it a computed value . A ticker that rewrites text every second? Tick at the granularity you display. Popover opens paying page-wide layout? Add the contain: layout CSS property to large scrollers. Diagnostics For tooling and module authors: window.ManifestDefer.stats() returns { pending, warm, cap, ready, bootDrained, armed, observed, head, routes: { enabled, stashed, rendered } } . ManifestDeferConfig.prewarmCap sets how many containers warming may prepare (default 48 ). ManifestDeferConfig.routes = true is the script-side form of data-defer-routes . manifest:defer-render fires on a container after its contents initialize, for code that touches rendered children.


# Framework docs / Core Modules


## Core Modules — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/framework/core-modules

## Chat — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/framework/core-modules/chat

Chat Add conversations with AI or people to your project. Overview The chat module adds conversations to your project. A conversation is a reactive object: its messages, participants, and typing indicators update live, and you render them with your own markup. The same markup can power an AI assistant, a support box, a group thread, or a comment section. Adapters decide where messages live. Built-in adapters cover AI models, an Appwrite backend, and an in-browser demo — or you can register your own. A conversation with an AI works the same as one between people. The module renders nothing itself. See the chats element styles for ready-made conversation layouts. Each works without the other. Setup Chat is opt-in. It loads automatically when $chat appears in your page's markup, or when manifest.json contains an ai or chat entry (a config block, or "chat": true ). It can also be declared in data-modules , where the + prefix adds it alongside the default modules. Manifest Trigger (default) Declared <!-- Meta: manifest.json contains an "ai" or "chat" entry --> < link rel = "manifest" href = "/manifest.json" > <!-- Scripts --> < script src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mnfst@latest/lib/manifest.min.js" > </ script > <!-- Meta --> < link rel = "manifest" href = "/manifest.json" > <!-- Scripts: defaults plus chat --> < script src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mnfst@latest/lib/manifest.min.js" data-modules = "+chat" > </ script > Markup detection covers $chat written in the page itself. If your only usage lives inside a lazily loaded component , use one of the other two triggers. AI Chat Manifest supports turnkey AI integration using Anthropic's Claude, grounded in your own content. Published Manifest sites serve the AI relay on /_ai/chat themselves, so the API key never reaches the browser and there is no server to run. Setup takes four steps: Add an ai block to manifest.json . Give Manifest your Anthropic API key. Use the claude adapter in your chat markup. Publish. Configuration Register the model in manifest.json under an ai block: manifest.json { "ai" : { "provider" : "anthropic" , "model" : "claude-haiku-4-5" , "system" : "You are the support assistant for Universal Exports. Answer briefly." , "grounding" : "https://universalexports.com/llms.txt" } } Property Default Description provider "anthropic" The AI provider; more may be added in the future. model "claude-haiku-4-5" Any Claude model ID. Haiku is fast and inexpensive; larger models reason more deeply. system – Instructions that shape every reply, like the assistant's role, tone, and boundaries. grounding – An https URL or project file whose text is added to the instructions, so answers come from your content instead of the model's general knowledge. maxTokens 1024 The maximum length of a single reply, up to 4096 . The relay reads the ai block from your published manifest.json , so changes take effect when you publish. The model and instructions are always set here: a visitor's browser can't change them. A grounding URL is read once per published version and cached for up to a day. Publish again to pick up changes to it. Treat system and grounding as public. Anyone can open manifest.json , and a model can be talked into repeating its instructions, so never put secrets there. Long system and grounding text is sent as a cacheable prompt. After the first message, Anthropic serves it from cache at a fraction of the price. API Key Replies use your own Anthropic API key, so usage bills to your Anthropic account. AI chat is free on every Manifest plan. Give the key to Manifest through the connector by asking your agent, for example: "set up AI chat with my Anthropic key". Manifest stores it encrypted. Ask again to replace the key, change the daily request limit, or remove it. A project's staging and production sites share one key and one daily limit. The daily request limit is your cost ceiling. For a small site, ask for a lower limit than the default. Never put the key in manifest.json or a PUBLIC_ environment variable. Both are sent to every visitor's browser. For local work, npx mnfst-run serves the same /_ai/chat route using ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from the project's .env file. Without a key it streams mock replies, so you can build the interface first. The same markup works locally and once published. .env ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-your-key-here Limits Limit or error Response About 20 requests per minute per visitor 429 1000 requests per day per project, shared by staging and production (adjustable through the connector) 429 5 MB per request, including attachments 413 An attachment that isn't a JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP image or a PDF (SVG and other files aren't supported) 400 invalid_messages More than 100 messages of history Older messages are dropped automatically A request from another site 403 forbidden_origin No ai block in the published manifest.json 404 ai_not_enabled No API key set up 503 ai_not_configured Requests the relay rejects as invalid don't count toward the daily limit. The claude adapter shows the relay's error message in the conversation. Markup Open a conversation with $chat.open and render it. The call returns a reactive handle. Loop over its messages , bind a field to a draft, and call send . Three details complete the UI. Style your own messages by comparing each message's author to the handle's me . Render finished replies with the markdown module, and show plain text with x-text while a reply streams. When the text comes from participants you don't control, use x-markdown.safe to sanitize it.
