Right-clicking a piece opens your menu, and $edit.target is the piece you clicked, set before the menu opens; every $edit action uses it when called without an element. $edit.can(action) says whether an action applies to it, so a button bound to it disables itself. < ul x-edit.move = "toys" x-dropdown.context = "toy-menu" > < li > Ball </ li > < li x-edit.lock.remove > Rope (can't be deleted) </ li > < li > Squeaky duck </ li > </ ul > < menu popover id = "toy-menu" > < button @ click = "$edit.copy()" > Copy </ button > < button :disabled = "!$edit.can('cut')" @ click = "$edit.cut()" > Cut </ button > < button :disabled = "!$edit.can('paste')" @ click = "$edit.paste()" > Paste </ button > < button :disabled = "!$edit.can('duplicate')" @ click = "$edit.duplicate()" > Duplicate </ button > < button :disabled = "!$edit.can('remove')" @ click = "$edit.remove()" > Delete </ button > < hr > < button x-show = "$edit.can('remove')" @ click = "$edit.lock($edit.target, 'remove')" > Lock deleting </ button > < button x-show = "!$edit.can('remove')" @ click = "$edit.unlock($edit.target, 'remove')" > Unlock deleting </ button > </ menu > Right-click a toy, copy it, then right-click another and paste. Lock deleting on one and the Delete button disables itself for it. $edit.lock(el, action) and $edit.unlock(el, action) do at runtime what .lock does in markup, so the people using your editor can protect parts of a page from their own mistakes. Leave out the action to lock everything. A runtime lock is a step of the history, so it undoes, and .persist keeps it, but it's never written to your source: it belongs to the editing session, not the page. Unlocking also lifts a .lock written in the markup. $edit.can() answers for move , remove , duplicate , text , attrs , class , size , copy , cut , and paste , taking the region's capabilities and every lock into account. A component piece answers false for copy and cut . Other actions for menus and panels are in the reference : $edit.move() , nest() , and unnest() move a piece by script, and $edit.attr() and $edit.classes change attributes and classes as recorded edits. In Rich Text , block means a paragraph-level tag such as a heading or a list. Here it means any piece of the page. History Every edit on the page joins one history, shared by every region, in the order the edits were made. Cmd/Ctrl + Z undoes the last one and Shift + Cmd/Ctrl + Z (or Ctrl + Y ) redoes it, wherever you are on the page, except in form fields and in elements with their own x-rich-text , which keep their own undo. While you're in a piece of text, the shortcuts first step through what you've done in it since you clicked in, typing burst by typing burst, then through the page's history. Put data-edit-hotkeys="off" on a region, or on any element above it such as <html> , to leave the shortcuts to your own code. The browser's own undo can't do this: it only knows about typing in one field at a time, not about pieces moving, nesting, resizing, or closing. Visual Editing replaces it with one history of its own, so moves, nesting, resizes, closes, locks, and text edits all step back in the order they were made. There's no built-in toolbar. Build your own from buttons that call $edit.undo() , $edit.redo() , and $edit.publish() , and bind them to $edit.canUndo and $edit.canRedo so they disable themselves when there's nothing to step to. < div x-data = "{ sent: '', init() { this.$edit.onPublish = patches => this.sent = 'Published at ' + new Date().toLocaleTimeString() } }" > < div class = "row gap-1" > < button :disabled = "!$edit.canUndo" @ click = "$edit.undo()" aria-label = "Undo" > < span x-icon = "lucide:undo-2" > </ span > </ button > < button :disabled = "!$edit.canRedo" @ click = "$edit.redo()" aria-label = "Redo" > < span x-icon = "lucide:redo-2" > </ span > </ button > < button @ click = "$edit.publish()" > Publish </ button > < span x-text = "sent" > </ span > </ div > < ul x-edit.persist = "chores" > < li > Fill the water bowl </ li > < li > Buy kibble </ li > < li > Book the groomer </ li > </ ul > </ div > The undo and redo buttons step through the whole page's history, so they also undo edits made in the other examples on this page. Publish sends the edits and clears the history; here they only go to a handler that shows the time, see Publishing . What a Reload Keeps Edits live in memory, so a reload loses the ones not yet published. .persist keeps a region's unpublished edits, and their undo history, in this browser's localStorage , and replays them when the page loads again. Edit the list above, reload, and your changes are still there. A publish clears them. It's opt-in because the saved edits belong to one browser on one device, are invisible to everyone else, and go stale if the source changes underneath them; on a shared computer the next person would see them too. Use it for an editor where people work across reloads before they publish. .persist keeps text, order, nesting, sizes, attributes and classes, runtime locks, and a data list's order and record fields. Theme values are kept when .persist is on their control or their .theme scope. It doesn't keep closes, which are page state, or rows added, duplicated, or deleted in a data list. The history is one for the whole document, so in a single-page app it carries across routes, and it's saved under every path the page has shown, capped at the latest 400 steps. Theme Controls x-edit.cssvar binds an input to a CSS variable, so a control panel can restyle the page live. A bare variable name writes it on :root , for the whole page. A name with a scope: prefix writes it on the element that declares that scope with x-edit.theme , so it applies only inside that element. data-unit adds a unit to a number or range input's value. < div x-edit.theme = "card" style = "--color-brand-surface: #7c3aed; --color-brand-inverse: #ffffff; --radius: 0.5rem" > < button class = "brand" > Give Poochie a treat </ button > </ div > < label > Brand < input type = "color" x-edit.cssvar = "card:--color-brand-surface" > </ label > < label > Radius < input type = "range" min = "0" max = "2" step = "0.125" data-unit = "rem" x-edit.cssvar = "card:--radius" > </ label > The variable changes live as the input moves, and is recorded as a step of the history when the input commits its value: when you let go of a slider or close the colour picker, and at each arrow-key step on a focused slider. Undo puts the previous value back. .theme on its own only declares a scope and makes nothing editable, so it can wrap regions safely. .persist on the control, or on its scope element, keeps unpublished values across a reload. When published, a global value goes to the project's own manifest.theme.css , and a scoped value into the scope element's style attribute, so it never reaches :root . See Publishing for which file each is written to. Reference Modifiers Modifier On Effect (none) A region Text and move .text A region Text can be rewritten in place .move A region Pieces can be moved: reordered, nested, un-nested, between regions .size An element Resize handles on its edges and corners .data A region with an x-for list Record fields shown with x-text or x-html , in a row or as the row itself, can be edited .gated A region Off until $edit.on() .persist A region, a .cssvar control, or a .theme scope Unpublished edits survive a reload in this browser .bare A region No editing visuals; everything else works .lock An element in a region No edits to it or anything inside it .lock.move .lock.remove .lock.duplicate .lock.text .lock.attrs .lock.size An element in a region Blocks one action; combine as needed .grab An element inside a piece Makes it the piece's handle: the piece drags only from it. See Grab Handles .theme Any element Declares a scope for .cssvar , named by its value .cssvar An input Binds the input to --var or scope:--var $edit Magic Member Description active , on() , off() , toggle() Whether .gated regions are on; switch them undo() , redo() Step through the history canUndo , canRedo Whether there's a step to undo or redo version A number that changes with every edit and target change; read it to make a binding re-evaluate target The piece last right-clicked; assignable can(action, el) Whether an action applies: move , remove , duplicate , text , attrs , class , size , copy , cut , paste copy(el) , cut(el) , paste(el) , duplicate(el) , remove(el) Block actions; paste lands after el move(el, dest, before) Move a piece into dest , a container element or a region's key, before before or at the end nest(el) , unnest(el) Move a piece into the container before it, or out one level lock(el, action) , unlock(el, action) Lock or unlock one action, or every action without one, a component piece included; recorded in the history block(node) The piece holding a node, or null ; a component is one piece attr(name, value, el) Set an attribute: a string sets it, true sets it empty, null or false removes it classes.add(cls, el) , .remove() , .toggle(cls, el, force) , .set(value, el) , .has() , .list(el) Change and read an element's classes; classes from a :class binding are left to it scope(el) , scope(value, el) For a region wrapping exactly one component: scope(el) reads the scope of el 's region, 'instance' or 'main' ; scope(value, el) sets it revert(el) Drop a component instance's edits to one element, or to all of them when el is the region patches() The patches a publish would send publish(options) Send the patches, after any publish still running; resolves with the response. { rebase: true } writes over source that changed since the page loaded stale Files changed since the page loaded: from a refused publish, or a reload held back to keep unpublished edits conflicts Edits dropped because the source changed under them: { region, key, element, prop, value, before, reason } each clearConflicts() Empty conflicts ; for .persist regions they're kept across reloads until this is called onPublish A function that receives the patches instead of the development server export() The raw history, { log, cursor } Methods that take el use $edit.target when it's left out, and return true when they made a change or false when they didn't apply. Events Event Fires on detail edit:size The resized element, throughout a resize and once when it's recorded width , height (pixels), css ( { width, height } as written), done edit:stale document , when a publish is refused because source files changed, or a reload is held back files edit:conflict document , when edits are dropped because their element changed in the source conflicts , as in $edit.conflicts Attributes Attribute On Purpose data-edit-hotkeys="off" A region or any element above it Turns off the undo and redo shortcuts there data-unit A .cssvar input A unit added to the input's value :data-key A row of a data list The record's id , bound as in :data-key="walk.id" , when the x-for has no :key Styles Every editing visual is drawn by CSS on the elements being edited, keyed off data-edit-* attributes the module sets, and wrapped in :where() so your own rules win without a fight. No box is ever drawn around a region: a page being edited still looks like the page. .bare turns all of it off. Accent --edit-accent colours every visual at once. Set it on a region to recolour that region, or on :root for everything. < ul x-edit = "treats" style = "--edit-accent: #db2777" > < li > Peanut butter biscuits </ li > < li > Carrot sticks </ li > </ ul > Hover and Focus A piece shows a thin outline on hover and a solid one when focused. Text shows its own outline while you edit it, and a text cursor over it, while the rest of a piece shows a grab cursor. < style > .chunky [data-edit-piece]:hover { outline: 2px dashed currentColor; outline-offset: 6px; } </ style > < ul x-edit.move = "beds" class = "chunky" > < li > Basket </ li > < li > Cushion </ li > </ ul > Variables Variable Default Sets --edit-accent --color-brand-content Colour of every editing visual --edit-ghost-opacity 0.4 Opacity of the stand-in during a drag --edit-drop-reach 48px How far outside another region a drop still lands in it --edit-size both Resize axes: both , x , y , none ; see Resize --edit-size-edges every edge and corner of those axes Which handles to draw --edit-size-handle 1rem Grab area of each handle --edit-size-snap , -x , -y none Snap points --edit-size-snap-distance , -x , -y none, always the nearest point How close an edge must come to snap --edit-size-close , -x , -y none Below this, an x-show element closes State Attributes Attribute Set on data-edit-area Every region; bare on a .bare one data-edit-piece Every piece that can be moved data-edit-grabbable A piece with its own x-edit.grab handle data-edit-text Page text being edited with Rich Text data-edit-dragging The piece being dragged; keyboard when picked up by keyboard data-edit-ghost The stand-in holding a dragged piece's place data-edit-drop-target Other regions a dragged piece can land in data-edit-handle A resize handle, valued by its edge data-edit-resizing The handle being dragged data-edit-snapped The element being resized, and its handle, while an edge sits on a snap point data-edit-key Source elements in a region, naming them for publishing; never set or change it Related Move drags pieces within and between regions. Resize adds edge handles, snap points, and closing. Publishing sends the edits to your backend or writes them into your source files. Rich Text edits a field's text with formatting, and powers page text here. Dropdowns build the right-click menus.


## Move — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/framework/core-modules/move

Move Drag pieces to reorder them, nest them, and move them between regions. Overview .move makes every piece of a region draggable. One drag covers every kind of move: among its siblings, into a container, out of one, or into another region. While you drag, a faint stand-in shows where the piece will land and the container it would land in gets a dashed outline. A piece drags from anywhere on it, its text included: a press that moves a few pixels picks the piece up, and a click that doesn't move edits the text. While you're typing in a piece, dragging across its text selects words instead. The cursor shows a text caret over text and a grab hand elsewhere on a piece. A drop the browser would rewrite is refused and the piece goes back: a <div> into a <p> , a <li> outside a list, a link inside a link, and anything else HTML doesn't allow. x-edit.move is part of Visual Editing : set it up there first. A region with no capability named, as in x-edit="key" , moves and edits text; x-edit.move moves only. Grab Handles To make a piece drag only from one part of it, such as a dotted handle, put x-edit.grab on that part. The rest of the piece then edits and clicks as usual, and only the handle picks it up, so the piece shows no grab cursor elsewhere. The handle is never editable text, and it stays in your markup through copies, duplicates, and publishing. Keep the text beside the handle in its own element, as in the <span> here: a text element that holds a handle isn't edited as one piece of text. < div x-edit = "walkers" > < div class = "row items-center gap-3" > < span x-edit.grab x-icon = "lucide:grip-vertical" > </ span > < span > Poochie's morning walker </ span > </ div > < div class = "row items-center gap-3" > < span x-edit.grab x-icon = "lucide:grip-vertical" > </ span > < span > Poochie's evening walker </ span > </ div > </ div > A handle belongs to the nearest piece around it. Pieces nested inside a piece with a handle still drag from their own surface. In a List or Grid Pieces in a list, a row, or a grid take the order you drop them in. Hovering a piece outlines it, so you can see what you're about to pick up. < ul x-edit.move = "queue" > < li > Wash Poochie </ li > < li > Trim nails </ li > < li > Brush coat </ li > < li > Photo shoot </ li > </ ul > By keyboard, Tab to a piece and press Space or Enter to pick it up. The arrow keys move it, Enter or Space drops it, and Escape puts it back. Alt + Up and Alt + Down move a focused piece one step at once, and work while you're typing in it too; in text, Space and Enter keep typing, so press Alt + Enter first to step out to the piece, then pick it up. A list rendered by x-for reorders its data instead of the markup: the array itself changes order. Each record needs an id , given to the loop as its :key . Add .data to edit record fields too: the row, or any element in it, whose x-text or x-html is a record field, such as x-text="walk.name" , becomes editable, and the edit updates the record when the text loses focus. A row that is itself the field drags from its surface, like other text. Rows from data stay in their own list. To publish a list's order and field edits with mnfst-run --edit , its records must come from a CSV or JSON file declared as a data source in manifest.json , as in $x.walks . A list written inline in x-data , like the one here, edits on the page and reaches onPublish , but has no file to write to. < div x-data = "{ walks: [{ id: 1, name: 'Main Street' }, { id: 2, name: 'Beach' }, { id: 3, name: 'Park' }] }" > < ul x-edit.move.data = "walks" > < template x-for = "walk in walks" :key = "walk.id" > < li x-text = "walk.name" > </ li > </ template > </ ul > < p x-text = "walks.map(w => w.name).join(' → ')" > </ p > </ div > Nesting Any element in a moving region that holds other elements is a container, empty ones included. Paragraphs, headings, and other text elements are always pieces, never containers. Dropping a piece in the middle of a container puts it inside; dropping near the container's edge puts it beside it. Dragging a piece out of its container un-nests it. While you drag, empty containers grow enough to drop into. By keyboard, Alt + Right moves a focused piece into the container just before it, and Alt + Left moves it out one level. In text, Alt + Left and Right keep jumping by word, so press Alt + Enter first. < div x-edit.move = "kennel" > < p > Biscuit </ p > < div > < p > Poochie </ p > < p > Rex </ p > </ div > < p > Mochi </ p > < div > </ div > </ div > Between Regions A piece can be dragged from one region into another that also allows moving. Every region it could land in shows a dashed outline while you drag, an empty one included, and a drop just outside a region still lands in it. The move is one step of the history, and publishing writes it to both places. < div class = "grid grid-cols-2 gap-4" > < ul x-edit.move = "monday" > < li > Bath </ li > < li > Walk </ li > </ ul > < ul x-edit.move = "tuesday" > < li > Vet </ li > </ ul > </ div > Regions of written markup, in the page or in component files, can trade pieces, whole components included. Rows of a data list and the parts inside a component stay where they are, and so does a piece that is itself a region. Freeform Whether a dropped piece flows or sits where you let go is decided by CSS, after the drop. If the piece is in normal flow in its new container, as in a block, flex, or grid layout, it takes its place in that order, and any left and top left over from an earlier freeform drop are removed. If it ends up absolutely positioned, by its own CSS or its container's, it's placed at the drop point. The new left and top are written in the units the piece already uses, so a % position stays fluid. Here the canvas positions its children absolutely and the tray doesn't, so the same sticker sits where you drop it on the canvas and lines up in the tray. They're two regions, so a sticker crosses between them as in Between Regions . < div class = "grid grid-cols-2 gap-4" > < div x-edit.move = "canvas" class = "relative h-48 [&>*]:absolute" > < span style = "left: 1rem; top: 1rem" > Fetch </ span > < span style = "left: 40%; top: 5rem" > Nap </ span > </ div > < div x-edit.move = "tray" class = "col gap-2" > < span > Dinner </ span > </ div > </ div > [&>*]:absolute gives every child of the canvas position: absolute . Dropped in the tray, a sticker is no longer a child of the canvas, so it's in flow and its left and top are removed; dropped back on the canvas, it's positioned again at the drop point. A piece that is absolutely positioned by its own style or classes stays positioned wherever it goes. A positioned piece is dropped inside its container's box, never past its edges. With one focused, the arrow keys nudge it by 4 pixels, or 16 with Shift. Styles Drop Targets While you drag, the container a piece would land in gets a dashed outline, other regions it could land in are marked with data-edit-drop-target , and the stand-in holding its place is marked data-edit-ghost . < style > .targets [data-edit-drop-target], .targets :has(> [data-edit-ghost]) { outline: none; background: color-mix(in oklch, #16a34a 12%, transparent); } .targets [data-edit-ghost] { opacity: 1; outline: 2px dashed #16a34a; } </ style > < div class = "targets grid grid-cols-2 gap-4" > < ul x-edit.move = "indoor" > < li > Puzzle </ li > < li > Tug </ li > </ ul > < ul x-edit.move = "outdoor" > < li > Frisbee </ li > </ ul > </ div > Related Visual Editing sets up regions, text editing, history, and the $edit reference. Resize adds edge handles to an element. Publishing writes moves back to your source.


## Resize — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/framework/core-modules/resize

Resize Resize elements by their edges, with limits, snap points, and closing. Overview .size gives an element handles on its edges and corners. The new width and height are written in the units the element already uses, so rem stays rem and % stays % . The element's own min- and max- width and height are the limits. Each panel below has a handle on its inner edge. Drag it near 12rem or 16rem and it snaps there, and the edge thickens while it holds. Drag it below 6rem and the panel closes as you drag; drag back out and it reopens. Let go while it's closed and it stays closed: the buttons reopen it, and so does undo. < div x-data = "{ left: true, right: true }" class = "row h-48 border border-line" > < div x-edit.size = "left-panel" x-show = "left" style = "width: 12rem; min-width: 8rem; max-width: 20rem; --edit-size: x; --edit-size-edges: end; --edit-size-snap: 12rem 16rem; --edit-size-snap-distance: 1rem; --edit-size-close: 6rem" > Left panel </ div > < main class = "grow col gap-2" > < span > Main content </ span > < button @ click = "left = !left" > Toggle left </ button > < button @ click = "right = !right" > Toggle right </ button > </ main > < div x-edit.size = "right-panel" x-show = "right" style = "width: 12rem; min-width: 8rem; max-width: 20rem; --edit-size: x; --edit-size-edges: start; --edit-size-snap: 12rem 16rem; --edit-size-snap-distance: 1rem; --edit-size-close: 6rem" > Right panel </ div > </ div > Everything is set with --edit-size-* variables, on the element or anywhere above it, so a theme file can set project-wide defaults. Snapping and closing are off unless you set them. none on any of the variables cancels a value inherited from above. x-edit.size is part of Visual Editing : set it up there first. It can go on its own element, or on a region that also moves and edits text. Handles and Limits Variable Default Sets --edit-size both Which way it resizes: both , x , y , or none --edit-size-edges every edge and corner of those axes The handles, from top right bottom left , corners such as bottom-right , and logical start end top-start bottom-end that follow the writing direction --edit-size-handle 1rem How wide each handle's grab area is A handle shows when you hover the element, and it can be focused with Tab: the arrow keys then resize by 8 pixels, or 32 with Shift. edit:size fires on the element throughout a resize, and once more when it's recorded, with detail.done set. Handles are drawn inside the element, so an image, video, or other element that can't hold children is resized through a wrapper, like the <figure> in the Visual Editing overview . Snap Points --edit-size-snap lists sizes the edge is pulled to, in any CSS length, such as 12rem 16rem 50% . --edit-size-snap-distance sets how close the edge must come before it's pulled in. Without a distance, the size is always the nearest snap point. -x and -y variants, such as --edit-size-snap-x , set each axis on its own and take priority over the shared value. While an edge sits on a snap point, the element and its handle carry data-edit-snapped , and the edge is drawn thicker, so you can feel the snap before you let go. Close and Reopen --edit-size-close (or -close-x , -close-y ) closes the element as soon as the edge is dragged past that size, while you're still holding it, and reopens it if you drag back out. Closing rides x-show : its x-show variable is set to false , so Alpine hides it. Let go while it's closed and the close is recorded: the element keeps its minimum size, or the size it had if it has no minimum, ready to reopen. Reopen it with your own button that sets the variable back, or undo: one undo restores both the size and the visibility. Pressing Escape mid-drag, or any cancelled drag, reopens it. The x-show value must be something that can be assigned, such as left or panels.left . Without one, Visual Editing warns in the console and a resize dragged below the close size goes back to the size it had when released. Closing and reopening are part of the page state, not the content: they aren't kept by .persist or published. Styles Handles Each handle is a <span data-edit-handle> inside the element, valued by its edge. Its grab area is transparent and its visible line is its ::before . While a handle is being dragged it carries data-edit-resizing , and data-edit-snapped while its edge sits on a snap point. < style > .thick-handles [data-edit-handle]::before { background-color: var(--color-line); border-radius: 999px; } .thick-handles [data-edit-handle="right"]::before { width: 4px; height: 2.5rem; } .thick-handles [data-edit-handle="bottom"]::before { width: 2.5rem; height: 4px; } </ style > < div x-edit.size = "kennel-size" class = "thick-handles" style = "width: 16rem; height: 6rem; --edit-size-edges: right bottom" > Drag the right or bottom edge </ div > Related Visual Editing sets up regions, history, and the $edit reference. Move drags pieces to new places. Publishing writes sizes back to your source.


## Publishing — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/framework/core-modules/edit-publishing

Publishing Send edits to your own backend, or write them into your source files. Overview Edits are kept as a history of changes until you publish them. $edit.patches() turns that history into patches: the final state of each changed region, in terms of your source. $edit.publish() sends them, and where they go depends on who the editor is for: Your own product , where people edit content you store: set $edit.onPublish and the patches go to your code. Your own project , which you edit in the browser while you build it: run mnfst-run --edit and the patches are written into your source files. Publishing is part of Visual Editing : set it up there first. Patches Edit the profile below and watch its patches change. Each edit updates the list as soon as it's recorded, and undo takes it back out. < article x-edit = "profile" > < h3 > Poochie </ h3 > < p > Loves pasta and ice cream. </ p > </ article > < pre x-text = "($edit.version, JSON.stringify($edit.patches(), null, 2))" > </ pre > Reading $edit.version makes the binding run again after every edit. The demo shows only its own region's patches; $edit.patches() returns every region's. A text edit in markup produces one patch for its region. Rename Poochie and it looks like this: { "kind" : "static-tree" , "region" : "profile" , "tree" : { "key" : "@profile@ARTICLE:Poochie Loves pasta and " , "children" : [ { "key" : "@profile@H3:Poochie" , "at" : "0" , "edits" : { "text" : "Poochie the Great" } } ] , "path" : true } } Field Means kind What was edited: static-tree for markup, data-val for a record field, data for a data list's order, component for a component's text and classes, theme for a theme value region The x-edit key the edits belong to tree The changed elements, nested as in your markup; untouched elements are left out key An element's identity in your source: its region, its tag, and the first 24 characters of its text when the page loaded at Its position among its parent's children, as 0 , 1.2 , and so on edits The final values: text , class , style , or another attribute; null removes it Moves, nesting, and sizes show up in the same tree: a reordered container lists its children's keys in their new order, and a resize is a style edit. A data list produces one data-val patch per edited field, { kind, region, source, id, field, value } , and, when reordered, one data patch, { kind, region, op: 'reorderData', source, order } . A component edit is { kind, scope, component, region, edits, reverts } , where scope is main for the component file or instance for one instance, and only an instance carries region and reverts . A global theme value is one theme patch, { kind, scope, var, value, file } , with file left null for the server to choose. To Your Own Backend Set $edit.onPublish to a function, and publish() hands it the patches. Send them wherever your product keeps its content: your API, a database row, or the pipeline that rebuilds a published site. Return the response, or a promise of it; unless it reports an error, the edits count as published and the history starts again from there. < div x-data = "{ init() { this.$edit.onPublish = async patches => { const res = await fetch('/api/pages/home', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify(patches) }); if (!res.ok) throw new Error('Saving failed: ' + res.status); return res.json(); }; } }" > </ div > If the handler throws, or its promise rejects, publish() rejects with that error and the history is kept, so nothing is lost and the person can try again. A response shaped { results: [...] } in which any result has status: 'error' counts as failed in the same way. Show the outcome where people can see it: < div x-data = "{ message: '' }" > < button :disabled = "!$edit.canUndo" @ click = "$edit.publish() .then(() => message = 'Published') .catch(err => message = err.message)" > Publish </ button > < span x-text = "message" > </ span > </ div > canUndo doubles as "there's something to publish", since a publish clears the history. To Your Source Files Run the local development server with editing switched on, edit the page in the browser, and publish. With no onPublish set, the patches go to the server, which writes them straight into your source files. npx mnfst-run --edit Rename Poochie in the page and publish, and index.html changes from the first version to the second, with nothing else in the file touched: Before After < article x-edit = "profile" > < h3 > Poochie </ h3 > < p > Loves pasta and ice cream. </ p > </ article > < article x-edit = "profile" > < h3 > Poochie the Great </ h3 > < p > Loves pasta and ice cream. </ p > </ article > Edited Written to Markup in a region index.html , or the component's HTML file when the region is written in one A data list's order and record fields The CSV or JSON file the data source names in manifest.json (a JSON file must hold an array of records) A component instance The instance's attributes in index.html , or the component's HTML file in main scope Global theme values The manifest.theme.css that index.html links, wherever it lives; with none linked, styles/core/manifest.theme.css if it exists Scoped theme values The scope element's own style attribute, in the file it's written in; a scope inside content another module generates has no file, so its values are refused by name publish() resolves with the server's report, one result per patch: { "results" : [ { "region" : "profile" , "status" : "written" , "file" : "index.html" } , { "region" : "walks" , "status" : "error" , "reason" : "file not found: data/walks.csv" } ] } Each result's status is written , error with a reason , or skipped when a related region failed. Each kind of edit writes only its own kind of file (HTML, CSS, or data), inside the project, and never into a hidden folder such as .git or into node_modules . Files are written together or not at all. If one region or theme value can't be published, the others are published without it: its result names it and the reason, and its edits stay in the history; a region tied to it by a move between them stays back with it. Publishes run one at a time: a second waits for the first to finish, then builds on its result. When the page loads, it reads from the server how each source file looks, and publishing needs that. If it couldn't be read, because the page isn't served by mnfst-run --edit or the server didn't answer, a publish is refused and the edits are kept. In a single-page app, a region that isn't on screen keeps its edits: they wait in the history, show again when the region comes back, and publish then. A region inside content another module generates, such as x-markdown or x-html output, edits on the page and reaches onPublish , but its markup isn't in a file, so mnfst-run --edit refuses it by name, keeps its edits, and publishes the other regions. Visual Editing warns about it once in the console. The examples in these articles are regions of that kind, inside each article's markdown, so their patches are real but have no file to be written to. The server only accepts edits from pages it serves on your machine, and its editing endpoints don't exist without --edit . Changed Source A publish checks that the source still matches what the page loaded. The development server reloads an open page whenever an HTML file changes, so the page normally shows the source as it is now. While edits that .persist doesn't keep are waiting to be published, including edits in a region that's off screen in a single-page app, that reload is held back so they aren't lost: Visual Editing warns in the console, adds the files to $edit.stale , and fires edit:stale . Publish them with rebase , as below, and the page reloads itself afterwards. Typing still in progress in a .persist region is recorded before a reload, so it isn't lost either, and a publish includes typing in progress wherever it is. If an HTML file the publish would rewrite has changed since the page loaded, the whole publish is refused, so a stale page can't overwrite newer work. Stylesheets and data files aren't checked this way, because their edits are written value by value: a CSS or data file saved in your code editor while the page is open doesn't block a publish. A refused publish keeps the history, lists the changed files in $edit.stale , and fires edit:stale on the document with detail.files . Either reload, to start again from the new source, or call $edit.publish({ rebase: true }) to take the source as it is now and write the edits over it, each into the element it belongs to. After a rebase that wrote over changes, the page reloads itself shortly afterwards to show the result, and until it has, a plain publish is refused as stale. < div x-data @ edit:stale.document = "console.warn('Changed since this page loaded:', $event.detail.files)" > < p x-show = "$edit.stale.length" > < span x-text = "$edit.stale.join(', ')" > </ span > changed since this page loaded. < button @ click = "$edit.publish({ rebase: true })" > Publish over it </ button > < button @ click = "location.reload()" > Reload </ button > </ p > </ div > The page also remembers each element it shows as it was when it loaded: its tag, its attributes, and its own text. A publish that edits an element changed in the meantime is refused with reload to continue , rebase or not, because its edit could land on the wrong thing. The same goes for identical elements, such as two <li>Walk</li> , when any of them moved or changed: the page can no longer tell which one you edited. Changes elsewhere in the file, outside the elements you edited, don't get in the way of a rebase. Conflicts Edits kept from before, by .persist or by a region coming back on screen, can find the source changed under them. A text or attribute edit whose element changed can't be applied. Moves and other layout edits are kept when the only change was text in pieces they didn't move; if a piece they moved, added, or removed changed, the region's layout edits can't be applied, and if pieces swapped places, Visual Editing reports it rather than guess which is which. Edits that can't be applied are dropped from the history and reported: $edit.conflicts lists them, edit:conflict fires on the document with detail.conflicts , and Visual Editing warns in the console. Each entry has a reason in words, its region , the element's key and its tag and text as element , the prop it edited, and the value it held. Layout entries have prop: 'structure' , and their value holds what was dropped, { changed, moved, copies } , so typed content can be recovered. For a .persist region, the list survives reloads until you call $edit.clearConflicts() . < div x-data x-show = "$edit.conflicts.length" > < p > Some edits no longer fit the page and were set aside: </ p > < ul > < template x-for = "c in $edit.conflicts" > < li > < strong x-text = "c.element" > </ strong > : < span x-text = "c.reason" > </ span > </ li > </ template > </ ul > < button @ click = "$edit.clearConflicts()" > Dismiss </ button > </ div > Related Visual Editing sets up regions, history, and the $edit reference. Move and Resize cover the layout edits that publish here.


# Framework docs / Appwrite Modules


## Appwrite Modules — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/framework/appwrite-modules

Article does not exist There is no documentation at this path.


## Appwrite Setup — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/framework/appwrite-modules/appwrite-setup

Appwrite Setup Use Appwrite to turn Manifest projects into production-ready applications. Overview Appwrite provides turnkey backend infrastructure, available open source or cloud hosted with a generous free tier. Together with Manifest you can quickly generate feature-complete applications including user authentication, databases, and storage. In Appwrite Establish a project with any name and region in Appwrite . Once created you'll access the project console: Credentials Your Manifest project will need the Appwrite project's Project ID and API Endpoint to connect. Get them from the Appwrite project's general Settings , under API credentials: Web Platform Appwrite only accepts browser requests from hostnames registered with the project. From the project Overview , select Add platform > Web and enter each hostname that will run your Manifest project: localhost for local development Each staging and production domain, such as example.com Without this, sign-in and data requests are blocked by the browser. Dev Key An optional Dev Key can also be used during Manifest project development to bypass Appwrite's rate limits. It should not be included in production. Get one from Overview > Dev keys : Manifest Setup Scripts Add the Appwrite SDK and manifest.js scripts to the HTML head. manifest.json is also required to register Appwrite credentials and data sources. Appwrite modules can be loaded in two ways: explicitly via the data-modules attribute, or automatically from manifest.json . When auto-detected, the data module loads when an appwrite object is present, the auth module when that object includes auth (even "auth": {} ), and presence when it includes presence . The supporting core data module will also be loaded whether or not it's declared. Auto-detect Declared <!-- Meta --> < link rel = "manifest" href = "/manifest.json" > <!-- Scripts --> < script src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/appwrite@latest" > </ script > < script src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mnfst@latest/lib/manifest.min.js" > </ script > <!-- Meta --> < link rel = "manifest" href = "/manifest.json" > <!-- Scripts --> < script src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/appwrite@latest" > </ script > < script src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mnfst@latest/lib/manifest.min.js" data-modules = "+appwrite-auth,+appwrite-data" > </ script > manifest.json Add the Appwrite project credentials detailed above to manifest.json under an appwrite property. These are inherited by any other objects in the manifest that reference Appwrite, like database or storage sources. The Project ID and API Endpoint are public and safe to commit — Appwrite enforces access via its own project-level permissions. The Dev Key is sensitive (it bypasses rate limits) and must not be committed. Reference it via ${PUBLIC_APPWRITE_DEV_KEY} and put the value in a gitignored .env file. Only variables prefixed PUBLIC_ reach the browser, so the name needs that prefix. The same ${VAR} syntax is also supported for the Project ID and API Endpoint if you prefer to keep them out of source. manifest.json .env { "appwrite" : { "projectId" : "your-project-id" , "endpoint" : "your-API-endpoint" , "devKey" : "${PUBLIC_APPWRITE_DEV_KEY}" } } PUBLIC_APPWRITE_DEV_KEY=your-appwrite-dev-key How ${VAR} resolution works. The framework substitutes ${VAR} placeholders in manifest.json against window.env at runtime. The npx mnfst-run dev server reads your project's .env at startup and injects its PUBLIC_ variables as a window.env = {…} block into served HTML. Other variables stay on the server, so a placeholder without the prefix is left unresolved, and an unresolved Dev Key turns the auth module off. If you serve the project with your own local server (Python's http.server , live-server , serve , etc.), it won't inject window.env for you; you'll need to add a <script>window.env = {…}</script> block to index.html before the manifest.min.js tag, or your placeholders will reach the module unresolved and the auth/data modules will refuse to initialize. Production deployments. Static hosts (Netlify, Vercel, Cloudflare Pages, GitHub Pages, S3, etc.) serve manifest.json verbatim — no runtime substitution. The Dev Key should not ship to production in the first place: it's strictly a development-time convenience for bypassing Appwrite's rate limits, and Appwrite enforces real auth through project-level permissions for live users. For any other ${VAR} values you actually need in production, either hardcode them directly in manifest.json (acceptable for public values like Project ID and API Endpoint), bake them into the prerendered HTML at build time, or use your host's env-var injection feature. Data sources always connect with these appwrite credentials. A database source can name its own database with appwriteDatabaseId ; without it, the source uses appwrite.databaseId , then main . Next Steps After a successful setup above, your Manifest project should be paired with your Appwrite project(s). Proceed to configuring: Users or Teams Databases or Storage


## Auth — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/framework/appwrite-modules/auth

Auth Implement a complete authentication solution for your app with a connected Appwrite project. Setup Complete the Appwrite setup steps to connect your Appwrite and Manifest projects. Add the Appwrite SDK and manifest.js scripts to the HTML head. manifest.json is also required for Appwrite credentials and configuring auth details. The auth module auto-loads when the appwrite object includes auth , even an empty "auth": {} . Auto-detect Declared <!-- Meta --> < link rel = "manifest" href = "/manifest.json" > <!-- Scripts --> < script src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/appwrite@latest" > </ script > < script src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mnfst@latest/lib/manifest.min.js" > </ script > <!-- Meta --> < link rel = "manifest" href = "/manifest.json" > <!-- Scripts --> < script src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/appwrite@latest" > </ script > < script src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mnfst@latest/lib/manifest.min.js" data-modules = "+appwrite-auth" > </ script > Next Steps Complete authentication support using the guides for: Users Teams (optional)


## Users — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/framework/appwrite-modules/users

Users Enable guests and user accounts in your project. Appwrite Configuration Your Appwrite project's Auth dashboard provides various options to customize the user experience. Go to Auth > Settings to enable your preferred sign-in methods. The auth module currently supports: OAuth2 Providers (Google, Apple, GitHub, Discord, and 35+ more) Anonymous (guest sessions) Magic URL Email OTP (one-time passcode) Phone OTP (SMS one-time passcode) See Appwrite's Auth docs for all configuration details. Sign-in Methods With Manifest and Appwrite, a frontend user registration flow (vs. a login flow) is not required. Unrecognized users will have a new account automatically generated, while known users will login to their existing account (from any sign-in method). Interactive examples on this page demonstrate real authentication with you as the user. Each example reflects the most recent auth state you've set (e.g. signed-in or out). Example styles and layouts may differ from code snippets. In manifest.json , use the auth methods array to define your project's sign-in methods, and enable each one in the connected Appwrite project. Without methods , magic URLs and OAuth are enabled ( ["magic", "oauth"] ). The auth object itself is what loads the auth module, so include it even when empty ( "auth": {} ). manifest.json { "appwrite" : { "projectId" : "your-project-id" , "endpoint" : "your-API-endpoint" , "auth" : { "methods" : [ "oauth" , "magic" , "guest-manual" ] } } } Method Description guest-auto Automatically creates anonymous guest sessions for all visitors ( guest is an accepted synonym) guest-manual Allows users to manually create guest sessions via $auth.requestGuest() magic Enables passwordless login via magic URLs sent to email otp Enables passwordless login via a one-time passcode sent to email phone Enables passwordless login via a one-time passcode sent by SMS oauth Enables OAuth sign-in with providers like Google, GitHub, etc. OAuth OAuth enables sign-in with third-party providers like Google, GitHub, and 35+ other services supported by and configured in Appwrite's Auth > Settings page. manifest.json HTML { "appwrite" : { ... "auth" : { "methods" : [ "oauth" ] } } } < button @ click = "$auth.loginOAuth('google')" :disabled = "($auth.isAuthenticated && !$auth.isAnonymous) || $auth.inProgress" > Sign in with Google </ button > < button @ click = "$auth.loginOAuth('github')" :disabled = "($auth.isAuthenticated && !$auth.isAnonymous) || $auth.inProgress" > Sign in with GitHub </ button > < button @ click = "$auth.logout()" :disabled = "!$auth.isAuthenticated || $auth.inProgress" > Logout </ button > <!-- Status --> < p x-show = "$auth.inProgress" > Authorizing... </ p > < p x-show = "$auth.isAuthenticated" > You're signed-in using < b x-text = "$auth.method || 'guest'" > </ b > < span x-show = "$auth.provider" > via < b x-text = "$auth.provider" > </ b > </ span > as < b x-text = "$auth.user?.email || 'a guest'" > </ b > </ p > < p x-show = "!$auth.isAuthenticated" > You're not signed-in. </ p > < p x-show = "$auth.error" x-text = "$auth.error" > </ p > Sign in with Google Sign in with GitHub Logout Authorizing... You're signed-in using guest via as a guest You're not signed-in. The $auth.loginOAuth('...') method accepts provider names like google , github , and discord . When applicable, the user is redirected to the provider's sign-in page and gets returned when authenticated. Magic URLs Magic URLs provide passwordless authentication via email. Users enter their email address and get emailed a sign-in link that's valid for one hour, which can be used once. manifest.json HTML { "appwrite" : { ... "auth" : { "methods" : [ "magic" ] } } } <!-- Form --> < input type = "email" pattern = ".*@.*\..*" required autocomplete = "on" placeholder = "Input email" aria-label = "Email" class = "peer" @ keyup.enter = "$auth.sendMagicLink()" :disabled = "($auth.isAuthenticated && !$auth.isAnonymous) || $auth.inProgress" /> < button class = "peer-invalid:disabled" @ click = "$auth.sendMagicLink()" :disabled = "($auth.isAuthenticated && !$auth.isAnonymous) || $auth.inProgress" > Send Magic URL </ button > < button @ click = "$auth.logout()" :disabled = "!$auth.isAuthenticated || $auth.inProgress" class = "!w-fit" > Logout </ button > <!-- Status --> < p x-show = "$auth.inProgress" > Authorizing... </ p > < p x-show = "$auth.magicLinkSent" > Magic URL sent. Check your inbox or spam to sign-in. </ p > < p x-show = "$auth.magicLinkExpired" > Magic URL expired. Please try again. </ p > < p x-show = "$auth.isAuthenticated" > You're signed-in using < b x-text = "$auth.method || 'guest'" > </ b > < span x-show = "$auth.provider" > via < b x-text = "$auth.provider" > </ b > </ span > as < b x-text = "$auth.user?.email || 'a guest'" > </ b > </ p > < p x-show = "!$auth.isAuthenticated" > You're not signed-in. </ p > < p x-show = "$auth.error" x-text = "$auth.error" > </ p > Send Magic URL Logout Authorizing... Magic URL sent. Check your inbox or spam to sign-in. Magic URL expired. Please try again. You're signed-in using guest via as a guest You're not signed-in. The button's $auth.sendMagicLink() method automatically finds the email input in the same parent element, form element, or otherwise finds the first email input on the page. To target a specific input, add its element ID like $auth.sendMagicLink('#email-input') . When activated, a magic URL is sent and the email input field is cleared. When users click the magic URL in their email, they're redirected back to your app. The module automatically handles the callback and creates the session. Email content can be customized in Appwrite under Auth > Templates > Magic URL . Email OTP Email OTP provides passwordless authentication via a one-time passcode. Users enter their email address, receive a short code by email, then enter that code to sign in — all on the same page, with no redirect. manifest.json HTML { "appwrite" : { ... "auth" : { "methods" : [ "otp" ] } } } <!-- Step 1: request a code --> < input type = "email" placeholder = "Email" x-show = "!$auth.otpSent" @ keyup.enter = "$auth.sendEmailOTP()" /> < button x-show = "!$auth.otpSent" @ click = "$auth.sendEmailOTP()" > Email code </ button > <!-- Step 2: enter the code --> < input name = "otp" placeholder = "Code" x-show = "$auth.otpSent" @ keyup.enter = "$auth.submitOTP()" /> < button x-show = "$auth.otpSent" @ click = "$auth.submitOTP()" > Verify </ button > < p x-show = "$auth.otpSent" > Code sent — check your inbox. </ p > Email Code Verify Logout Authorizing... Code sent. Check your inbox or spam. Code was invalid or expired. Please try again. You're signed-in using guest as a guest You're not signed-in. $auth.sendEmailOTP() finds the email input the same way sendMagicLink() does (nearest input, form, or first on the page), or accepts a selector like $auth.sendEmailOTP('#email-input') . After a code is sent, $auth.otpSent becomes true ; $auth.submitOTP() reads the code input (any input[name="otp"] , autocomplete="one-time-code" , or numeric input) and completes sign-in. Pass { phrase: true } to sendEmailOTP to enable Appwrite's anti-phishing security phrase, then display $auth.otpPhrase alongside the code field. Email content and code length can be customized in Appwrite under Auth > Templates > OTP . Phone OTP Phone OTP provides passwordless authentication via a one-time passcode sent by SMS. Users enter their phone number, receive a short code by text, then enter that code to sign in — all on the same page, with no redirect. manifest.json HTML { "appwrite" : { ... "auth" : { "methods" : [ "phone" ] } } } <!-- Step 1: request a code --> < input type = "tel" placeholder = "+14155550123" x-show = "!$auth.otpSent" @ keyup.enter = "$auth.sendPhoneOTP()" /> < button x-show = "!$auth.otpSent" @ click = "$auth.sendPhoneOTP()" > Text code </ button > <!-- Step 2: enter the code --> < input name = "otp" placeholder = "Code" x-show = "$auth.otpSent" @ keyup.enter = "$auth.submitOTP()" /> < button x-show = "$auth.otpSent" @ click = "$auth.submitOTP()" > Verify </ button > < p x-show = "$auth.otpSent" > Code sent — check your phone. </ p > $auth.sendPhoneOTP() finds the phone input the same way sendEmailOTP() does (nearest input[type="tel"] , form, or first on the page), or accepts a selector like $auth.sendPhoneOTP('#phone-input') . Numbers must include the country code (international E.164 format, e.g. +14155550123 ); common separators like spaces, dashes, and parentheses are stripped automatically. The code-entry step is shared with email OTP: the same $auth.submitOTP() and $auth.otpSent / $auth.otpExpired flags drive it, so the verify markup is identical. Phone OTP requires an SMS provider (Twilio, Vonage, MSG91, or Telesign) connected in Appwrite under Messaging > Providers , and the Phone method enabled under Auth > Settings . Guest Sessions Guest sessions allow visitors to browse your app without creating an account, with each session registered in the Appwrite userbase (including repeat visits from the same user). With Manifest, guest sessions can begin automatically or by a user action. By default, when a guest signs in, a fresh account is created and the guest session is discarded, along with anything tied to it (such as guest-created teams ). To keep them: Sign-in method Keep the guest's data with OAuth, magic URL guestUpgrade : converts the guest's account in place Email OTP, phone OTP guestMigration : moves the guest's teams to the new account OTP sign-ins can't convert a guest in place (an Appwrite limitation), so they always create a fresh account. Auto Guest Sessions When guest-auto is enabled in your manifest, all visitors automatically enter a guest session on page load. manifest.json { "appwrite" : { ... "auth" : { "methods" : [ "guest-auto" ] } } } Manual Guest Sessions When guest-manual is enabled, visitors must explicitly choose to continue as a guest. manifest.json HTML { "appwrite" : { ... "auth" : { "methods" : [ "guest-manual" ] } } } < button @ click = "$auth.requestGuest()" :disabled = "$auth.isAuthenticated || $auth.inProgress" > Continue as Guest </ button > < button @ click = "$auth.logout()" :disabled = "!$auth.isAuthenticated || $auth.inProgress" > Logout </ button > <!-- Status --> < p x-show = "$auth.isAnonymous" > You're a guest </ p > < p x-show = "!$auth.isAnonymous && $auth.isAuthenticated" > You're already signed in </ p > < p x-show = "!$auth.isAuthenticated" > You're not signed in </ p > Continue as Guest Logout You're a guest You're already signed in You're not signed in Guest Upgrade Set guestUpgrade to true to convert a guest's existing account in place when they sign in with OAuth or a magic URL, preserving its data and team memberships. manifest.json { "appwrite" : { ... "auth" : { "methods" : [ "guest-manual" , "magic" , "oauth" ] , "guestUpgrade" : true } } } No markup changes are needed — $auth.sendMagicLink() and $auth.loginOAuth() handle the upgrade automatically when a guest signs in. guestUpgrade defaults to the value of teams.guests , so enabling guest teams turns it on for you. Guest Team Carryover (OTP) For email and phone OTP sign-ins, guestMigration carries the guest's teams over to the new account by reassigning team membership. Reassigning team ownership between accounts is privileged — it needs a server API key, so it has to run on a server, not in the browser. To make that turnkey, Manifest provides a ready-to-deploy guest-migration function template . Deploy it to your Appwrite project and point the module at it: manifest.json { "appwrite" : { ... "auth" : { "methods" : [ "guest-manual" , "otp" ] , "teams" : { "permanent" : [ "Workspace" ] , "guests" : true } , "guestMigration" : { "functionId" : "<your function id>" } } } } No markup changes — after a guest verifies an OTP code, the module transparently moves their teams to the new account. The same function also garbage-collects abandoned guests and their orphaned teams on a schedule. The template is one ready-made implementation; the module just calls a function that speaks a small prepare / commit contract, so you can swap the function's internals for your own backend logic if you ever need to. Its README walks through deploying it. Combined Methods Sign-in methods can be stacked to provide optionality to users. manifest.json HTML { "appwrite" : { ... "auth" : { "methods" : [ "guest-manual" , "magic" , "oauth" ] } } } <!-- OAuth Buttons --> < button @ click = "$auth.loginOAuth('google')" :disabled = "($auth.isAuthenticated && !$auth.isAnonymous) || $auth.inProgress" > < i x-icon = "simple-icons:google" > </ i > < span > Sign in with Google </ span > </ button > < button @ click = "$auth.loginOAuth('github')" :disabled = "($auth.isAuthenticated && !$auth.isAnonymous) || $auth.inProgress" > < i x-icon = "simple-icons:github" > </ i > < span > Sign in with GitHub </ span > </ button > < div class = "divider my-8" > OR </ div > <!-- Magic URL Form --> < input class = "peer" type = "email" pattern = ".*@.*\..*" required autocomplete = "on" placeholder = "Input email" aria-label = "Email" @ keyup.enter = "$auth.sendMagicLink()" :disabled = "($auth.isAuthenticated && !$auth.isAnonymous) || $auth.inProgress" /> < button class = "peer-invalid:disabled" @ click = "$auth.sendMagicLink()" :disabled = "($auth.isAuthenticated && !$auth.isAnonymous) || $auth.inProgress" > Send Magic URL </ button > < div class = "divider my-8" > OR </ div > <!-- Guest Button --> < button @ click = "$auth.requestGuest()" :disabled = "$auth.isAuthenticated || $auth.inProgress" > Continue as Guest </ button > <!-- Status --> < div class = "my-8" > < p x-show = "$auth.inProgress" > Authorizing... </ p > < p x-show = "$auth.magicLinkSent" > Magic URL sent. Check your inbox or spam to sign-in. </ p > < p x-show = "$auth.magicLinkExpired" > Magic URL expired. Please try again. </ p > < p x-show = "$auth.isAuthenticated" > You're signed-in using < b x-text = "$auth.method || 'guest'" > </ b > < span x-show = "$auth.provider" > via < b x-text = "$auth.provider" > </ b > </ span > as < b x-text = "$auth.user?.email || 'a guest'" > </ b > </ p > < p x-show = "!$auth.isAuthenticated" > You're not signed-in. </ p > < p x-show = "$auth.error" x-text = "$auth.error" > </ p > </ div > <!-- Logout --> < button @ click = "$auth.logout()" :disabled = "!$auth.isAuthenticated || $auth.inProgress" > Logout </ button > Sign in with Google Sign in with GitHub OR Send Magic URL OR Continue as Guest Authorizing... Magic URL sent. Check your inbox or spam to sign-in. Magic URL expired. Please try again. You're signed-in using guest via as a guest You're not signed-in. Logout Properties The auth module provides an $auth magic property that exposes authentication state and methods. Authentication State User Profile ($auth.user) Current user profile (null if not authenticated). The user object comes directly from Appwrite's account.get() . Property Type Description $auth.user?.$id string User's unique ID $auth.user?.email string User's email address $auth.user?.name string User's display name $auth.user?.$createdAt string Account creation timestamp $auth.user?.$updatedAt string Last update timestamp $auth.user?.prefs object User preferences object Other properties - All other Appwrite User object properties are available Session Information ($auth.session) Current session details (null if not authenticated). The session object comes directly from Appwrite's session data. Property Type Description $auth.session?.$id string Session ID $auth.session?.userId string User ID associated with session $auth.session?.expire string Session expiration timestamp $auth.session?.provider string Authentication provider used ( 'anonymous' , 'magic-url' , 'email' or 'token' for email OTP, 'phone' , or the OAuth provider name) $auth.session?.ip string IP address of session $auth.session?.osCode string Operating system code $auth.session?.osName string Operating system name $auth.session?.osVersion string Operating system version $auth.session?.deviceName string Device name $auth.session?.deviceBrand string Device brand $auth.session?.deviceModel string Device model Other properties - All other Appwrite Session object properties are available Status Flags Property Type Description $auth.isAuthenticated boolean Indicates if user is authenticated $auth.isAnonymous boolean Indicates if user is a guest $auth.inProgress boolean Indicates if an auth operation is in progress $auth.error string | null Error message string (null if no error) $auth.magicLinkSent boolean Indicates if magic link was sent $auth.magicLinkExpired boolean Indicates if magic link expired $auth.otpSent boolean Indicates if an OTP code (email or SMS) was sent and awaits entry $auth.otpExpired boolean Indicates if the entered OTP code was invalid or expired $auth.otpPhrase string | null Email OTP anti-phishing security phrase (when requested with { phrase: true } ) $auth.guestManualEnabled boolean Indicates if manual guest creation is enabled Computed Properties Property Type Description $auth.method string | null Authentication method: 'oauth' , 'magic' , 'otp' , 'phone' , 'anonymous' , or null $auth.provider string | null OAuth provider name (e.g., 'google' , 'github' ) or null for non-OAuth methods Available Methods Method Parameters Description $auth.loginOAuth(...) provider (string), successUrl (optional), failureUrl (optional) Sign in with OAuth provider. Redirects to provider. $auth.sendMagicLink(...) emailInputOrRef (element ID or element, optional), redirectUrl (optional) Send magic link to email. $auth.sendEmailOTP(...) emailInputOrRef (selector or element, optional), options (optional, { phrase: true } for a security phrase) Email a one-time passcode. $auth.sendPhoneOTP(...) phoneInputOrRef (selector or element, optional) Text a one-time passcode to a phone number (E.164 format). $auth.submitOTP(...) codeInputOrRef (selector or element, optional) Verify the entered passcode and complete sign-in (email or phone). $auth.requestGuest() None Create a manual guest session. $auth.logout() None Delete current session and sign out. If automatic guest sessions are enabled, a new guest session will begin after logout. $auth.refresh() None Refresh user data from Appwrite. $auth.canAuthenticate() None Check if user can authenticate (not already signed in or in progress). Session Recovery Signing in or out in one tab updates every open tab, and every Appwrite table and bucket source reloads for the new user, so the previous user's entries never linger. With auto guest sessions, signing out moves every tab to a new guest session. If the app opens offline, it renders signed out ( $auth.isAuthenticated is false ) and restores the session on its own once Appwrite is reachable (it rechecks on reconnect, on tab refocus, and after 2, 5, 15 and 60 seconds); no guest session is created over the real one. Only a genuine "no session" answer from Appwrite signs a user out. Listen for manifest:auth:login to react when the session returns. While offline, persisted rows saved for the user last signed in on this device stay shown for every source, including tables with a scope and sources whose queries reference $auth. values, unless the persistence scope depends on the signed-in user or team, which can't be evaluated until the session is verified (the saved rows stay on the device until then). A restored session reloads them; a "no session" answer, a sign-out, or a different user clears them. Events The auth module dispatches these events on window : Event Fires when manifest:auth:initialized The session check on page load has finished, signed in or not ( detail.isAuthenticated , detail.isAnonymous ) manifest:auth:login A user signs in, or a session is restored ( detail.user holds the user) manifest:auth:anonymous A guest session starts manifest:auth:logout The user signs out, or the session has expired manifest:auth:session-cleared The session ended or changed elsewhere, such as in another tab manifest:auth:teams-loaded The user's teams have loaded manifest:auth:before-logout A session is about to end through $auth : signing out, or a guest session replaced by a sign-in ( detail.waitUntil(promise) holds the sign-out briefly) < div x-data @ manifest:auth:login.window = "$toast('Welcome back')" > </ div > Cleanup Before Sign-out Since 0.5.307, manifest:auth:before-logout fires while the session is still valid, so your code can finish work that needs it, such as deleting a record only the user may delete. Pass a promise to event.detail.waitUntil() and the session ends once it settles, or after 3 seconds at most so sign-out never hangs. Presence uses it to remove the person's status. window . addEventListener ( 'manifest:auth:before-logout' , ( event ) => { event. detail . waitUntil ( saveDraft ()); }); The event only fires for sessions ended through $auth . A session that expires or is revoked elsewhere ends without it. Next Steps See teams to enable shared workspaces between users, including roles and permissions.


## Teams — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/framework/appwrite-modules/teams

Teams Allow users to work together within your application. Team Management Teams are collaborative workspaces where members share roles and permissions. Teams are automatically loaded when a user authenticates, and changes sync in realtime across all active sessions. Enable teams in manifest.json under the auth property: manifest.json { "appwrite" : { ... "auth" : { ... "teams" : { } } } } If your app requires default teams be created automatically for all users, configure them in manifest.json . manifest.json { "appwrite" : { ... "auth" : { ... "teams" : { "permanent" : [ "Permanent Workspace" ] , "template" : [ "Template Workspace" , "Dream Team" ] } } } } Default teams are defined by their name within array objects: permanent : Permanent teams cannot be deleted by the user, such as a default personal workspace. template : Template teams can be deleted and reapplied by the user, such as demo workspaces. guests : Set to true to also seed these default teams for guest (anonymous) sessions. Off by default, so guests start with no teams. authenticated : Whether to seed these default teams for authenticated (signed-in) sessions. true by default. Set to false (with "guests": true ) to make seeding guest-only — a per-guest sandbox that is never minted for a signed-in user who already belongs to their real workspace. The user is the owner and only initial member of each default team. Depending on their role and permissions, the team can be modified and other members invited. Guests are full Appwrite sessions, so they can own teams. When "guests": true , a guest's default teams are created the moment their session starts. Pair this with guestUpgrade so those teams carry over when the guest later signs in (via magic link or OAuth) — otherwise they're left behind on the discarded guest account. For a guest-only sandbox (a demo workspace for anonymous visitors that signed-in users should never receive), combine "template" with "guests": true, "authenticated": false . Every user can generate custom teams, view all teams, and manage them with the respective permissions. Existing teams can also be duplicated, optionally cloning their members and roles to spin up a new workspace from a known configuration. Create Team List & Manage Teams <!-- Team name input --> < input type = "text" placeholder = "Team name" aria-label = "Team name" x-model = "$auth.newTeamName" :disabled = "$auth.isCreatingTeam()" /> <!-- Create button --> < button @ click = "$auth.createTeamFromName()" :disabled = "!$auth.newTeamName || $auth.isCreatingTeam()" > Create Team </ button > <!-- Add back deleted template teams --> < template x-for = "teamName in $auth.deletedTemplateTeams" :key = "teamName" > < button @ click = "$auth.reapplyTemplateTeam(teamName)" :disabled = "$auth.isCreatingTeam()" > Create < b x-text = "teamName" > </ b > Team </ button > </ template > <!-- List teams --> < template x-for = "team in $auth.teams" :key = "team.$id" > < div x-data = "{ editingTeamName: team.name }" > <!-- Team details --> < p x-text = "team.name" > Team name </ p > < small > ID: < b x-text = "team.$id" > </ b > </ small > < small > Created: < b x-text = "$auth.teamCreatedAt(team)" > </ b > </ small > < small > Modified: < b x-text = "$auth.teamUpdatedAt(team)" > </ b > </ small > <!-- Rename team --> < input type = "text" placeholder = "Insert name" aria-label = "Team name" class = "transparent hug w-fit rounded-none no-focus" onclick = "this.select()" x-model = "editingTeamName" :disabled = "!$auth.isTeamRenamable(team) || $auth.isUpdatingTeam(team.$id)" @ blur = "if (editingTeamName !== team.name && editingTeamName.trim()) { $auth.updateTeamName(team.$id, editingTeamName.trim()); }" @ keydown.enter = "$event.target.blur()" /> <!-- Delete team (enabled if user has the deleteTeam permission) --> < button class = "sm" @ click = "$auth.deleteTeam(team.$id)" :disabled = "$auth.isActionDisabled('deleteTeam') || !$auth.isTeamDeletable(team) || $auth.isDeletingTeam(team.$id)" aria-label = "Delete team" > Delete </ button > <!-- Duplicate team --> < button @ click = "$auth.duplicateTeam(team.$id, { newName: team.name + ' copy' })" > Duplicate </ button > <!-- Duplicate with members and roles --> < button @ click = "$auth.duplicateTeam(team.$id, { copyMembers: true, copyRoles: true })" > Duplicate with Members </ button > </ div > </ template > +14 You're not signed-in. Use one of the interactive examples above to sign in. Create Team No teams yet Roles & Permissions Without roles configured, every team member holds Appwrite's owner role, with full permission to manage the team and its members. To override this behaviour, define default roles and their permissions in manifest.json , which are made available to every new team. manifest.json { "appwrite" : { ... "auth" : { ... "roles" : { "permanent" : { "Admin" : [ "inviteMembers" , "updateMembers" , "removeMembers" , "manageRoles" , "renameTeam" , "deleteTeam" ] } , "template" : { "Editor" : [ "inviteMembers" ] , "Viewer" : [ ] } } , "creatorRole" : "Admin" } } } Like default teams, default roles are established by their name in one of two objects: Role Type Description permanent Permanent roles cannot be modified or deleted by anyone template Template roles can be modified and deleted by users with the manageRoles permission Each role can have permissions. Manifest provides these built-in permissions: Permission Description inviteMembers Invite new members to the team updateMembers Edit other members' roles removeMembers Remove members from the team manageRoles Create, rename, set permissions, and delete custom roles renameTeam Change the team name deleteTeam Delete the team Custom permissions can be added to the array with unique names, such as manageBilling . Check them in Alpine directives such as x-show with $auth.hasTeamPermissionSync('manageBilling') . Users can also generate custom permissions if you expose the inputs to do so. Role names can contain spaces or any characters, such as Live Agent . The creatorRole is the role assigned to the team creator. It must reference a role defined in the permanent or template roles. If the creatorRole property is absent or does not reference a defined role, the creator is assigned the first defined role. Owner-only creators Use creatorRoles (plural) for finer control over what the creator receives, assigned atomically as the team is created: Value Result [] or null Owner-only — the creator holds just Appwrite's intrinsic owner role, with no template role. Your template / permanent roles stay defined but unassigned, ready for invited members. "Admin" Assigns that single role. ["Admin", "Editor"] Assigns multiple roles. manifest.json { "appwrite" : { "auth" : { "roles" : { "template" : { "Admin" : [ "manageRoles" , "inviteMembers" ] , "Editor" : [ "inviteMembers" ] } } , "creatorRoles" : [ ] } } } creatorRoles takes precedence over creatorRole . When neither is set, the creator is assigned the first defined role. Owner-only is the safest choice for a creator who should have full, future-proof access: a member holding no custom role resolves to all permissions (including any you add later), so they can never be locked out. By contrast, assigning the creator a custom role scopes them to exactly that role's permissions — if you later edit that role down, the creator loses access too. Prefer creatorRoles: [] for owners; reserve named roles for invited members. Use await $auth.updateRolePermissions(teamId, roleName, ['manageBilling', ...]) — it persists straight to team prefs with a plain array and refreshes $auth.allTeamRoles() . Don't assign to $auth.editingRole.permissions programmatically: that object is reactive and is meant for x-model -bound inputs (as above). For a mid-edit flow, call $auth.setEditingPermissions([...]) then $auth.saveEditingRole() . Members Team members can be invited, updated, and removed, subject to the respective user permissions. Team State Property Type Description $auth.teams array Array of all user's teams $auth.currentTeam object | null Currently selected team $auth.currentTeamMemberships array Members of the current team $auth.deletedTemplateTeams array Array of deleted template team names (can be reapplied) Input Properties Team Inputs Property Type Description $auth.newTeamName string Input for creating teams $auth.updateTeamNameInput string Input for renaming teams Member Inputs Property Type Description $auth.inviteEmail string Input for member invitations $auth.inviteRoles array Array of selected roles for invitations Role Inputs Property Type Description $auth.newRoleName string Input for creating roles $auth.newRolePermissions array Array of selected permissions for roles $auth.allAvailablePermissions array Cached list of all available permissions $auth.editingRole object | null Current role being edited $auth.editingMember object | null Current member being edited Team Management Methods Method Parameters Description $auth.createTeamFromName() None Create a team using newTeamName property $auth.viewTeam(...) team (object) Load team details and memberships $auth.updateCurrentTeamName() None Update current team name using updateTeamNameInput property $auth.updateTeamName(...) teamId (string), name (string) Rename a team $auth.deleteTeam(...) teamId (string) Delete a team $auth.duplicateTeam(...) teamId (string), options (object, optional) Duplicate a team. Options: newName , copyMembers , copyRoles . Returns { success: boolean, team?: object, error?: string } . Defaults: copyMembers: false , copyRoles: false , newName: '{originalName} copy' $auth.reapplyTemplateTeam(...) teamName (string) Reapply a deleted template team Member Management Methods Method Parameters Description $auth.inviteToCurrentTeam() None Invite member using inviteEmail and inviteRoles properties $auth.inviteMember(...) teamId (string), roles (array), email (string) Invite a member by email. Returns { success, membership, normalized } ; normalized is true when the stored roles differ from those requested (for example, a role with owner-level permissions also gets Appwrite's owner role) $auth.updateMembership(...) teamId (string), membershipId (string), roles (array) Set a member's roles. Returns the same normalized flag as inviteMember $auth.startEditingMember(...) teamId (string), membershipId (string), currentRoles (array) Start editing a member $auth.saveEditingMember() None Save member edits $auth.cancelEditingMember() None Cancel member editing $auth.deleteMember(...) teamId (string), membershipId (string) Remove a member from team $auth.leaveTeam(...) teamId (string), membershipId (string) Leave a team (user removes themselves) Role Management Methods Method Parameters Description $auth.createRoleFromInputs(...) teamId (string) Create a role using newRoleName and newRolePermissions properties $auth.updateRolePermissions(...) teamId (string), roleName (string), permissions (array) Set a role's permissions directly (reactive-safe). Persists to team prefs and refreshes allTeamRoles() . Preferred for programmatic edits. $auth.startEditingRole(...) teamId (string), roleName (string) Start editing a role (for x-model -bound UI) $auth.setEditingPermissions(...) permissions (array) Set the in-progress edit's permissions safely (use with saveEditingRole() ) $auth.saveEditingRole() None Save role edits $auth.cancelEditingRole() None Cancel role editing $auth.deleteUserRole(...) teamId (string), roleName (string) Delete a role Permission & Role Checks Method Parameters Description $auth.hasTeamPermission(...) permission (string) Check if user has a team permission (async, for JavaScript; use hasTeamPermissionSync in bindings) $auth.hasTeamPermissionSync(...) permission (string) Check if user has a team permission (synchronous) $auth.hasRole(...) roleName (string) Check if user has a specific role $auth.getUserRole() None Get user's primary role (async) $auth.getUserRoles() None Get all user's roles (async) $auth.getCurrentTeamRoles() None Get current user's roles in current team $auth.isCurrentTeamOwner() None Check if user is owner of current team $auth.canManageRoles() None Check if user can manage roles $auth.canInviteMembers() None Check if user can invite members $auth.canUpdateMembers() None Check if user can update members $auth.canRemoveMembers() None Check if user can remove members $auth.isActionDisabled(...) permission (string) Check if an action is disabled (combines inProgress and permission check) Convenience Methods Method Parameters Description $auth.isTeamDeletable(...) team (object) Check if a team can be deleted $auth.isTeamRenamable(...) team (object) Check if a team can be renamed $auth.isTeamImmutable(...) teamId (string), async Resolves true if the team is configured as permanent (cannot be deleted or renamed) $auth.teamCreatedAt(...) team (object) Formatted creation date $auth.teamUpdatedAt(...) team (object) Formatted update date $auth.allTeamRoles(...) team (object, optional) Get all roles for a team $auth.getMemberDisplayName(...) membership (object) Get member display name $auth.getMemberEmail(...) membership (object) Get member email $auth.isRoleBeingEdited(...) teamId (string), roleName (string) Check if a role is being edited $auth.isRoleDeletable(...) teamId (string), roleName (string) Check if a role can be deleted $auth.isRolePermanentSync(...) teamId (string), roleName (string) Check if a role is permanent (synchronous). Returns false until the team's roles have loaded, such as after viewTeam Loading States Team Operations Method Parameters Description $auth.isUpdatingTeam(...) teamId (string) Check if a specific team is being updated. Returns true only for the team being updated, allowing other teams to remain interactive $auth.isDeletingTeam(...) teamId (string) Check if a specific team is being deleted. Returns true only for the team being deleted $auth.isCreatingTeam() None Check if a team is being created. Returns true when creating a new team $auth.isAnyTeamOperationInProgress() None Check if any team operation is in progress.
