## Cloud Data — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/framework/appwrite-modules/cloud-data

Cloud Data Access Appwrite databases and storage with the same $x API as local data . Setup Complete the Appwrite setup steps to connect your Appwrite and Manifest projects. Add the Appwrite SDK and manifest.js scripts to the HTML head. manifest.json is also required for Appwrite credentials and to register database tables or storage buckets. Auto-detect Declared <!-- Meta --> < link rel = "manifest" href = "/manifest.json" > <!-- Scripts --> < script src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/appwrite@latest" > </ script > < script src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mnfst@latest/lib/manifest.min.js" > </ script > <!-- Meta --> < link rel = "manifest" href = "/manifest.json" > <!-- Scripts --> < script src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/appwrite@latest" > </ script > < script src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mnfst@latest/lib/manifest.min.js" data-modules = "+appwrite-data" > </ script > If data-modules lists modules without the + prefix and leaves out the core data module (with its $x magic method), it is still loaded automatically to enable Appwrite database and storage operations in the frontend. Overview Appwrite's cloud data sources work identically to local data sources in the frontend, using the same $x magic method syntax. The module automatically handles authentication, permissions, and realtime updates. Key Features: Unified Syntax : Same $x.sourceName pattern for databases, storage, and local files Realtime Updates : Changes sync automatically across all active sessions Permission-Aware : Respects Appwrite permissions and scopes CRUD Operations : Create, read, update, and delete using intuitive methods Scoping : Automatically scope queries by user, current team, or all of the user's teams Who Sees What What a visitor can read depends on who they are: through scopes , $auth. queries, or the row and file permissions set in Appwrite. Identity changes reload sources. When someone signs in, signs out, or switches accounts (a guest signing in included), in any tab, every table and bucket source reloads for the new identity. The previous user's or guest's rows are cleared at once; rows read while signed out stay on screen until the new ones arrive. Unscoped sources follow Appwrite permissions. Tables and buckets without a scope or $auth. queries read whatever Appwrite allows, including rows and files open to everyone ( read("any") ) or to the guests role for signed-out visitors. When Appwrite refuses a signed-out visitor's table read outright, the source reports an "Authentication required" $error ; with row security on and no rows readable by guests, it settles empty with no $error . Scoped sources wait for a user. Scoped tables, and sources whose queries use $auth. values, stay empty until someone signs in. After an offline start , a persisted source keeps the rows saved for the user last signed in on this device until the session is checked. The prerender runs signed out. x-for lists over a table re-render from live rows at runtime; values bound directly (e.g. x-text ) and data-static lists keep the rows readable by any or guests as rendered until the next render and publish. Mark such an element with data-hydrate to keep it live. Cloud sources can keep their last rows on the visitor's device with the same persist option as any other source, so a return visit shows data before the network answers. See persisted data . How Data Updates The parts of the page that read $x.products follow only the products source. When one source updates — including a realtime change from another session — only the parts of the page that read it are refreshed; everything else is left alone. Rows keep their identity. When new data arrives for rows you already have, the existing rows are updated in place, so lists don't flicker and edits you are making are not disturbed. Fields you add to a row yourself (a _pending flag on a placeholder, say) survive too — the network never sends them, so nothing clears them for you; clear them explicitly once the real data has landed. Your own changes show immediately. $create , $update , $delete and direct assignments appear on the page at once, even while data is still arriving from the network. Until Appwrite confirms a change, it stays on screen through any reload or update that arrives meanwhile, and data fetched before the change never shows the old values again, even when it arrives after Appwrite confirms. $x.products.$saving(id) is true while a row has a change waiting, and $x.products.$pending counts those rows. If Appwrite refuses a change, it is undone: a failed update restores only the fields it changed (unless someone else has changed them since), back to their values before any of your unconfirmed changes, a failed delete puts the row back where it was, and a failed create removes its placeholder. The call rejects, $error is set, and the window receives a manifest:data-mutation-error event with { type, dataSourceName, entryId, error } . Network updates are batched. Many arriving at once are applied together, once per frame. $x.products is the same array every time you read it until the source changes, then a new one, so results computed from it can be kept against the array itself. Failed loads are retried before $error shows, and $x.products.$reload() fetches the source again, both as for local sources . On a cloud source, $reload() keeps an active $query and, on a paged source , as many rows as are loaded. If a source was loaded before, you see its cached rows immediately while fresh data loads. $x.products.$stale is true until the fresh data has landed, and $x.products.$fresh is a promise that resolves at that moment, for a single reveal. A reload keeps the rows on screen and merges the fresh data in place; a failed reload keeps the old rows and sets $error . Identical concurrent loads make one request. < small x-show = "$x.products.$stale" > Refreshing… </ small > Rendering Untrusted Content Cloud data is the case where Manifest's default-permissive rendering deserves a second thought: the values in an Appwrite table can be written by your end users (reviews, comments, bios, uploaded SVGs, etc.), not just by you. For those cases, prefer the safe variants when rendering into HTML or SVG sinks: Source Default render Safe opt-in User-submitted markdown <div x-markdown="$x.comments.body"> <div x-markdown.safe="$x.comments.body"> User-uploaded SVG <span x-svg="$x.profile.avatar"> <span x-svg.safe="$x.profile.avatar"> x-text , attribute bindings ( :href , :src , :alt ), toasts, tooltips, and the standard Alpine x-show / x-if always treat values as data — they're safe by default. The .safe opt-ins exist for the HTML/SVG sinks where the default has to be permissive so authors can render their own rich content. Next Steps Complete cloud data support using the guides for: Databases of cloud-hosted content Storage of cloud-hosted files


## Databases — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/framework/appwrite-modules/databases

Databases Query and manage Appwrite database tables. Appwrite Configuration In your Appwrite project's Databases dashboard, create a database. The database must have at least one table. Add columns to the table matching your data structure. Appwrite automatically applies $id , $createdAt , and $updatedAt columns to every table. In the example above, we've established a table that will store fictitious "projects". To scope rows to users or teams, also add a userId and/or teamId string column. Manifest fills them in on $create . The examples on this page use a table with name , type , userId and teamId string columns. In a table's Settings tab, ensure any permissions required by your frontend user experience ( Create , Read , Update , Delete ) are checked. Register Database Tables Register database tables in your manifest.json under the data property, same as local data files . Include the appwriteDatabaseId and appwriteTableId values provided by Appwrite. manifest.json { "data" : { "projects" : { "appwriteDatabaseId" : "your-database-id" , "appwriteTableId" : "your-table-id" } } , "appwrite" : { "projectId" : "your-project-id" , "endpoint" : "your-API-endpoint" } } In this example, the "projects" data source name is arbitrary, used to later reference table content in the frontend. An Appwrite data source will automatically reference the appwrite property for credentials. appwriteDatabaseId falls back to appwrite.databaseId , then to main , so later examples omit it. Appwrite returns 25 rows when a request sets no limit, so a table source without a limit query shows at most 25 rows. Add a ["limit", N] query to its queries to load more, or set paging to load every row or a window you extend as people scroll. Scope Scoping automatically filters queries by user or team, ensuring users only see data they're permitted to access. Configure scope in manifest.json : manifest.json { "data" : { "projects" : { "appwriteTableId" : "your-table-id" , "scope" : "user" } } } Scope options are: Scope Description Column Used "user" Single user's data userId "team" Current team's data teamId "teams" All teams user belongs to teamId ["user", "team"] User's data OR current team's data userId OR teamId ["user", "teams"] User's data OR any team's data userId OR teamId Scope queries are always prepended to user queries, ensuring scope restrictions cannot be bypassed. By default scope filters on the userId / teamId columns. If your table names them differently (e.g. a workspaceId column), set scopeColumn : manifest.json { "data" : { "projects" : { "appwriteTableId" : "your-table-id" , "scope" : "team" , "scopeColumn" : "workspaceId" } } } scopeColumn can also be an object to name the user and team columns independently: { "team": "workspaceId", "user": "ownerId" } . When using ["user", "team"] scope, projects are shown for the current user OR the current team. If no team is selected ( $auth.currentTeam ), only user-scoped projects will display. Use "teams" (plural) instead of "team" (singular) to query all teams the user belongs to, not just the current team. Signed out. While no user is signed in, a scoped table (or one whose queries reference $auth. values) settles as empty: the source is [] , $ready is true , and no request is sent. It loads when the user signs in. An offline start is the exception: a persisted table keeps the rows saved for the user last signed in on this device until the session is checked. Like every table source, it reloads whenever the identity changes, so one user's entries never carry over to the next (see cloud data and session recovery ). All interactive examples below require you to be logged into a dummy account via the users article. The data entries you generate below use the team scope. Display & Manage Entries Database tables work identically to local data sources. Access entries using the $x magic method and perform all CRUD operations. Team-scoped rows are read and created for $auth.currentTeam , so the "All" example first selects the user's permanent team : All Display Create Update Duplicate Delete <!-- Manage projects for permanent team --> < div x-data = "{ permanentTeam: null, newName: '' }" x-effect = "(async () => { if (permanentTeam || !$auth.teams || $auth.teams.length === 0) return; for (const team of $auth.teams) { if (await $auth.isTeamImmutable(team.$id)) { permanentTeam = team; $auth.currentTeam = team; $auth.viewTeam(team); break; } } })()" > < div class = "col" > <!-- Create --> < div class = "row-wrap gap-2 mb-2" > < input type = "text" placeholder = "Project name" aria-label = "Project name" x-model = "newName" :disabled = "!$auth.currentTeam" class = "flex-1" /> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$create({ name: newName, type: 'demo' }).then(() => { newName = ''; })" :disabled = "!newName || !$auth.currentTeam || $x.projects.$error" > Create </ button > </ div > <!-- List with inline edit, duplicate, and delete --> < template x-for = "project in $x.projects" :key = "project.$id" > < div class = "row gap-2 py-1 items-center border-t border-line" > < input type = "text" :value = "project.name" @ blur = "$x.projects.$update(project.$id, { name: $event.target.value })" class = "ghost flex-1" /> < button class = "sm" @ click = "$x.projects.$duplicate(project.$id, { files: 'same' })" x-icon = "lucide:copy" aria-label = "Duplicate" title = "Duplicate" > </ button > < button class = "sm" @ click = "$x.projects.$delete(project.$id)" x-icon = "lucide:trash" aria-label = "Delete" title = "Delete" > </ button > </ div > </ template > < small x-show = "!$x.projects || $x.projects.length === 0" class = "text-content-subtle" > No projects yet </ small > </ div > </ div > < small x-show = "!$auth.teams || $auth.teams.length === 0" class = "text-content-subtle" > No teams available </ small > <!-- Display all entries --> < template x-for = "project in $x.projects" :key = "project.$id" > < p x-text = "project.name" > </ p > </ template > <!-- Display single entry --> < p x-text = "$x.projects[0]?.name" > </ p > <!-- Display within teams ("scope": "teams") --> < template x-for = "team in $auth.teams" :key = "team.$id" > < div > < p x-text = "team.name" > </ p > < template x-for = "project in $x.projects.filter(p => p.teamId === team.$id)" :key = "project.$id" > < p x-text = "project.name" > </ p > </ template > </ div > </ template > <!-- Basic create --> < div x-data = "{ newName: '' }" > < input type = "text" placeholder = "Project name" aria-label = "Project name" x-model = "newName" /> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$create({ name: newName }).then(() => { newName = ''; })" > Create Project </ button > </ div > <!-- With explicit ID --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$create({ name: 'My Project' }, 'custom-id')" > Create with Custom ID </ button > <!-- Single update (on blur) --> < template x-for = "project in $x.projects" :key = "project.$id" > < input type = "text" :value = "project.name" @ blur = "$x.projects.$update(project.$id, { name: $event.target.value })" /> </ template > <!-- Batch update --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$update( [$x.projects[0].$id, $x.projects[1].$id], { status: 'archived' } )" > Archive Selected </ button > <!-- Duplicate entry with same file references --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$duplicate(project.$id, { files: 'same' })" > Duplicate </ button > <!-- Duplicate entry and duplicate all files --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$duplicate(project.$id, { files: 'duplicate' })" > Duplicate with Files </ button > <!-- Duplicate entry without file references --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$duplicate(project.$id, { files: 'none' })" > Duplicate (No Files) </ button > <!-- Duplicate with custom name and file handling --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$duplicate(project.$id, { name: project.name + ' Copy', files: 'same' })" > Duplicate with Custom Name </ button > <!-- Single delete --> < template x-for = "project in $x.projects" :key = "project.$id" > < div > < p x-text = "project.name" > </ p > < button @ click = "$x.projects.$delete(project.$id)" > Delete </ button > </ div > </ template > <!-- Batch delete --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$delete([project1.$id, project2.$id])" > Delete Selected </ button > Create No projects yet No teams available Database tables automatically sync changes in realtime across all active sessions. When one user creates, updates, or deletes an entry, all other users see the change immediately without page refresh. All live features share one connection per tab; see Realtime Options to filter or cap live updates. Method details: Method Parameters Description $create(data, rowId?) data (object), rowId (string, optional) Create a new entry. Returns created entry. If scope is configured, userId and/or teamId are automatically injected $update(idOrArray, data) idOrArray (string, object, or array), data (object) Update entry(ies). Returns updated entry(ies) $duplicate(entryId, options?) entryId (string or object with $id ), options (object, optional) Duplicate an entry. Options: files , newRowId , and any field overrides. Returns duplicated entry. The files option controls file handling: 'duplicate' (create new files), 'same' (share file references, default), or 'none' (remove file references) $delete(idOrArray) idOrArray (string, object, or array) Delete entry(ies). Returns deleted entry(ies) Search & Query Entries Use $query to filter and sort entries in Appwrite, and $search to filter rows already loaded in the browser. $query refetches from Appwrite and replaces the source's rows, so every place that shows $x.projects changes; $query([]) restores the list with only its scope applied; $query('default') returns to the configured default query. All Key Search Query < div x-data = "{ searchTerm: '', sortBy: 'newest' }" class = "col gap-4" > <!-- Search Input --> < input type = "text" placeholder = "Search projects..." x-model = "searchTerm" class = "w-full" /> <!-- Sort Buttons --> < div class = "row-wrap gap-2" > < button @ click = "sortBy = 'newest'; $x.projects.$query([['orderDesc', '$createdAt']])" > Sort by Newest </ button > < button @ click = "sortBy = 'name'; $x.projects.$query([['orderAsc', 'name']])" > Sort by Name </ button > < button @ click = "sortBy = 'all'; searchTerm = ''; $x.projects.$query([])" > Show All </ button > </ div > <!-- Results List --> < div class = "col gap-2" > < template x-for = "project in $x.projects.$search(searchTerm, 'name')" :key = "project.$id" > < div class = "p-2 bg-surface-2 rounded" > < p x-text = "project.name" > </ p > </ div > </ template > < small x-show = "!$x.projects || $x.projects.$search(searchTerm, 'name').length === 0" class = "text-content-subtle" > No projects found </ small > </ div > </ div > <!-- Text search: filters data already loaded in browser (no network request) --> < input type = "text" placeholder = "Search..." x-model = "searchTerm" /> < template x-for = "project in $x.projects.$search(searchTerm, 'name')" :key = "project.$id" > < div x-text = "project.name" > </ div > </ template > <!-- Filter, sort, limit: sends query to Appwrite backend, returns filtered results --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$query([ ['equal', 'status', 'active'], ['orderDesc', '$createdAt'] ])" > Load Active Projects </ button > Sort by Newest Sort by Name Reset No projects found Query Syntax These are Appwrite query methods. Each query is an array with the format ['method', 'attribute', 'value'] . Use these patterns to build query arrays: Query Methods: Category Method Format Example Comparison equal ['equal', 'attribute', 'value'] ['equal', 'status', 'active'] notEqual ['notEqual', 'attribute', 'value'] ['notEqual', 'status', 'archived'] greaterThan ['greaterThan', 'attribute', value] ['greaterThan', 'priority', 5] greaterThanOrEqual ['greaterThanOrEqual', 'attribute', value] ['greaterThanOrEqual', 'priority', 5] lessThan ['lessThan', 'attribute', value] ['lessThan', '$createdAt', '2024-01-01'] lessThanOrEqual ['lessThanOrEqual', 'attribute', value] ['lessThanOrEqual', '$createdAt', '2024-01-01'] between ['between', 'attribute', min, max] ['between', 'price', 10, 50] Null Checks isNull ['isNull', 'attribute'] ['isNull', 'deletedAt'] isNotNull ['isNotNull', 'attribute'] ['isNotNull', 'email'] String Operations contains ['contains', 'attribute', 'value'] ['contains', 'name', 'keyword'] startsWith ['startsWith', 'attribute', 'value'] ['startsWith', 'name', 'prefix'] endsWith ['endsWith', 'attribute', 'value'] ['endsWith', 'name', 'suffix'] search ['search', 'attribute', 'value'] ['search', 'name', 'keyword'] (requires fulltext index) Sorting orderAsc ['orderAsc', 'attribute'] ['orderAsc', '$createdAt'] orderDesc ['orderDesc', 'attribute'] ['orderDesc', '$updatedAt'] orderRandom ['orderRandom'] ['orderRandom'] Pagination limit ['limit', number] ['limit', 10] offset ['offset', number] ['offset', 20] cursorAfter ['cursorAfter', 'rowId'] ['cursorAfter', lastId] cursorBefore ['cursorBefore', 'rowId'] ['cursorBefore', firstId] Logic or ['or', [query, query, ...]] ['or', [['equal', 'status', 'active'], ['equal', 'status', 'draft']]] // Comparison operators [ 'equal' , 'status' , 'active' ] // status equals 'active' [ 'notEqual' , 'status' , 'archived' ] // status does not equal 'archived' [ 'greaterThan' , 'priority' , 5 ] // priority greater than 5 [ 'greaterThanOrEqual' , 'priority' , 5 ] // priority greater than or equal to 5 [ 'lessThan' , '$createdAt' , '2024-01-01' ] // createdAt before date [ 'lessThanOrEqual' , '$createdAt' , '2024-01-01' ] // createdAt before or equal to date [ 'between' , 'price' , 10 , 50 ] // price between 10 and 50 (inclusive) // Null checks [ 'isNull' , 'deletedAt' ] // deletedAt is null [ 'isNotNull' , 'email' ] // email is not null // String operations [ 'contains' , 'name' , 'keyword' ] // name contains 'keyword' [ 'startsWith' , 'name' , 'prefix' ] // name starts with 'prefix' [ 'endsWith' , 'name' , 'suffix' ] // name ends with 'suffix' [ 'search' , 'name' , 'keyword' ] // Full-text search (requires fulltext index) // Sorting [ 'orderAsc' , '$createdAt' ] // Sort ascending by createdAt [ 'orderDesc' , '$updatedAt' ] // Sort descending by updatedAt [ 'orderRandom' ] // Random order // Pagination [ 'limit' , 10 ] // Return maximum 10 results [ 'offset' , 20 ] // Skip first 20 results [ 'cursorAfter' , lastId] // Rows after this row ID // Either condition [ 'or' , [[ 'equal' , 'status' , 'active' ], [ 'equal' , 'status' , 'draft' ]]] // Combine multiple queries (all applied together with AND logic) [ [ 'equal' , 'status' , 'active' ], [ 'orderDesc' , '$createdAt' ], [ 'limit' , 20 ] ] See Appwrite's query documentation for the complete list of query methods and operators. Reusable Queries Define reusable queries in manifest.json and reference them in HTML: manifest.json HTML { "data" : { "projects" : { "appwriteTableId" : "your-table-id" , "queries" : { "default" : [ [ "orderDesc" , "$createdAt" ] ] , "active" : [ [ "equal" , "status" , "active" ] , [ "orderDesc" , "$createdAt" ] ] , "recent" : [ [ "orderDesc" , "$createdAt" ] , [ "limit" , 10 ] ] } } } } <!-- Reference a query defined in manifest.json by name --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$query('active')" > Load Active Projects </ button > A query value can also reference the signed-in user or the active locale. Only these values are allowed: $auth.user.$id (or $auth.userId ), $auth.currentTeam.$id (or .id ), $auth.session.$id (or .id ) and $locale.current . Any other path resolves to an empty string. manifest.json { "data" : { "projects" : { "appwriteTableId" : "your-table-id" , "queries" : { "default" : [ [ "equal" , "workspaceId" , "$auth.currentTeam.$id" ] ] } } } } If the referenced value isn't available yet (auth still loading, no current team selected), the read is skipped rather than sent with a broken value — it retries automatically once auth settles. queries is either an array, applied at load, or an object of named queries whose default key is applied at load; the others run when you call $query('name') . Scope applies to both. An unknown name throws instead of loading unfiltered. $query replaces the source's rows with its result, and $loading is true while it runs. If its queries use a $auth. value that isn't available yet, it waits for sign-in to settle and then runs, and after a sign-in a source showing a $query shows it again for the signed-in user. If you call it again before an earlier call returns, only the latest call's rows land, so a fast filter change never shows a slower, older result. Until the next default load, realtime events and the pagination methods follow the active $query : its filters decide which live rows join, and its order decides where they go. Large Tables Set paging on a table source to go past one request's rows. Every page lands in $x.<source> like any other load, so realtime, $query , persistence and $stale all keep working. manifest.json { "data" : { "teams" : { "appwriteTableId" : "teams" , "queries" : [ [ "orderAsc" , "name" ] ] , "paging" : "all" } , "contacts" : { "appwriteTableId" : "contacts" , "queries" : [ [ "orderDesc" , "$createdAt" ] ] , "paging" : { "mode" : "window" , "size" : 100 } } } } Option Default Description mode – "all" loads every row, page by page, up to max . "window" loads size rows; $more() adds the next page. A string value sets the mode with the defaults. size 100 Rows per request, up to 4999 max 5000 The most rows the source holds through paging Use "all" for tables that stay small enough to hold in the browser, like settings, teams or tags. Use "window" for tables that grow without bound, like contacts, messages or orders: people scroll, and the source loads more as they reach the end. $x.<source>.$more() loads the next page after the rows already held, and resolves with the number of rows added. Calling it again while a page is loading returns the same request, and calling it while a reload or $query is in flight loads the next page once that lands (that call resolves with 0). $hasMore says whether $more() can load another page: it turns false at the end of the table or at max . $total is Appwrite's count of matching rows, so $total above the number of rows held at max means more exist; Appwrite stops counting at 5000, so when $totalCapped is true show it as "5000+". Virtual lists fire virtual-end when the last loaded row is shown, which is the moment to ask for more: < div x-virtual class = "h-[600px] overflow-auto" @ virtual-end = "$x.contacts.$more()" > < template x-for = "contact in $x.contacts" :key = "contact.$id" > < p x-text = "contact.name" > </ p > </ template > </ div > < small x-show = "$x.contacts.$hasMore" > < span x-text = "$x.contacts.length" > </ span > of < span x-text = "$x.contacts.$totalCapped ? '5000+' : $x.contacts.$total" > </ span > </ small > $query on a paged source starts the new filter at its first window (or loads all of it), and $more() then continues within that filter. A limit in the queries is ignored, because paging sets its own. Live updates follow the rows you have loaded. A new row that sorts within them appears in its place; one that sorts after the last loaded row, or any new row on an unsorted source, arrives with the page that contains it while more pages remain. A loaded row whose sort value changes past the last loaded row leaves until its page loads. Rows you create yourself always appear straight away, in sort order. Paged sources aren't capped by the realtime growth limit, since paging already bounds them; set realtime.maxRows to cap them anyway. After the connection comes back, the source fetches again as many rows as it held. Storage File References Database entries can reference files stored in Appwrite storage buckets, such as a project (the entry) with files. When duplicating entries, you can control how file references are handled. Linking Files to Entries Files are linked to entries via a fileIds column (or custom column name) that stores an array of file IDs: manifest.json { "data" : { "projects" : { "appwriteTableId" : "your-table-id" , "storage" : { "assets" : "fileIds" } } , "assets" : { "appwriteBucketId" : "your-bucket-id" } } } The storage property maps bucket names to column names. In this example, files from the assets bucket are stored in the fileIds column. File Reference Options When duplicating an entry with $duplicate , use the files option to control file handling: <!-- 'same' (default): Share file references with original entry --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$duplicate(project.$id, { files: 'same' })" > Duplicate (Share Files) </ button > <!-- 'duplicate': Create new copies of all files --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$duplicate(project.$id, { files: 'duplicate' })" > Duplicate (Copy Files) </ button > <!-- 'none': Remove all file references --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$duplicate(project.$id, { files: 'none' })" > Duplicate (No Files) </ button > File handling options: Option Description Use Case 'same' New entry shares the same file references as the original Templates, drafts, or when files don't need to be copied 'duplicate' Creates new copies of all files and links them to the new entry When you need independent file copies 'none' Removes all file references from the duplicated entry When duplicating structure without files Accessing Entry Files Use the $files property to access files linked to an entry: <!-- Display files for an entry --> < template x-for = "file in project.$files" :key = "file.$id" > < div > < img x-show = "file.$isImage" :src = "file.$thumbnailUrl" :alt = "file.name" /> < p x-text = "file.name" > </ p > </ div > </ template > <!-- Check if entry has files --> < small x-show = "!project.$files || project.$files.length === 0" > No files attached </ small > See storage for more details on file management. Properties Entry Properties Each database entry includes standard Appwrite properties plus your table columns: Property Type Description $id string Unique identifier $createdAt string Creation timestamp (ISO format) $updatedAt string Last update timestamp (ISO format) $files array Files linked to the entry (if storage is configured) Custom columns varies All columns defined in your Appwrite table <!-- Access entry properties --> < div x-text = "project.$id" > </ div > <!-- Unique identifier --> < div x-text = "project.$createdAt" > </ div > <!-- Creation timestamp (ISO) --> < div x-text = "project.$updatedAt" > </ div > <!-- Last update timestamp (ISO) --> < div x-text = "project.name" > </ div > <!-- Your table columns --> State Properties Check data source loading state, errors, and readiness: Property Type Description $loading boolean Indicates if data is currently being loaded $error string | null Error message if an operation failed (null if no error) $ready boolean Indicates if the source has settled: loaded at least once, or resolved as empty because its scope can't apply (signed out, or no team) $pending number Rows with a change still waiting for Appwrite to confirm it $saving(id) boolean Whether that row has a change waiting for Appwrite $hasMore boolean Paged sources : $more() can load another page $total number | null Paged sources : Appwrite's count of matching rows $totalCapped boolean Paged sources : the count reached Appwrite's limit of 5000, so there may be more <!-- Loading state --> < small x-show = "$x.projects.$loading" > Loading projects... </ small > <!-- Error state --> < small x-show = "$x.projects.$error" x-text = "$x.projects.$error" class = "text-negative-content" > </ small > <!-- A row's save in progress --> < template x-for = "project in $x.projects" :key = "project.$id" > < p x-text = "project.name + ($x.projects.$saving(project.$id) ? ' · saving' : '')" > </ p > </ template > <!-- Ready state --> < small x-show = "$x.projects.$ready && !$x.projects.$loading" > Projects loaded: < b x-text = "$x.projects.length" > </ b > </ small > A source can be $ready with no entries because its scope can't apply yet (signed out, or no team), so check $auth.isAuthenticated to tell a signed-out visitor apart from a user with no entries. CRUD Methods $create $update $duplicate $delete <!-- Create single entry --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$create({ name: 'New Project' })" > Create </ button > <!-- Create with custom ID --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$create({ name: 'Project' }, 'custom-id')" > Create with ID </ button > <!-- Update single entry --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$update(project.$id, { name: 'Updated' })" > Update </ button > <!-- Update multiple entries with the same change --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$update([id1, id2], { status: 'archived' })" > Archive Selected </ button > <!-- Update multiple entries with different changes --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$update([{ id: id1, data: { rank: 1 } }, { id: id2, data: { rank: 2 } }])" > Reorder </ button > <!-- Duplicate entry with same file references (default) --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$duplicate(project.$id)" > Duplicate </ button > <!-- Duplicate entry and duplicate all files --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$duplicate(project.$id, { files: 'duplicate' })" > Duplicate with Files </ button > <!-- Duplicate entry without file references --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$duplicate(project.$id, { files: 'none' })" > Duplicate (No Files) </ button > <!-- Duplicate with field overrides --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$duplicate(project.$id, { name: project.name + ' Copy', status: 'draft', files: 'same' })" > Duplicate as Draft </ button > <!-- Delete single entry --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$delete(project.$id)" > Delete </ button > <!-- Delete multiple entries --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$delete([id1, id2])" > Delete Selected </ button > Query & Search Methods $query $search <!-- Query with filters and sorting --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$query([ ['equal', 'status', 'active'], ['orderDesc', '$createdAt'] ])" > Load Active </ button > <!-- Use pre-configured query --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$query('active')" > Load Active </ button > <!-- Frontend text search --> < input x-model = "searchTerm" /> < template x-for = "project in $x.projects.$search(searchTerm, 'name')" > < div x-text = "project.name" > </ div > </ template > Query & Search Methods: Method Parameters Description $query(queriesOrName) queriesOrName (array or string) Query entries with filters, sorting, and pagination. Accepts an array of query arrays or a pre-configured query name from manifest.json . Replaces the source's rows with the result $search(term, ...fields) term (string), fields (one or more strings, or a weights object like { title: 3, body: 1 } ) Frontend text search. Filters data already loaded in browser (no network request). Returns filtered array Pagination Methods $first $next $page <!-- Get first page (cursor-based) --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$first(10).then(result => { console.log(result.items); // Array of entries console.log(result.cursor); // Cursor for next page console.log(result.total); // Total count console.log(result.hasMore); // Boolean })" > Load First Page </ button > <!-- Get next page (cursor-based) --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$next(cursor, 10).then(result => { // Same structure as $first })" > Load Next Page </ button > <!-- Get specific page (offset-based) --> < button @ click = "$x.projects.$page(2, 10).then(result => { console.log(result.items); // Array of entries console.log(result.page); // Current page number console.log(result.total); // Total count console.log(result.totalPages); // Total pages console.log(result.hasMore); // Boolean })" > Load Page 2 </ button > Pagination Methods: Method Parameters Description $first(limit?) limit (number, default 10 ) Get first page (cursor-based). Returns { items, cursor, total, hasMore } $next(cursor, limit?) cursor (string), limit (number, default 10 ) Get the page after cursor . Returns { items, cursor, total, hasMore } $prev(cursor, limit?) cursor (string), limit (number, default 10 ) Get the page before cursor . Returns { items, cursor, total, hasMore } $page(pageNumber, limit?) pageNumber (number), limit (number, default 10 ) Get specific page (offset-based). Returns { items, page, total, totalPages, hasMore } Pages use the active $query if one is set, otherwise the source's default queries, with their own limit and position in place of any in the queries. hasMore says whether another page exists in that direction: after the last page it is false , and for $prev it is false once you reach the start. Page results are returned to you; they don't replace $x.<source> and don't receive realtime updates. total is Appwrite's count, which Appwrite caps (5000 by default). Realtime Options Realtime is multiplexed over one connection per tab: however many data sources subscribe, Manifest opens a single Appwrite Realtime client and one channel subscription per distinct table or bucket. Sources sharing a table each receive every event once. The auth module's team and account subscriptions and presence share the same connection, so N live features still count as one connection against your Appwrite plan. Where the project's Appwrite version supports Realtime queries (Web SDK 22.4+, server 1.8+), Manifest also filters events server-side by your scope configuration — Appwrite then only delivers (and bills) events in your scope — while your own queries continue filtering client-side, preserving instant removal of rows that stop matching. Set realtime: { "serverFilter": "all" } to push all expressible filters server-side (rows that stop matching then drop on the next load instead of instantly), or "serverFilter": false for no server filtering. Filters Appwrite can't evaluate in realtime ( search , contains , pagination and ordering) always stay client-side, and Manifest's event matcher runs in every mode as defense in depth. Events are filtered by the source's own queries before touching $x : a created or updated row that doesn't match the configured filters is ignored (or removed if it stops matching). Filters that can't be evaluated client-side ( search , unresolved $auth. values) are treated as matching, so live data is never silently dropped. Growth is bounded by default. Realtime appends stop at max(500, 2× the initially loaded rows); skipped events are counted in $x.<source>.$realtimeOverflow (reset on each load), so a UI can show "N new rows — refresh". Configure per source with a realtime key on the data source: Value Behavior (omitted) Subscribed; append mode, cap max(500, 2× initial rows) false No realtime subscription for this source { "mode": "append", "maxRows": 200 } Appends until 200 rows, then counts overflow { "mode": "window" } Holds the initial window size (the limit query if present), evicting the oldest realtime-appended rows first — initially loaded rows are never evicted. A window that is already full admits no live appends; watch $realtimeOverflow and reload to pull new rows into the window. { "mode": "append", "maxRows": 0 } Legacy unbounded growth (explicit opt-in; ignored in window mode, which falls back to the default cap) Updates and deletes to rows already held always apply, regardless of caps. On a sorted source (an orderAsc or orderDesc query), live rows join at their sort position and a row whose sort value changes moves to its new place; unsorted sources add live rows at the end. A row you create appears once, whether its realtime event arrives before or after Appwrite's reply. Events sent while the browser is offline or asleep are not replayed by Appwrite. When the connection comes back, or the tab returns after a minute or more in the background, live sources fetch again (the active $query , if one is set) and merge the result into the existing rows. For advanced programmatic control, window.ManifestDataRealtime.setFilter('<source>', (eventType, row) => boolean) runs per event per source before any merge work; return false to drop the event, pass null to clear. Next Steps See storage for managing file uploads and downloads.


## Storage — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/framework/appwrite-modules/storage

Storage Upload, view, and download files from Appwrite storage buckets. Appwrite Configuration In your Appwrite project's Storage dashboard, create a bucket. Within a bucket you can see its files and configure settings like allowed file types, maximum file size, encryption, and antivirus scanning. In a bucket's Settings tab, ensure any permissions required by your frontend user experience ( Create , Read , Update , Delete ) are checked. Register Storage Buckets Register storage buckets in your manifest.json under the data property, same as local data files and database tables . Include the appwriteBucketId value provided by Appwrite. manifest.json { "data" : { "assets" : { "appwriteBucketId" : "your-bucket-id" } } , "appwrite" : { "projectId" : "your-project-id" , "endpoint" : "your-API-endpoint" } } In this example, the "assets" data source name is arbitrary, used to later reference bucket content in the frontend. An Appwrite data source will automatically reference the appwrite property for credentials. Scope Scoping automatically filters file access by user or team, ensuring users only see files they're permitted to access. Configure scope in manifest.json : manifest.json { "data" : { "assets" : { "appwriteBucketId" : "your-bucket-id" , "scope" : "user" } } } Scope options are: Scope Description Permission Used "user" Single user's files User permissions "team" Current team's files Team permissions "teams" All teams user belongs to Team permissions ["user", "team"] User's files OR current team's files User OR team permissions ["user", "teams"] User's files OR any team's files User OR team permissions Scope filters are applied when listing files, ensuring users only see files they have permission to access based on Appwrite's permission system. When using ["user", "team"] scope, files are shown for the current user OR the current team. If no team is selected ( $auth.currentTeam ), only user-scoped files will display. Use "teams" (plural) instead of "team" (singular) to query all teams the user belongs to, not just the current team. Signed out. A bucket whose queries reference $auth. values settles as empty ( [] , $ready true ) without a request while no user is signed in, and loads on sign-in; after an offline start , a persisted bucket keeps the files saved for the user last signed in on this device while the listing can't be reached, until the session is checked; a scope-only bucket that is reachable before the session is verified can list as empty. A scope alone does not hold back the listing: the files are still requested, and any returned are filtered out. Like every bucket source, it reloads whenever the identity changes, so one user's files never carry over to the next (see cloud data and session recovery ). All interactive examples below require you to be logged into a dummy account via the users article. The files you generate below use the team scope. Display & Manage Files Storage buckets work identically to local data sources and database tables. Access files using the $x magic method and perform all CRUD operations. Team-scoped files are uploaded for $auth.currentTeam , so the "All" example first selects the user's permanent team : All Display Upload View & Download Duplicate Delete <!-- Manage files --> < div x-data = "{ permanentTeam: null }" x-effect = "(async () => { if (permanentTeam || !$auth.teams || $auth.teams.length === 0) return; for (const team of $auth.teams) { if (await $auth.isTeamImmutable(team.$id)) { permanentTeam = team; $auth.currentTeam = team; $auth.viewTeam(team); break; } } })()" > < div class = "col" > <!-- Upload --> < div class = "row-wrap gap-2 mb-2" > < label role = "button" class = "flex-1" > < input type = "file" @ change = "if ($event.target.files.length > 0) { $x.assets.$create($event.target.files[0]).then(() => { $event.target.value = ''; }).catch(err => $toast.negative('Upload failed: ' + err.message)); }" accept = "*/*" /> < span > Choose File </ span > </ label > </ div > <!-- List with actions --> < template x-for = "file in $x.assets" :key = "file.$id" > < div class = "row gap-2 py-1 items-center border-t border-line" > < div class = "flex-1 col gap-1" > < figcaption class = "text-sm font-semibold" x-text = "file.name || 'Unnamed file'" > </ figcaption > < small class = "text-content-subtle" x-text = "file.$formattedSize" > </ small > </ div > < button class = "sm" @ click = "$x.assets.$openUrl(file.$id)" x-icon = "lucide:external-link" aria-label = "View" title = "View" > </ button > < button class = "sm" @ click = "$x.assets.$duplicate(file.$id)" x-icon = "lucide:copy" aria-label = "Duplicate" title = "Duplicate" > </ button > < button class = "sm" @ click = "if (confirm('Delete ' + file.name + '?')) { $x.assets.$delete(file.$id); }" x-icon = "lucide:trash" aria-label = "Delete" title = "Delete" > </ button > </ div > </ template > < small x-show = "!$x.assets || $x.assets.length === 0" class = "text-content-subtle" > No files yet </ small > </ div > </ div > < small x-show = "!$auth.teams || $auth.teams.length === 0" class = "text-content-subtle" > No teams available </ small > <!-- Display all files --> < template x-for = "file in $x.assets" :key = "file.$id" > < div > < p x-text = "file.name" > </ p > < small x-text = "file.$formattedSize" > </ small > </ div > </ template > <!-- Display single file --> < div x-show = "$x.assets && $x.assets.length > 0" > < p x-text = "$x.assets[0].name" > </ p > < img x-show = "$x.assets[0].$isImage" :src = "$x.assets[0].$thumbnailUrl" :alt = "$x.assets[0].name" /> </ div > <!-- Display image files only --> < template x-for = "file in $x.assets" :key = "file.$id" > < img x-show = "file.$isImage" :src = "file.$thumbnailUrl" :alt = "file.name" /> </ template > <!-- Basic upload --> < label role = "button" > < input type = "file" @ change = "if ($event.target.files.length > 0) { $x.assets.$create($event.target.files[0]); }" accept = "*/*" /> < span > Upload with Custom ID </ span > </ label > <!-- Upload multiple files --> < label role = "button" > < input type = "file" multiple @ change = "Array.from($event.target.files).forEach(file => { $x.assets.$create(file); });" accept = "*/*" /> < span > Upload Multiple </ span > </ label > <!-- Upload with progress --> < label role = "button" > < input type = "file" @ change = "if ($event.target.files.length > 0) { $x.assets.$create($event.target.files[0], null, null, (progress) => { console.log('Upload progress:', progress); }" > Delete </ button > <!-- Delete multiple files --> < button @ click = "$x.assets.$delete([file1.$id, file2.$id])" > Delete Selected </ button > Choose File No files yet No teams available Storage buckets automatically sync changes in realtime across all active sessions. When one user uploads or deletes a file, all other users see the change immediately without page refresh. Method details: Method Parameters Description $create(file, fileId?, permissions?, onProgress | options?) file (File object), fileId (string, optional), permissions (array, optional). The 4th argument is either an onProgress callback function or an options object { entryId, table, fileIdsColumn? } for linking the file to another table's entry. Upload a new file. Returns uploaded file. If scope is configured, permissions are automatically set based on user/team $duplicate(fileId, options?) fileId (string or object with $id ), options (object, optional) Duplicate a file. Options: newName , newFileId . Returns duplicated file. If newName is not provided, the file name will be "{originalName} copy" $delete(fileIdOrArray) fileIdOrArray (string, object with $id , or array) Delete file(s) and remove them from the list and from any linked entries. Resolves once Appwrite confirms, with Appwrite's (empty) delete response, or an array of them for an array. If some files in an array fail, the rest stay deleted and the call rejects with the first error $url(fileId, token?) fileId (string or object with $id ), token (string, optional) Get file view URL. Returns URL string $download(fileId, token?) fileId (string or object with $id ), token (string, optional) Get file download URL. Returns URL string $preview(fileId, options?) fileId (string or object with $id ), options (object, optional) Get file preview URL (images only). Options: width, height, quality, output, etc. Returns preview URL string $openUrl(fileId, token?) fileId (string or object with $id ), token (string, optional) Open file view URL in new tab $openDownload(fileId, filename?, token?) fileId (string or object with $id ), filename (string, optional), token (string, optional) Download the file; filename names it when the endpoint is on the same origin $openPreview(fileId, options?) fileId (string or object with $id ), options (object, optional) Open file preview URL in new tab $filesFor(table, entryId, column?) table (string), entryId (string), column (string, optional, default fileIds ) Get the files linked to a table entry Link Files to Database Entries Files can be automatically linked to database entries when uploaded. Configure the relationship in manifest.json : manifest.json { "data" : { "assets" : { "appwriteBucketId" : "your-bucket-id" , "belongsTo" : { "table" : "projects" , "id" : "$entryId" , "fileIdsColumn" : "fileIds" } } , "projects" : { "appwriteTableId" : "your-table-id" , "storage" : { "assets" : "fileIds" } } } } When a file is uploaded with an entryId parameter, it's automatically added to that entry's fileIds array: <!-- Upload file and link to project entry --> < button @ click = "$x.assets.$create(file, null, null, { entryId: project.$id, table: 'projects' })" > Upload to Project </ button > Alternatively, link files manually after upload: <!-- Link file to entry after upload --> < button @ click = " $x.assets.$create(file).then(uploadedFile => { const currentFileIds = project.fileIds || []; $x.projects.$update(project.$id, { fileIds: [...currentFileIds, uploadedFile.$id] }); }); " > Upload and Link </ button > Deleting a file with $delete also removes its id from every loaded entry that links it: the columns named for that bucket in a table's storage mapping or a bucket's belongsTo.fileIdsColumn , and fileIds unless the mapping gives fileIds to another bucket. A column you only passed when uploading (the fileIdsColumn option) and never named in manifest.json is not unlinked; remove those ids yourself with the table's $update . The links are removed only after Appwrite confirms the delete, so a delete that fails (for example, no permission) leaves the file and its links as they were. See databases for more details on file references. }" accept = "*/*" /> < span > Upload with ID </ span > </ label > <!-- Upload with progress callback --> < label role = "button" > < input type = "file" @ change = "if ($event.target.files.length > 0) { $x.assets.$create($event.target.files[0], null, null, (progress) => { console.log('Progress:', progress + '%'); }); }" accept = "*/*" /> < span > Upload with Progress </ span > </ label > <!-- Duplicate file (auto-generates name) --> < button @ click = "$x.assets.$duplicate(file.$id)" > Duplicate </ button > <!-- Duplicate with custom name --> < button @ click = "$x.assets.$duplicate(file.$id, { newName: 'Copy of ' + file.name })" > Duplicate with Name </ button > <!-- Duplicate with custom file ID --> < button @ click = "$x.assets.$duplicate(file.$id, { newName: file.name + ' Copy', newFileId: 'custom-id' })" > Duplicate with ID </ button > <!-- Delete single file --> < button @ click = "if (confirm('Delete ' + file.name + '?')) { $x.assets.$delete(file.$id); }" > Delete </ button > <!-- Delete multiple files --> < button @ click = "$x.assets.$delete([file1.$id, file2.$id])" > Delete Selected </ button > View & Download Methods $url $download $preview $openUrl $openDownload $openPreview <!-- Get view URL --> < button @ click = "const url = await $x.assets.$url(file.$id); console.log(url);" > Get View URL </ button > <!-- Get view URL with token --> < button @ click = "const url = await $x.assets.$url(file.$id, token); console.log(url);" > Get URL with Token </ button > <!-- Get download URL --> < button @ click = "const url = await $x.assets.$download(file.$id); console.log(url);" > Get Download URL </ button > <!-- Get download URL with token --> < button @ click = "const url = await $x.assets.$download(file.$id, token); console.log(url);" > Get Download URL with Token </ button > <!-- Get preview URL (images only) --> < button @ click = "const url = await $x.assets.$preview(file.$id, { width: 800, height: 600 }); console.log(url);" > Get Preview URL </ button > <!-- Get preview with all options --> < button @ click = "const url = await $x.assets.$preview(file.$id, { width: 800, height: 600, quality: 90, output: 'webp' }); console.log(url);" > Get Preview with Options </ button > <!-- Open file in new tab --> < button @ click = "$x.assets.$openUrl(file.$id)" > View File </ button > <!-- Download the file --> < button @ click = "$x.assets.$openDownload(file.$id, file.name)" > Download File </ button > <!-- Open preview in new tab --> < button @ click = "$x.assets.$openPreview(file.$id, { width: 800, height: 600 })" > Preview Image </ button > See the Method details table near the top of this article for the full signatures of $url , $download , $preview , and their $open* variants. Image Handling Image files get a $thumbnailUrl (the full-size view URL) for display, and $preview / $openPreview for resized versions: <!-- Display image with thumbnail --> < template x-for = "file in $x.assets" :key = "file.$id" > < div x-show = "file.$isImage" > < img :src = "file.$thumbnailUrl" :alt = "file.name" /> < p x-text = "file.name" > </ p > </ div > </ template > <!-- Preview with custom dimensions --> < button @ click = "$x.assets.$openPreview(file.$id, { width: 1200, height: 800, quality: 95, output: 'webp' })" > High Quality Preview </ button > Image preview options: Option Type Description width integer Resize width (0-4000) height integer Resize height (0-4000) quality integer Image quality (0-100) output string Format: jpeg , jpg , png , gif , webp gravity string Crop gravity: center , top-left , top , top-right , left , right , bottom-left , bottom , bottom-right borderWidth integer Border width in pixels (0-100) borderColor string Border color (HEX without #) borderRadius integer Border radius in pixels (0-4000) opacity number Opacity (0-1, PNG only) rotation integer Rotation in degrees (-360 to 360) background string Background color (HEX without #, PNG only) Next Steps See databases for managing database entries and linking files to entries.


## Presence — Manifest

Source: https://manifestx.dev/docs/framework/appwrite-modules/presence

Presence Show who's here and what they're up to, live, with $presence . Overview Presence is a live picture of who's currently using your app. Anyone with a session — a full account or a guest — publishes a simple status like online , away , or any label you choose, and everyone on the team sees it update the moment it changes. When someone leaves or closes the tab, their status quietly disappears on its own. It's the mechanism behind the little green dots in a chat app, the "3 people viewing" line on a shared document, and the "typing…" hint in a conversation. Presence is built on Appwrite 's native realtime service. Statuses are held in memory and expire automatically, so there's nothing to clean up and no database table to manage. Presence identifies people by their auth session — a signed-in account or a guest both work equally well. A visitor with no session at all sees no roster and can't publish a status; use guest sessions to include them. When your project uses teams , statuses are shared within the current team, so each workspace sees only its own members. Setup Complete the Appwrite setup and auth steps to connect your project and give people a way in — a full sign-in, guest access, or both. Presence needs auth, since it identifies each person by their session. Add the Appwrite SDK and manifest.js scripts to the HTML head, then turn presence on by adding a presence block to your appwrite config in manifest.json . It loads automatically whenever that block is present or $presence appears in your page's markup (bringing auth along with it), or you can load it explicitly with data-modules ( "+appwrite-presences" adds it alongside the defaults). Auto-detect Declared <!-- Meta --> < link rel = "manifest" href = "/manifest.json" > <!-- Scripts --> < script src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/appwrite@latest" > </ script > < script src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mnfst@latest/lib/manifest.min.js" > </ script > <!-- Meta --> < link rel = "manifest" href = "/manifest.json" > <!-- Scripts --> < script src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/appwrite@latest" > </ script > < script src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mnfst@latest/lib/manifest.min.js" data-modules = "+appwrite-presences" > </ script > Enable it in manifest.json : manifest.json { "appwrite" : { "projectId" : "your-project-id" , "endpoint" : "your-API-endpoint" , "auth" : { } , "presence" : { } } } The interactive examples below are real — they publish your status to this page's team. Each one includes a quick sign-in, so you can try them right here. Start Tracking Call $presence.start() once the person has a session — whether they signed in or joined as a guest. It begins publishing their status and loads everyone else's, keeping the roster in sync from then on. HTML <!-- Begin tracking presence --> < button @ click = "$presence.start()" > Go online </ button > <!-- Reflect the live state --> < p x-show = "$presence.ready" > You're online as < b x-text = "$presence.me" > </ b > </ p > Sign in with Google Continue as guest Go online Stop You're online as Sign out By default, tracking is automatic: a person is marked away when none of their tabs is visible (they switched to another site, minimized the browser, or locked the screen) and goes back to their status as soon as one is visible again. Since 0.5.307 this follows tab visibility across all of the person's tabs; earlier releases flipped on window focus, one tab at a time. Adjust this with options passed to start() : Option Default Description auto true Show away while none of the person's tabs is visible, and their own status again when one is. status "online" The status to publish when tracking begins. keepAliveMs 300000 How often, in milliseconds, to refresh an unchanged status so it doesn't expire. Capped at 10 minutes. See Expiry . heartbeatMs Older name for keepAliveMs , still accepted. Before 0.5.307 it set a fixed 25-second refresh from every tab. scope 'team' with teams, otherwise 'global' Who sees the status: the current team, everyone ( 'global' ), or a specific team ID. See Scoping the Roster . Manual control <!-- Start with a custom status and no automatic away-detection --> < button @ click = "$presence.start({ auto: false, status: 'available' })" > Start </ button > A status you set yourself stays put: with auto on, someone who is busy shows away while all their tabs are hidden and busy again when they come back. Set a Status $presence.set(status) publishes any label you like — there's no fixed list. Pass an optional second argument to attach extra details, such as which page the person is viewing. HTML < button @ click = "$presence.set('online')" > Online </ button > < button @ click = "$presence.set('away')" > Away </ button > < button @ click = "$presence.set('busy')" > Busy </ button > <!-- Any label works, with optional details — a name (handy for guests), a page, anything --> < button @ click = "$presence.set('editing', { name: 'Ada', page: 'Invoice #42' })" > Editing </ button > < p > Your status: < b x-text = "$presence.me" > </ b > </ p > Sign in using the first example above to try this. Online Away Busy Set Your status: Press Go online in the example above first. See Who's Here $presence.list is the live roster — an array of everyone currently present, yourself included. It updates on its own as people arrive, change status, and leave. Loop over it to build whatever display you like. It's the one roster for your whole app, shared by every component and every open tab, so read it wherever you need it. There's no need to subscribe to Appwrite's presence channel yourself; a second subscription only repeats work the module already does. Each person carries a color for easy visual distinction and a metadata.name . The name is the person's real account name when they have one, or null when they don't — a guest, say. Because that fallback is null , you decide the label to show in its place, so it's yours to name and to localize . HTML < template x-for = "person in $presence.list" :key = "person.userId" > < div class = "row items-center gap-2" > <!-- Coloured status dot --> < figure class = "size-2 rounded-full" :style = "`background:${person.color}`" > </ figure > <!-- Your label for the nameless — rename or localize freely --> < span x-text = "person.metadata?.name || 'Guest'" > </ span > < small class = "capitalize" x-text = "person.status" > </ small > </ div > </ template > Sign in using the first example above to try this. No one here yet — press Go online above. To look up one specific person instead of the whole roster, use $presence.of(userId) : <!-- Is this teammate around? --> < span x-show = "$presence.of(user.$id)" > < b x-text = "user.name" > </ b > is < span x-text = "$presence.of(user.$id).status" > </ span > </ span > Stop & Clear Presence tidies up after itself. A person's status is removed when they close their last tab, and when their session is ended through $auth — signing out, or a guest signing in to an account — the status is removed first, while the session still allows it (since 0.5.307). A session that ends some other way, such as expiring or being revoked from another device, leaves the status in place until it expires, at most 15 minutes later. Removal on closing the last tab is best effort, since the browser may not finish the request as the tab closes; if it doesn't, the status expires the same way. To end tracking yourself, use clear to remove your status (in every tab) or stop to stop tracking in this tab. clear finishes only once the status is gone, so it's safe to await it right before signing someone out another way. <!-- Remove your status but keep watching others --> < button @ click = "$presence.clear()" > Appear offline </ button > <!-- Stop tracking in this tab --> < button @ click = "$presence.stop()" > Stop </ button > Many Tabs People often keep an app open in several tabs. Since 0.5.307, presence treats a browser as one person, however many tabs they have open: One tab speaks for the browser. The tabs pick one of themselves to publish the status and receive everyone else's, and share the roster with the others. Ten open tabs cost the same as one. Closing that tab hands over. Another tab takes over immediately, without the person blinking offline. The same happens when the browser puts a background tab to sleep, and if that tab stops responding, another takes over within a few minutes or as soon as the person changes their status. The most active tab wins. A person is only away when none of their tabs is visible, so a hidden tab never marks them away while they're working in another. Any tab can set the status. set() and clear() in one tab apply to all of them, and setting a status that hasn't changed sends nothing. Statuses are only sent when they change, plus a slow refresh to keep them from expiring, so a busy app doesn't send a stream of updates while nothing is happening. Bursts of updates from other people are grouped into a single roster update, so a team arriving at once doesn't redraw the page once per person. Tabs coordinate with standard browser features available in every current browser. In an older browser without them, each tab publishes on its own, as earlier releases did. Only tabs that called start() take part, so call it in every tab that shows presence rather than calling set() alone. One person's tabs share a single status, so if two of their tabs are on different teams, the tab that most recently switched or set a status decides where it's shown. Expiry Appwrite removes a status 15 minutes after its last update. While nothing changes, presence refreshes it every 5 minutes ( keepAliveMs ), which stays well inside that window even when the browser slows down background tabs, so nobody flickers offline. If a browser crashes or loses its connection, the person drops off everyone's roster when their status expires, at most 15 minutes after its last refresh; each roster removes expired statuses on its own, without waiting for Appwrite. Rosters stay current through Appwrite's realtime connection. If that connection drops for a while, updates sent in the meantime are missed: someone who arrived or changed status can be missing or out of date until their next refresh, at most 5 minutes later. Scoping the Roster When your project uses teams , the roster automatically follows the person's current team: their status is shared with teammates only, and the roster only shows people from the same team. Without teams, everyone signed in to the project shares one global roster. You can override the default in manifest.json or when starting: manifest.json { "appwrite" : { "presence" : { "scope" : "global" } } } <!-- 'team' (default when teams are in use), 'global', or a specific team ID --> < div x-init = "$presence.start({ scope: 'global' })" > </ div > Switching teams moves your status with you: it disappears from the old team's rosters and appears in the new one. The scope is enforced twice — Appwrite only delivers presence updates to people allowed to read them, and the module also drops anything outside the current scope before it reaches the roster. Until a person's team is known — however long that takes — their status stays private to them; it is never shared project-wide while a team is loading. This also means people who never resolve a team (such as guests outside any team) stay invisible to each other on team-scoped projects; if you want everyone visible regardless of teams, set the scope to global . If some visitors are on an older release of Manifest, their statuses are shared globally rather than per team, so scoped rosters won't show them (and theirs show everyone). This resolves itself once they update, as their next status refresh adopts the current rules. Properties Read these anywhere in your markup — each updates reactively as presence changes. Property Type Description $presence.list array Everyone currently present, yourself included. $presence.records object The same people keyed by their user ID, for direct lookups. $presence.me string | null Your own current status, or null if you aren't publishing one. $presence.ready boolean true once tracking has started and the roster has loaded. $presence.error string | null The most recent error message, or null . $presence.leader boolean true in the one tab that publishes for this browser. See Many Tabs . Methods Method Parameters Description $presence.start(options?) options (object, optional) Begin tracking and publish your status. Options: auto , status , keepAliveMs , scope . $presence.set(status, metadata?) status (string), metadata (object, optional) Publish a status label with optional details. $presence.of(userId) userId (string) Get one person's presence record, or null if they aren't present. $presence.all() None Return the full roster as an array (same as list ). $presence.clear() None Remove your own status, in every tab. Resolves once it's gone. $presence.stop() None Stop tracking in this tab and empty its roster. A Presence Record Every entry in the roster has this shape. Property Type Description userId string The person's account ID. status string Their current status label. metadata object Details attached with set , including color and name (the account name, or null — pass your own with set(status, { name }) ). color string A consistent colour for this person, handy for dots and avatars. lastSeen number Timestamp of their most recent update. expiresAt string | null When the status will expire if not refreshed (15 minutes after its last update). Next Steps See teams to scope presence to a workspace, or cloud data to pair it with shared databases and files.
